sentences.zh: 積家而成國，家恆男婦半。

translations.literal: Families accumulate to form a state; in a household men and women are always half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Households build up into a nation, and in every home men and women are always half and half.

sentences.zh: 女順父母，婦敬舅姑，妻助夫，母長子女，姊妹娣姒，各盡其分。

translations.literal: Daughters obey parents, daughters-in-law revere parents-in-law, wives assist husbands, mothers nurture sons and daughters, sisters and sisters-in-law each fulfill their roles.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters defer to their parents, daughters-in-law honor their husbands' parents, wives support their husbands, mothers raise their children, and sisters and sisters-in-law each perform their allotted parts.

sentences.zh: 人如是，家和；

translations.literal: When people are thus, the family is harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: When everyone acts this way, the household is at peace;

sentences.zh: 家如是，國治。

translations.literal: when families are thus, the state is well governed.
translations.idiomatic: and when households are thus, the realm is well governed.

sentences.zh: 是故匹婦黽勉帷闥之內，議酒食，操井臼，勤織紝組紃，乃與公卿大夫士謀政事。

translations.literal: Therefore ordinary wives diligently within the inner quarters discuss food and drink, manage the well and mortar, and work hard at weaving silk and hemp, and thus share in governing affairs with dukes, ministers, grand masters, and officers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ordinary wives, laboring within the inner quarters over meals and drink, the well and mortar, and the steady work of weaving silk and hemp, share in the nation's business no less than dukes, ministers, and gentlemen who deliberate policy at court.

sentences.zh: 農勞稼穡，工業勢曲，商賈通貨財，同有職於國，而不而闕。

translations.literal: Farmers labor in the fields, artisans master their crafts, merchants circulate goods and wealth—all alike have offices in the state and cannot be wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers till the soil, artisans master their trades, and merchants move goods and wealth through the realm; each has a duty to the state, and none may be dispensed with.

sentences.zh: 晚近好異議，以謂女豢於父，妻豢於夫，戚戚求自食。

translations.literal: In recent times people delight in heterodox opinions, saying that daughters are kept by fathers and wives kept by husbands, anxiously seeking to feed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times many have taken to eccentric views, claiming that daughters are kept by their fathers and wives by their husbands, and fretting only over how to earn their own bread.

sentences.zh: 或謂女制於父母，婦制於舅姑，妻制於夫，將一切排決，舍家而躐國，務為閎大，其過不及若殊，要為自棄其所職而害中於家國則均。

translations.literal: Others say daughters are controlled by parents, daughters-in-law by parents-in-law, wives by husbands, and would cast all these aside, leave the family and leap to the state, striving for what is vast and grand; though excess and deficiency seem different, in essence both abandon their proper duties and alike harm the core of family and state.
translations.idiomatic: Others hold that daughters are ruled by their parents, daughters-in-law by their husbands' parents, and wives by their husbands, and would cast all such bonds aside, forsake the home, and vault straight to the nation, chasing a grand public role. The excess of one view and the shortfall of the other look different, yet both come to the same thing: abandoning one's proper station and wounding the heart of family and state alike.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，何其誣也！

translations.literal: Alas, how slanderous!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, what a slander on the truth!

sentences.zh: 古昔聖王經國中而為之軌，億萬士女毋或逾焉。

translations.literal: Of old the sage kings laid down norms within the state, and myriads of men and women did not transgress them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the sage kings set the norms of the realm, and countless men and women did not step beyond them.

sentences.zh: 是故矜其變，所以誨其正；

translations.literal: Therefore one honors their departures, thereby to instruct them in what is correct;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the state honors those who depart from the norm, in order to teach others what is right;

sentences.zh: 愍其異，所以勵其庸：範而趨於一。

translations.literal: pities their exceptions, thereby to encourage the ordinary: setting a model and moving all toward one standard.
translations.idiomatic: and commiserates with the extraordinary, in order to stir the common run of women to virtue—offering models until all converge on a single way.

sentences.zh: 使凡為女若婦者，循循各盡其職。

translations.literal: So that all who are daughters or wives may each in orderly fashion fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: So that every daughter and every wife may quietly and fully perform her allotted duty.

sentences.zh: 則且廣之為風俗，永之為名教。

translations.literal: Then it may be extended as custom and made lasting as moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Then custom may be broadened and moral teaching made enduring.

sentences.zh: 有國者之事，以權始，以化終。

translations.literal: The business of those who hold a state begins with authority and ends in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: For those who govern a realm, the work begins with authority and ends in moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 權故行，化故成，國以治平。

translations.literal: Because authority is exercised it takes effect; because transformation is achieved the state is governed and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Authority makes policy effective; transformation makes it endure, and the realm is governed and at peace.

sentences.zh: 清製，禮部掌旌格孝婦、孝女、烈婦、烈女、守節、殉節、未婚守節，歲會而上，都數千人。

translations.literal: Under Qing institutions the Board of Rites supervised commendation of filial wives, filial daughters, chaste martyrs, chaste women, those who preserved chastity, those who died for chastity, and betrothed women who preserved chastity; each year they were gathered and reported upward, totaling several thousand in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing system the Board of Rites oversaw honors for filial wives and daughters, heroic martyrs, chaste women, widows who preserved their chastity, those who died for chastity, and betrothed maidens who remained faithful—each year the lists were compiled and sent up, amounting to several thousand cases in the capital alone.

sentences.zh: 軍興，死寇難役輒十百萬，則別牘上請。

translations.literal: When armies were raised and deaths from banditry or corvée labor ran into the millions, separate memorials were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out and deaths from bandit raids or forced labor ran into the millions, separate petitions were sent up.

sentences.zh: 捍強暴而死，爰書定，亦別牘上請，皆謹書於實錄。

translations.literal: Those who died resisting violence, once the legal record was settled, were likewise reported in separate memorials, all carefully entered in the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Women who died resisting violence, once the case was legally settled, were also reported in separate memorials, and all were carefully recorded in the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 其徵之也廣，其襮之也顯，流風餘韻，綿綿延延，風雨如晦​​，雞鳴不已。

translations.literal: The summons was broad, the display conspicuous; the lingering influence stretched on and on, like dark rain yet the cock still crows without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The call went out far and wide, the honors were proclaimed openly, and the lingering moral force stretched on unbroken—like the verse says: though the night is dark as rain, the cock still crows without end.

sentences.zh: 故知權所以能行，化所以能成，尤必有當於人人之心，固不可強而致也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that authority can be exercised and transformation achieved only when it accords with every person's heart and cannot be forced into being.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that authority can take effect and transformation succeed only when they answer to what lies in every heart—they cannot be imposed by force.

sentences.zh: 列女入史，始後漢書，用其例，擇尤炳著如乾人，賢母、孝女、孝婦、賢婦、節婦、貞婦、貞女、烈婦義行，邊徼諸婦，以類相從，其處變事相亞者，厭而比焉。

translations.literal: Exemplary women entered the histories beginning with the Book of Later Han; following that precedent, those especially illustrious are chosen—such as the woman of Qian, worthy mothers, filial daughters, filial wives, worthy wives, chaste wives, faithful wives, faithful maidens, heroic wives and righteous conduct, and women of the frontier—arranged by category; where their responses to change and their deeds are similar, they are grouped and compared.
translations.idiomatic: The inclusion of exemplary women in the histories began with the Book of Later Han. Following that precedent, we select the most striking cases—the woman of Qian, worthy mothers, filial daughters and wives, worthy wives, chaste and faithful wives and maidens, heroic wives and women of righteous conduct, and women of the borderlands—arranged by kind; where their conduct under trial and their deeds are alike, they are set side by side for comparison.

sentences.zh: 纂昔懿，傃來淑，敬我彤管，宜有助於興觀。

translations.literal: Gathering past excellence and summoning coming virtue, honoring our red brush-staff, it should aid in stirring reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering the excellence of the past and summoning the virtue yet to come, honoring the red brush of the Odes, these records should help awaken the reader's heart.

sentences.zh: 田緒宗妻張，德州人。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Tian Xuzong, was a native of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Tian Xuzong, came from Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 緒宗，順治九年進士，官浙江麗水知縣，有聲。

translations.literal: Xuzong, a jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi, served as magistrate of Lishui in Zhejiang and had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzong passed the jinshi examination in Shunzhi 9 and served as magistrate of Lishui in Zhejiang, where he won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 張預戒管庫，謹視賦徭所入，發牘覈其數。

translations.literal: Zhang beforehand warned the treasury clerks, carefully watched the tax and corvée receipts, opened the registers and checked the figures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang had already warned the treasury clerks to keep careful watch on tax and corvée receipts; she opened the account books and verified every figure.

sentences.zh: 代者至，請知府臨察，無稍舛漏，乃持喪歸。

translations.literal: When his successor arrived, she asked the prefect to inspect in person; finding no slightest discrepancy, she then returned with the coffin in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived, she asked the prefect to inspect the accounts in person; once he found not the slightest error, she bore the coffin home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 教三子雯、需、霢，皆有文行。

translations.literal: She taught her three sons Wen, Xu, and Mai, all of whom had literary accomplishment and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: She raised her three sons Wen, Xu, and Mai, each distinguished for learning and character.

sentences.zh: 張通詩、春秋傳，能文。

translations.literal: Zhang was versed in the Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals and could write well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was versed in the Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals and was herself a capable writer.

sentences.zh: 年七十，裡黨將為壽，誡諸子曰：「禮，婦人無夫者稱未亡人，凡吉凶交際之事不與，亦不為主名，故春秋書'紀履緰來逆女'。

translations.literal: At age seventy, when the neighborhood was about to celebrate her birthday, she admonished her sons, saying: 'By ritual, a woman without a husband is called one not yet dead; she does not take part in matters of good or ill fortune that involve others, nor does she lend her name as host. Therefore the Spring and Autumn records "Ji Lüxi came to receive the bride."'
translations.idiomatic: When she turned seventy, her neighbors planned a birthday celebration. She warned her sons: 'By ritual, a woman without a husband is called one who is not yet dead. She takes no part in others' occasions of joy or mourning, nor does she lend her name as host. That is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records only "Ji Lüxi came to receive the bride," and not the mother.'

sentences.zh: 公羊傳曰：'紀有母，何以不稱母？

translations.literal: The Gongyang Commentary says: 'Ji had a mother—why is the mother not named?'
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang Commentary asks: 'Ji had a mother—why is she not called mother?'

sentences.zh: 母不通也。

translations.literal: The mother does not appear in the record.
translations.idiomatic: Because the mother does not appear in the record.

sentences.zh: '何休云：'婦人無外事，所以遠別也。

translations.literal: He Xiu says: 'A woman has no external affairs—that is why she is kept apart.'
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu explains: 'A woman has no business outside the home—that is why she is kept apart from public affairs.'

sentences.zh: '後世禮意失，始有登堂拜母之事。

translations.literal: Later ages lost the ritual meaning, and only then arose the practice of ascending the hall to pay respects to a mother.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages lost the true meaning of ritual, and only then did men begin ascending the hall to pay court to another man's mother.

sentences.zh: 戰國時，嚴仲子自觴聶政母前，且進百金為壽。

translations.literal: In Warring States times Yan Zhongzi himself poured wine before Nie Zheng's mother and moreover presented a hundred in gold as a birthday gift.
translations.idiomatic: In Warring States times Yan Zhongzi poured wine himself before Nie Zheng's mother and even offered a hundred pieces of gold as a birthday gift.

sentences.zh: 蓋任俠好交之流，有所求而然耳，豈禮意當如是耶？

translations.literal: That was the sort who delight in chivalry and friendship and act thus because they want something—how could ritual propriety require such behavior?
translations.idiomatic: That was the way of swaggering men who court friends because they want something in return. How could ritual propriety ever require such behavior?

sentences.zh: 吾自汝父之歿於官，攜扶小弱，千里歸櫬，含艱履戚，三十年餘。

translations.literal: Since your father's death in office I have led the little and weak, borne the coffin a thousand li home, endured hardship and walked in grief for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Since your father died in office I have led you little ones home a thousand li with his coffin, bearing hardship and walking in grief for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 闔戶闢績，以禮自守。

translations.literal: I closed the door and kept to weaving, guarding myself by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I shut the door and kept to my loom, holding myself to ritual.

sentences.zh: 幸汝曹皆得成立，養我餘年，然此中長有隱痛。

translations.literal: Fortunately you all have been able to establish yourselves and support me in my remaining years, yet within this there has long been a hidden pain.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately you have all grown up and can support me in my old age, yet a hidden sorrow has never left me.

sentences.zh: 每歲時膢臘，兒女滿前，牽衣嬉笑，輒怦怦心動，念汝父之不及見。

translations.literal: At each year's festivals my children would fill the room, tugging my clothes and laughing; my heart would pound as I thought that your father could not see this.
translations.idiomatic: At every festival my children would crowd before me, tugging my clothes and laughing, and my heart would pound with the thought that your father could not see it.

sentences.zh: 故或中坐嘆息，或輟箸掩淚。

translations.literal: Therefore sometimes in mid-meal I would sigh, or set down my chopsticks and cover my tears.
translations.idiomatic: So sometimes in the middle of a feast I would sigh, or set down my chopsticks and hide my tears.

sentences.zh: 今一旦賓客填門，為未亡人稱慶，未亡人尚可以言慶乎？

translations.literal: Now suddenly guests fill the door to celebrate one not yet dead—can one not yet dead speak of celebration?
translations.idiomatic: Now suddenly guests crowd the door to celebrate a woman not yet dead—can such a woman speak of celebration at all?

sentences.zh: 三十年吉凶交際之事不與知，而今日更強我為主名，其可謂之禮乎？

translations.literal: For thirty years I have not taken part in others' occasions of joy and mourning, yet today you would force me to lend my name as host—can this be called ritual?
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years I have had no part in others' joys and sorrows, yet today you would force me to stand as host—can that be called ritual?

sentences.zh: 處我以非禮，不足為我慶，而適足增我悲耳。

translations.literal: Treating me contrary to ritual is no celebration for me but only adds to my grief.
translations.idiomatic: Treating me contrary to ritual is no honor for me—it only deepens my grief.

sentences.zh: 汝曹官於朝，宜曉大體，其詳思禮意，以安老人之心！

translations.literal: You hold office at court and should understand the larger principles; ponder the meaning of ritual carefully to set an old woman's heart at ease!
translations.idiomatic: You serve at court and ought to understand the larger principles. Think carefully about what ritual requires, and set your old mother's heart at ease!

sentences.zh: 張年七十七而卒，有茹荼集，雯官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhang died at seventy-seven; she left a collection called Bitter Herb, and Wen rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang died at seventy-seven. She left a collection called Bitter Herb, and her son Wen rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嵇永仁妻楊，永仁，無錫人；

translations.literal: Yang, wife of Ji Yongren—Yongren was a native of Wuxi;
translations.idiomatic: Yang, wife of Ji Yongren—Yongren came from Wuxi;

sentences.zh: 楊，長洲人。

translations.literal: Yang was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 永仁死福建總督范承謨之難，楊時年二十七，子曾筠生七年。

translations.literal: Yongren died in the disaster of Fujian Governor Fan Chengmo; Yang was then twenty-seven, and her son Zengyun was seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yongren died in the disaster that claimed Fujian Governor Fan Chengmo. Yang was twenty-seven, and her son Zengyun was seven.

sentences.zh: 舅姑皆篤老，黽勉奉事，喪葬謹如禮。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law were both aged; she strove diligently to serve them, and the funerals were conducted scrupulously according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Both parents-in-law were elderly; she served them diligently, and the funerals were conducted scrupulously according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 福建定，永仁僕程治乃克以其喪還，楊質衣營葬。

translations.literal: When Fujian was pacified, Yongren's servant Cheng Zhi was able at last to bring back the coffin; Yang pawned her clothes to pay for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: After Fujian was pacified, Yongren's servant Cheng Zhi was finally able to bring the coffin home. Yang pawned her clothes to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 葬竟，撫曾筠而泣曰：「我前所以不死，以有舅姑在。

translations.literal: When the burial was finished, she embraced Zengyun and wept, saying: 'The reason I did not die before was that my parents-in-law were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was over, she held Zengyun and wept: 'I did not die before because my parents-in-law were still alive.

sentences.zh: 舅姑既而葬，今又葬汝父，我可以死，則又有汝在。

translations.literal: Now that they are buried, and your father too is buried, I could die—but then there is still you.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are buried, and your father is buried too. I could die—but then there is still you.

sentences.zh: 汝父以諸生死國事，汝未成人，當如何？

translations.literal: Your father died as a scholar-official for the state; you are not yet grown—what then should be done?'
translations.idiomatic: Your father died as a scholar-official for the state. You are not yet grown—what then am I to do?'

sentences.zh: 」則又嗚咽曰：「我其如何？

translations.literal: " Then she sobbed again: 'What am I to do?'
translations.idiomatic: " Then she sobbed again: 'What am I to do?'

sentences.zh: 」曾筠長而力學，楊日織布易米以為食，指謂曾筠曰：「汝能讀書，乃得啖此，未亡人則歠粥。

translations.literal: " Zengyun grew up and studied hard; Yang wove cloth each day and exchanged it for rice to eat, pointing and saying to Zengyun: 'Only because you can study do you get to eat this; one not yet dead drinks only gruel.'
translations.idiomatic: " Zengyun grew up and studied hard. Each day Yang wove cloth and traded it for rice. Pointing to the food she told him: 'Only because you study do you get to eat this. As for one not yet dead, she drinks only gruel.'

sentences.zh: 」及曾筠官漸顯，恆誡以廉慎。

translations.literal: " When Zengyun's office gradually became prominent, she constantly admonished him to be incorrupt and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: " As Zengyun rose in office, she constantly admonished him to be honest and cautious.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，卒，年八十有四。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng she died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Yongzheng 11, aged eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 永仁、曾筠皆有傳。

translations.literal: Yongren and Zengyun both have biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yongren and Zengyun have biographies elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 永仁妾蘇，字瑤青。

translations.literal: Yongren's concubine Su, style name Yaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yongren's concubine Su, whose style was Yaoqing.

sentences.zh: 從永仁福州，臨難，取帶面永仁而縊，年十七。

translations.literal: She followed Yongren to Fuzhou; at the crisis she took her belt, faced Yongren, and hanged herself, aged seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: She followed Yongren to Fuzhou. When disaster struck she took her belt, turned to face Yongren, and hanged herself. She was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 張英妻姚，桐城人。

translations.literal: Yao, wife of Zhang Ying, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, wife of Zhang Ying, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 英初官翰林，貧甚，或餽之千金，英勿受也。

translations.literal: When Ying first served in the Hanlin Academy he was very poor; someone once presented him with a thousand in gold, but Ying would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying first served in the Hanlin Academy the family was very poor. Someone once offered him a thousand taels of silver, but Ying refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 故以語姚，姚曰：「貧家或餽十金五金，僮僕皆喜相告。

translations.literal: He therefore told Yao; Yao said: 'In a poor household, if someone gives ten or five in gold, even the servants delight in telling one another.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yao about it. Yao said: 'In a poor household, even ten or five taels make the servants crow with delight.

sentences.zh: 今無故得千金，人問所從來，能勿慚乎？

translations.literal: Now to receive a thousand in gold for no reason—when people ask where it came from, can one not feel ashamed?'
translations.idiomatic: To receive a thousand taels for no reason—when people ask where it came from, how can we not be ashamed?'

sentences.zh: 」居恆質衣貰米。

translations.literal: " In daily life she pawned clothes to buy rice on credit.
translations.idiomatic: " In ordinary times she pawned her clothes to buy rice on credit.

sentences.zh: 英祿稍豐，姚不改其儉，一青衫數年不易。

translations.literal: When Ying's salary grew somewhat ample, Yao did not change her frugality; one blue gown she wore for years without replacing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying's salary grew more ample, Yao did not change her frugal ways. One blue gown she wore for years without replacing it.

sentences.zh: 英既相，彌自謙下。

translations.literal: After Ying became chief minister, she became all the more modest and deferential.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying became chief minister, she became all the more modest and unassuming.

sentences.zh: 戚黨或使婢起居，姚方補故衣，不識也。

translations.literal: When relatives sometimes sent maidservants to inquire after her, Yao would be mending old clothes and did not recognize them.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives sent maidservants to call on her, Yao would be mending old clothes and did not even recognize who they were.

sentences.zh: 問：「夫人安在？

translations.literal: [The maidservant] asked: "Where is the lady?"
translations.idiomatic: The maid asked, "Where is the lady?"

sentences.zh: 」姚逡巡起應，婢大慚沮。

translations.literal: " Yao rose hesitantly to answer; the maidservant was deeply ashamed and crestfallen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao rose hesitantly to reply. The maid was utterly ashamed.

sentences.zh: 英年六十，姚制棉衣貸寒者。

translations.literal: When Ying reached sixty, Yao made cotton padded garments to lend to those suffering from cold.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying turned sixty, Yao made cotton padded coats to lend to those in need during the cold.

sentences.zh: 子廷玉繼入翰林，直南書房，聖祖嘗顧左右曰：「張廷玉兄弟，母教之有素，不獨父訓也！

translations.literal: Her son Tingyu afterward entered the Hanlin Academy and served in the Southern Studio; the Sagely Ancestor once turned to those beside him and said: "Zhang Tingyu and his brothers—their mother's teaching has been thorough; it is not the father's instruction alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Her son Tingyu later entered the Hanlin Academy and served in the Southern Studio. The Kangxi Emperor once turned to those around him and said, "Zhang Tingyu and his brothers owe their upbringing not only to their father's instruction—their mother's teaching has been thorough."

sentences.zh: 」卒，年六十九，有含章閣詩。

translations.literal: " She died at sixty-nine; she left the Hanzhangge Poems.
translations.idiomatic: She died at sixty-nine. Her collected verses were published as the Hanzhangge Poems.

sentences.zh: 女令儀，為同縣姚士封妻，好學，有蠹窗集。

translations.literal: Her daughter Lingyi became the wife of Yao Shifeng of the same county; she loved learning and authored the Duochuang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Her daughter Lingyi married Yao Shifeng of the same county. A devoted student of books, she compiled the Duochuang Ji.

sentences.zh: 英、廷玉皆有傳。

translations.literal: Both Ying and Tingyu have biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhang Ying and Zhang Tingyu have biographies elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 蔡璧妻黃，漳浦人，世遠母也。

translations.literal: Huang, wife of Cai Bi, was a native of Zhangpu and mother of Shiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, wife of Cai Bi, came from Zhangpu. She was the mother of Cai Shiyuan.

sentences.zh: 璧喪妻，以為妾。

translations.literal: Bi had lost his wife and took her as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi lost his wife, he took Huang as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠為變，璧方客京師，黃奉璧父母避山中。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Bi was then traveling in the capital; Huang escorted Bi's parents into the mountains to escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Bi was away in the capital. Huang led Bi's parents into the mountains for safety.

sentences.zh: 璧母老不能粒食，輟女子子乳乳之。

translations.literal: Bi's mother, old and unable to take grain, ceased nursing her own daughter's child and breastfed the old woman instead.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's mother was too old to eat grain. Huang stopped nursing her own daughter and suckled the old woman instead.

sentences.zh: 璧父母命璧以為妻。

translations.literal: Bi's parents ordered Bi to take her as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's parents commanded that she be made Bi's wife.

sentences.zh: 世遠妻劉，事舅姑孝。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Shiyuan, served her parents-in-law with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Cai Shiyuan, served her parents-in-law with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 世遠既貴，家人謀買婢，勿許。

translations.literal: After Shiyuan had risen to high rank, the household proposed buying maidservants; she would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shiyuan had risen to high office, the family proposed buying servants. She refused.

sentences.zh: 謀傭乳母，劉曰：「吾六子四女皆自乳，吾不以貴易其素。

translations.literal: They proposed hiring a wet nurse; Liu said: "I have nursed all six sons and four daughters myself; I will not trade my accustomed ways for wealth."
translations.idiomatic: They suggested hiring a wet nurse. Liu said, "I nursed all six sons and four daughters myself. I will not abandon my accustomed ways now that we are wealthy."

sentences.zh: 」世遠有傳。

translations.literal: " Shiyuan has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 尹公弼妻李，博野人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Yin Gongbi, was a native of Boye.
translations.idiomatic: Li, wife of Yin Gongbi, came from Boye.

sentences.zh: 公弼早卒，家貧，舅姑老，父母衰病，無子。

translations.literal: Gongbi died young; the family was poor; her parents-in-law were old; her own parents were frail and ill; there were no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Gongbi died young. The household was poor. Her parents-in-law were elderly, her own parents were frail and ill, and there were no sons.

sentences.zh: 養生送死，拮据黽勉。

translations.literal: She supported the living and saw off the dead, struggling on with tireless effort.
translations.idiomatic: She supported the living and arranged the funerals of the dead, struggling on with tireless effort.

sentences.zh: 教子會一有法度，通籍，出為襄陽府知府，李就養。

translations.literal: She taught her son Huiyi with strict discipline; he entered the registers and was appointed prefect of Xiangyang; Li went to live with him in support.
translations.idiomatic: She raised her son Huiyi with strict discipline. He took office and was appointed prefect of Xiangyang, and Li went to live with him.

sentences.zh: 雨暘不時，必躬自跽禱，禳疫驅蝗亦如之。

translations.literal: When rain and sunshine were untimely, she would kneel in prayer herself; she did the same to dispel plague and drive away locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rain and sunshine failed in season, she knelt in prayer herself. She did the same to dispel plague and drive away locusts.

sentences.zh: 冬寒，民六十以上，量予布帛。

translations.literal: In winter's cold, to commoners over sixty she allotted cloth and silk according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: In winter's cold she measured out cloth and silk for every commoner over sixty.

sentences.zh: 襄陽民德之，為建賢母堂。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangyang were grateful to her and built for her the Hall of the Worthy Mother.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiangyang were grateful and built for her the Hall of the Worthy Mother.

sentences.zh: 李賦詩辭之，不能止。

translations.literal: Li composed a poem declining the honor, but they could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li wrote a poem declining the honor, but the people would not be dissuaded.

sentences.zh: 會一移揚州府知府，揚州俗奢，李為作女訓十二章，教以儉。

translations.literal: When Huiyi was transferred to be prefect of Yangzhou—a place of luxurious customs—Li composed for him twelve chapters of Instructions for Women, teaching thrift.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiyi was transferred to Yangzhou, whose customs were luxurious, Li wrote for him twelve chapters of Instructions for Women teaching thrift.

sentences.zh: 累遷河南巡撫，所至節俸錢，畀高年布帛，週貧民，佐軍餉，皆以母命為之。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to governor of Henan; wherever he went he saved from his salary, gave cloth and silk to the aged, relieved poor commoners, and assisted military provisions—all by his mother's command.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become governor of Henan. Wherever he served he economized from his salary, gave cloth to the elderly, relieved the poor, and assisted military provisions—all at his mother's command.

sentences.zh: 民間輒為立生祠，如在襄陽時。

translations.literal: The people everywhere erected living shrines to her, as in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The people everywhere erected shrines to her in her lifetime, as they had in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 會一內擢左副都御史，李以疾不能入京師，陳情歸養。

translations.literal: When Huiyi was promoted within the capital to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Li, being ill and unable to enter the capital, presented a plea to return home for her support.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiyi was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief in the capital, Li was too ill to go to Beijing. She petitioned to return home and tend her mother.

sentences.zh: 復以母命，裡塾社倉次第設置。

translations.literal: Again by his mother's command, village schools and community granaries were set up in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Again at his mother's direction, village schools and community granaries were established one after another.

sentences.zh: 居數年，高宗賜詩嘉許，榜所居堂曰「荻訓松齡」。

translations.literal: After several years, the Gaozong Emperor bestowed a poem in praise and inscribed the hall where she dwelt "Lessons from the Reeds, Longevity of the Pine."
translations.idiomatic: Some years later the Qianlong Emperor bestowed a poem of praise and inscribed the name of her hall as "Lessons from the Reeds, Longevity of the Pine."

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: She died at seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: She died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 公弼曾孫溯醇妻徐，亦早寡，與其族公亮妻高、公聘妻楊、德一妻韓、成一妻李、多福妻劉、林妻王、二喜妻硃，合稱「尹氏九節」。

translations.literal: Xu, wife of Suochun the great-grandson of Gongbi, also became a widow young; together with Gao, wife of Gongliang; Yang, wife of Gongpin; Han, wife of Deyi; Li, wife of Chengyi; Liu, wife of Duofu; Wang, wife of Lin; and Zhu, wife of Ersi of the clan—they were together called "The Nine Chaste Women of the Yin Clan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu, wife of Yin Suochun (a great-grandson of Gongbi), was also widowed young. Together with Gao, wife of Yin Gongliang; Yang, wife of Yin Gongpin; Han, wife of Yin Deyi; Li, wife of Yin Chengyi; Liu, wife of Yin Duofu; Wang, wife of Yin Lin; and Zhu, wife of Yin Ersi—they were known collectively as "The Nine Chaste Women of the Yin Clan."

sentences.zh: 會一有傳。

translations.literal: Huiyi has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyi has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 錢綸光妻陳，名書。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of Qian Lunguang, personal name Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of Qian Lunguang, whose personal name was Shu.

sentences.zh: 綸光，嘉興人；

translations.literal: Lunguang was a native of Jiaxing;
translations.idiomatic: Lunguang came from Jiaxing;

sentences.zh: 陳，秀水人。

translations.literal: Chen was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 幼端靜，讀書通大義。

translations.literal: From childhood she was composed and quiet; in reading she grasped the great principles.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was composed and reserved. In her reading she grasped the larger moral principles.

sentences.zh: 初婚，綸光侍其父瑞徵出上塚，陳從樓上望見少年毆佃客幾死，咯血，方大雪，血沾衣盡赤，佃客家以其族黨至，洶洶。

translations.literal: Shortly after marriage, Lunguang attended his father Ruizheng on a tomb visit; Chen looked from upstairs and saw a young man beat a tenant farmer nearly to death until he spat blood; it was heavy snow, and the blood soaked his clothes completely red; the tenant's family and their clan kin arrived in a tumult.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after her marriage, Lunguang accompanied his father Ruizheng to tend the ancestral graves. From upstairs Chen saw a young man beat a tenant farmer nearly to death until he spat blood. Snow was falling heavily and blood soaked the man's clothes crimson. The tenant's kin arrived in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 陳遣蒼頭問，少年，從子也。

translations.literal: Chen sent a house servant to inquire; the young man was a nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent a servant to inquire. The young man was a nephew of the family.

sentences.zh: 乃舁佃客入室，召醫予藥，畀其母錢米，呼從子使受杖，眾乃散。

translations.literal: She then had the tenant carried indoors, summoned a physician and gave medicine, gave his mother money and rice, called the nephew to receive beating with the rod, and only then did the crowd disperse.
translations.idiomatic: She had the tenant carried indoors, sent for a physician and medicine, gave his mother money and rice, called the nephew forward to be beaten with rods, and only then did the crowd disperse.

sentences.zh: 瑞徵還，亟賢之。

translations.literal: When Ruizheng returned, he greatly praised her worth.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizheng returned, he praised her highly.

sentences.zh: 陳善事舅姑，助綸光款賓客，週鄰里，​​曲盡恩意。

translations.literal: Chen served her parents-in-law well, helped Lunguang entertain guests, and aided neighbors—fulfilling every kindness in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chen tended her parents-in-law with devotion, helped Lunguang entertain guests, and aided the neighbors, extending kindness in every detail.

sentences.zh: 綸光卒，教子尤有法度。

translations.literal: After Lunguang died, she taught her sons with especial discipline.
translations.idiomatic: After Lunguang died, she raised her sons with especial discipline.

sentences.zh: 子陳群，自有傳；

translations.literal: Her son Chen Qun has his own biography;
translations.idiomatic: Her son Chen Qun has his own biography;

sentences.zh: 界，官陝西醴泉知縣，有賢聲。

translations.literal: Jie served as magistrate of Liquan in Shaanxi and had a reputation for worth.
translations.idiomatic: Jie served as magistrate of Liquan in Shaanxi and won a reputation for worth.

sentences.zh: 陳晚為詩，號复庵；

translations.literal: In her later years Chen wrote poetry under the sobriquet Fu'an;
translations.idiomatic: In her later years Chen wrote poetry under the sobriquet Fu'an;

sentences.zh: 署畫，號南樓老人。

translations.literal: she signed her paintings as the Old Man of the Southern Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On her paintings she signed herself the Old Man of the Southern Tower.

sentences.zh: 詩三卷，​​戒陳群毋付刻。

translations.literal: Her poems filled three scrolls; she admonished Chen Qun not to have them printed.
translations.idiomatic: Her poems filled three scrolls. She warned Chen Qun not to have them printed.

sentences.zh: 畫尤工，山水、人物、花草皆清迥高秀，力追古作者。

translations.literal: Her painting was especially skilled; landscapes, figures, and flowers and grasses were all clear, lofty, and refined, striving forcefully after ancient masters.
translations.idiomatic: Her painting was especially accomplished. Landscapes, figures, flowers, and grasses were all clear, lofty, and refined, as she strove to follow the ancient masters.

sentences.zh: 曾孫女與齡，字九英，為廣西太平府同知吳江蒯嘉珍妻。

translations.literal: Her great-granddaughter Yuling, courtesy name Jiuying, was wife of Kuai Jiazhen of Wujiang, vice prefect of Taiping in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-granddaughter Yuling, whose courtesy name was Jiuying, married Kuai Jiazhen of Wujiang, vice prefect of Taiping in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 亦能畫，題所居曰仰南樓。

translations.literal: She too could paint and inscribed her dwelling "Gazing up at the Southern Tower."
translations.idiomatic: She too painted, and named her residence the Gazing-up-at-the-Southern-Tower Studio.

sentences.zh: 胡彌禪妻潘，桐城人。

translations.literal: Pan, wife of Hu Mizhan, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pan, wife of Hu Mizhan, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 彌禪卒，遺三子，長子宗緒，方十歲。

translations.literal: When Mizhan died he left three sons; the eldest, Zongxu, was just ten.
translations.idiomatic: When Mizhan died he left three sons. The eldest, Zongxu, was only ten.

sentences.zh: 貧，遣就學村塾，旦倚閭泣而送之，踰嶺不見，乃返，暮复迎之而泣。

translations.literal: Poor, she sent him to study at the village school; at dawn she leaned on the lane and wept as she sent him off; when he passed over the ridge and was out of sight she returned, and at evening again went to meet him weeping.
translations.idiomatic: They were poor, so she sent him to the village school. Each morning she leaned in the doorway weeping as she sent him off. When he crossed the ridge and vanished from sight she would return; each evening she went to meet him again, weeping.

sentences.zh: 三年，貧益甚，罷學，潘不知書，使兒誦，以意為解說。

translations.literal: After three years poverty grew worse and schooling ceased; Pan could not read, yet made the boy recite and explained according to her own understanding.
translations.idiomatic: After three years their poverty grew worse and schooling had to stop. Pan could not read, yet she had the boy recite and explained the texts as best she could.

sentences.zh: 一日，聞程、硃語，嘆且起立曰：「我固謂世間當有此！

translations.literal: One day hearing words of Cheng and Zhu, she sighed and rose to her feet, saying: "I always knew the world must have such as this!
translations.idiomatic: One day, hearing teachings of the Cheng–Zhu school, she sighed and rose to her feet. "I always knew such men must exist in the world!

sentences.zh: 」聞誦司馬相如美人賦則怒，禁毋更讀。

translations.literal: " Hearing the Rhapsody on the Beautiful Woman of Sima Xiangru recited, she grew angry and forbade further reading of it.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard Sima Xiangru's Rhapsody on the Beautiful Woman recited, she grew angry and forbade them to read it again.

sentences.zh: 諸子出必告，襟濡露，則笞之，問：「奈何不由正路？

translations.literal: Whenever the sons went out she made them announce it; if their collars were damp with dew she beat them, asking: "Why do you not keep to the proper path?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever her sons went out she made them announce their departure. If their collars were damp with dew she beat them and asked, "Why do you not keep to the straight path?"

sentences.zh: 」歲饑，潘日茹瓜蔓，而為麥粥飯兒，有餘，以周里之餓者。

translations.literal: " In years of famine Pan daily ate melon vines while preparing wheat porridge to feed her sons; what remained she used to aid hungry neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years Pan ate melon vines herself while cooking wheat porridge for her sons. Whatever remained she gave to hungry neighbors.

sentences.zh: 嘗命僕治室，發地得千金，獻宗緒，宗緒不受，母聞乃喜。

translations.literal: Once she ordered a servant to repair a room; digging the ground they found a thousand in gold and presented it to Zongxu, who would not accept; when the mother heard of it she was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once she had a servant renovate a room. Digging in the ground they found a thousand taels of gold and presented them to Zongxu, who refused them. When his mother heard of it she was pleased.

sentences.zh: 宗緒成雍正八年進士，官至國子監司業，篤學行，有所述作。

translations.literal: Zongxu became a jinshi in the eighth year of Yongzheng, rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, was devoted in learning and conduct, and left written works.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxu passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Yongzheng, rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, was devoted in learning and conduct, and left written works.

sentences.zh: 張棠妻金，秀水人。

translations.literal: Jin, wife of Zhang Tang, was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, wife of Zhang Tang, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 棠卒，金作苦奉姑，晨炊偶有餘，日午復以進。

translations.literal: When Tang died, Jin practiced bitter devotion in serving her mother-in-law; if the morning cooking left a little over, at noon she again presented it.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang died, Jin practiced bitter devotion in serving her mother-in-law. If anything remained from the morning meal she brought it again at noon.

sentences.zh: 姑呼金共食，金慮姑不足，輒以腹痛辭。

translations.literal: When the mother-in-law called Jin to eat together, Jin, fearing there would not be enough for her, always declined on the excuse of stomach pains.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law invited her to eat together, Jin, fearing there would not be enough for her, always pleaded stomach pains.

sentences.zh: 姑病，侍食嘗藥，搔癢滌牏，鬋發拭垢，靡不躬焉。

translations.literal: When the mother-in-law fell ill, she attended her meals, tasted her medicine, scratched where she itched, washed the privy, combed and washed her hair—nothing she did not perform in person.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill she attended her meals, tasted her medicine, scratched her itches, washed the privy, combed and washed her hair—she did everything herself.

sentences.zh: 夜坐床下，聞呻吟即起。

translations.literal: At night she sat below the bed; hearing a moan she rose at once.
translations.idiomatic: At night she sat beside the bed. At the slightest moan she rose at once.

sentences.zh: 姑歿，哭之痛，曰：「吾將何怙，以冀孤兒長乎？

translations.literal: When the mother-in-law died she wept bitterly, saying: "On whom shall I now rely to hope that my orphaned son may grow up?"
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died she wept bitterly. "On whom can I rely now," she said, "to hope that my orphaned son may grow up?"

sentences.zh: 」則愈益作苦。

translations.literal: " She then practiced bitter devotion all the more.
translations.idiomatic: She then redoubled her bitter devotion.

sentences.zh: 方冬捆屨，兩手龜且裂，敷以醬及蠟淚，痛如割，必畢事乃寢。

translations.literal: In midwinter she bundled straw sandals; both hands were chapped and cracked; she spread them with sauce and beeswax, the pain like cutting, yet she would not sleep until the task was finished.
translations.idiomatic: In deep winter she wove straw sandals. Her hands cracked and bled. She dressed them with sauce and beeswax—the pain was like cutting—yet she would not sleep until the work was done.

sentences.zh: 子庚，稍長有文行，客遊以為養。

translations.literal: Her son Geng, when somewhat grown, had literary accomplishment; he traveled as a guest to support the household.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Geng, when he grew older, showed literary promise. He traveled abroad to support the household.

sentences.zh: 一日，金晨起，理髮竟，登案扳甍西南望曰：「我安得望見江西？

translations.literal: One day Jin rose in the morning, finished combing her hair, climbed onto a table, seized the ridge tile and gazed southwest, saying: "How could I hope to see Jiangxi?"
translations.idiomatic: One morning Jin finished combing her hair, climbed onto a table, gripped the roof ridge, and gazed southwest. "How could I ever see Jiangxi?" she said.

sentences.zh: 」時庚方客南昌，南昌於浙為西南，故云。

translations.literal: " At that time Geng was staying in Nanchang as a guest; Nanchang lies southwest of Zhejiang, hence her words.
translations.idiomatic: Geng was then staying in Nanchang as a guest. Nanchang lies southwest of Zhejiang—hence her words.

sentences.zh: 既得旌，泣而言曰：「我姑亦早寡​​，徒以年已逾三十，不中令甲，而我得被旌，我於是有私痛也。

translations.literal: When she received the commendation she wept and said: "My mother-in-law was also widowed young, yet only because her years had passed thirty did she fail the statutes, whereas I received the commendation—at this I feel private grief."
translations.idiomatic: When she received official commendation she wept and said, "My mother-in-law was also widowed young, yet because she was already past thirty she did not qualify under the statutes, whereas I was commended. At that I feel a private grief."

sentences.zh: 」年七十九而卒。

translations.literal: " She died at seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: She died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 洪翹妻蔣，武進人。

translations.literal: Jiang, wife of Hong Qiao, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, wife of Hong Qiao, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 翹尚義而貧，僦居臨大池，隘且濕，蔣擇處其尤陋者，暴雨，水浸淫床下。

translations.literal: Qiao valued righteousness but was poor; they rented a dwelling beside a great pond, cramped and damp; Jiang chose to lodge in the most squalid part; in a torrential rain, water seeped beneath the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao valued righteousness but was poor. They rented beside a great pond—a cramped, damp place. Jiang took the most miserable room. In a downpour water rose under the bed.

sentences.zh: 翹既不第，客遊養父母。

translations.literal: Qiao failed the examinations and traveled as a guest to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao failed the civil examinations and traveled as a guest scholar to support his parents.

sentences.zh: 俄書報病且歸，蔣挾二子舟迎，聞來舟哭聲，審其僕也，號而自擲於水，女傭持之，免。

translations.literal: Soon a letter reported that he was ill and about to return; Jiang took her two sons by boat to meet him; hearing weeping from the approaching boat, she realized it was his servant; she wailed and threw herself into the water; a maidservant seized her and she was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a letter came saying he was ill and returning. Jiang took her two sons by boat to meet him. Hearing weeping from the approaching boat she realized it was his servant. She wailed and threw herself into the water. A maidservant seized her and pulled her back.

sentences.zh: 自是率諸女針紉組織，力以自食。

translations.literal: From then on she led her daughters in needlework and weaving, supporting themselves by their own strength.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she led her daughters in needlework and weaving, supporting themselves by their own labor.

sentences.zh: 授其子禮吉讀，至禮經「夫者婦之天」，哭絕良久，呼曰：「吾何戴矣！

translations.literal: Teaching her son Liji to read, when they reached in the Book of Rites "the husband is the wife's heaven," she wept herself unconscious for a long while and cried out: "What have I left to live under!"
translations.idiomatic: Teaching her son Liji to read, when they reached in the Book of Rites "the husband is the wife's heaven," she wept until she nearly fainted and cried, "What heaven have I left to live under!"

sentences.zh: 」遂廢其句讀。

translations.literal: " She thereupon abandoned that lesson's reading and exposition.
translations.idiomatic: She stopped the lesson at that passage.

sentences.zh: 禮吉稍長，出就里中師，里中師不辨音訓，母為正其誤，日數十字。

translations.literal: When Liji grew somewhat older he went to study with a village teacher; the village teacher could not distinguish pronunciation and gloss; the mother corrected his errors, several dozen characters each day.
translations.idiomatic: When Liji grew older he studied with a village teacher who could not distinguish pronunciation and meaning. His mother corrected his errors, several dozen characters each day.

sentences.zh: 母織子誦，往往至夜分。

translations.literal: The mother wove while the son recited, often until the middle of the night.
translations.idiomatic: The mother wove while her son recited, often until midnight.

sentences.zh: 翹大父嘗守大同，父公寀獨償大​​同官逋十有餘萬，不以累弟昆。

translations.literal: Qiao's great-grandfather had once governed Datong; his father Gongcai alone repaid more than a hundred thousand in government arrears of Datong without burdening his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's great-grandfather had once governed Datong. His father Gongcai alone repaid more than a hundred thousand taels of official debt from Datong without burdening his brothers.

sentences.zh: 受託趙氏孤，坐累家破，卒全之，以此名孝義，蔣恆舉以勗禮吉。

translations.literal: Entrusted with the orphan of the Zhao clan, he was implicated, his family ruined, yet in the end preserved the orphan entirely—winning the reputation of filial righteousness; Jiang constantly cited this to encourage Liji.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with a Zhao orphan, he was ruined in the affair yet in the end preserved the child entirely, winning a reputation for filial righteousness. Jiang constantly cited this to encourage Liji.

sentences.zh: 喪舅姑，毀甚，既复喪母，疾作遂卒。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law died her grief was extreme; when she had again mourned her mother, illness seized her and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning her parents-in-law, she grieved excessively. After she had mourned her mother again, illness seized her and she died.

sentences.zh: 禮吉更名亮吉，有傳。

translations.literal: Liji changed his name to Liangji and has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liji changed his name to Hong Liangji and has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 張蟾賓妻姜，武進人。

translations.literal: Jiang, wife of Zhang Chanbin, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, wife of Zhang Chanbin, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 蟾賓父金第客死京師，妻白，食貧撫諸孤。

translations.literal: Chanbin's father Jindi died as a guest in the capital; his wife Bai, in dire poverty, raised the orphans.
translations.idiomatic: Chanbin's father Jindi died in the capital while away on business. His wife Bai, in bitter poverty, raised the orphans.

sentences.zh: 蟾賓复早卒，姜撫二子惠言、翊。

translations.literal: Chanbin also died young; Jiang raised the two sons Huiyan and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Chanbin also died young. Jiang raised their two sons Huiyan and Yi.

sentences.zh: 貧，惠言就其世父讀，歸省姜，無食，明日，惠言餓不能起，姜撫之曰：「兒不慣餓，憊耶？

translations.literal: Poor, Huiyan went to study with his father's elder brother; returning to visit Jiang, there was no food; the next day Huiyan was too hungry to rise; Jiang stroked him and said: "Child, you are not used to hunger—are you weary?"
translations.idiomatic: They were poor. Huiyan studied with his uncle and returned to visit Jiang, but there was nothing to eat. The next day Huiyan was too hungry to get up. Jiang stroked him and said, "Child, you are not used to hunger—are you worn out?"

sentences.zh: 吾與而姊、而弟時時如此也！

translations.literal: Your sister, your brother, and I are often like this!
translations.idiomatic: Your sister, your brother, and I go hungry like this all the time!

sentences.zh: 」惠言稍長，使授翊書，姜與女課女紅，常數線為節，晨起，盡三十線乃炊。

translations.literal: " When Huiyan grew somewhat older she had him teach Yi to read; Jiang and her daughter set women's needlework as their task, often counting threads for a measure—rising at dawn, they would not cook until thirty threads were finished.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiyan grew older she had him teach Yi to read. Jiang and her daughter kept to needlework, counting threads as their measure. Each morning they would not cook until thirty threads were spun.

sentences.zh: 夜燃燈視二子讀，恆至漏四下，裡黨稱姜苦節如其姑。

translations.literal: At night they burned lamps watching the two sons read, often until the fourth watch; neighbors called Jiang's bitter chastity the match of her mother-in-law's.
translations.idiomatic: At night they lit lamps and watched the two sons study, often until the fourth watch. Neighbors said Jiang's bitter devotion matched that of her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 惠言有傳。

translations.literal: Huiyan has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyan has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 施曾錫妻金，名鏡淑。

translations.literal: Jin, wife of Shi Zengxi, personal name Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, wife of Shi Zengxi, whose personal name was Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 曾錫，桐鄉人；

translations.literal: Zengxi was a native of Tongxiang;
translations.idiomatic: Zengxi came from Tongxiang;

sentences.zh: 金，震澤人。

translations.literal: Jin was a native of Zhenze.
translations.idiomatic: Jin came from Zhenze.

sentences.zh: 曾錫故有文行，以副榜貢生終。

translations.literal: Zengxi had from the first literary accomplishment and ended his career as a tribute student from the supplementary list.
translations.idiomatic: Zengxi was known from the first for literary accomplishment and ended his career as a tribute student from the supplementary civil service list.

sentences.zh: 孤福元生七年矣，教之嚴，夜篝燈讀書，福元稍怠，欲撲之，撲未下，涕泗交於頤，輒罷。

translations.literal: Orphaned, Fuyuan had been born seven years; she taught him strictly; at night by lamplight he read; when Fuyuan slackened slightly she wished to strike him, but before the blow fell tears streamed down her cheeks and she always stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed when Fuyuan was seven, she taught him strictly. Each night by lamplight he studied. When Fuyuan slackened she would reach for the rod, but before it fell tears streamed down her face and she always stopped.

sentences.zh: 初曾錫喪父母及所生父，金撤簪珥以佐葬；

translations.literal: Earlier when Zengxi mourned his adoptive parents and his birth father, Jin removed her hairpins and earrings to assist with the burials;
translations.idiomatic: When Zengxi was mourning his adoptive parents and his birth father, Jin sold her hairpins and earrings to help pay for the funerals;

sentences.zh: 及葬曾錫，家益貧。

translations.literal: When it came to burying Zengxi, the family grew still poorer.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they buried Zengxi, the household had grown still poorer.

sentences.zh: 紡績，冬寒皸瘃，十指皆流血。

translations.literal: She spun and wove; in the winter cold her hands chapped and frostbit, and all ten fingers bled.
translations.idiomatic: She spun and wove; in the winter cold her hands cracked with chilblains until all ten fingers bled.

sentences.zh: 所生姑亦卒，乃還依母。

translations.literal: Her father's sister-in-law also died, and she then returned to rely on her mother.
translations.idiomatic: When her father's sister-in-law also died, she returned to live with her mother.

sentences.zh: 歲大無，具飯飯母，並及福元，而自食豆粥雜糠覈。

translations.literal: In a year of great dearth, she prepared meals for her mother and also for Fuyuan, while she herself ate bean porridge mixed with chaff and husks.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine she set out proper meals for her mother and for Fuyuan, while she herself ate only bean porridge mixed with chaff and bran.

sentences.zh: 母病，侍尤謹。

translations.literal: When her mother fell ill, she waited upon her with especial care.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother fell ill, she nursed her with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 福元以舉人知西江安福縣，而金已前卒。

translations.literal: Fuyuan, as a juren, served as magistrate of Anfu County in western Jiangxi, while Jin had already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan passed the provincial examination and governed Anfu County in western Jiangxi, but Jin had already died.

sentences.zh: 廷璐妻惲，廷璐，完顏氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Yun, wife of Tinglu; Tinglu was of the Wanyan clan, a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner in Manchuria.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was wife of Tinglu; Tinglu was a Wanyan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 惲，陽湖人，名珠，字珍浦。

translations.literal: Yun was from Yanghu; her personal name was Zhu, her style Zhenpu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun came from Yanghu; her personal name was Zhu and her style was Zhenpu.

sentences.zh: 惲自壽平以畫名，其族多能畫。

translations.literal: The Yun clan had been famous for painting since Shouping, and many of the clan could paint.
translations.idiomatic: The Yun family had been renowned for painting since Shouping, and many of its members were skilled painters.

sentences.zh: 毛鴻調妻惲冰，字清於，畫尤工粉墨，映日有光，於珠為諸姑。

translations.literal: Mao Hongdiao's wife Yun Bing, style Qingyu, was especially accomplished in ink and color painting that gleamed in the sunlight; she was Zhu's senior aunt by marriage among the Yun women.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hongdiao's wife Yun Bing, styled Qingyu, excelled in ink painting whose colors shone in sunlight; among the Yun women she was Zhu's senior aunt.

sentences.zh: 珠亦能畫，善為詩。

translations.literal: Zhu could also paint and was skilled at composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu could paint as well and wrote poetry with skill.

sentences.zh: 廷璐為泰安知府，卒官。

translations.literal: Tinglu served as prefect of Tai'an and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Tinglu served as prefect of Tai'an and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 珠撫諸子麟慶、麟昌、麟書，教之嚴。

translations.literal: Zhu raised the sons Linqing, Linchang, and Linshu, teaching them strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu raised her sons Linqing, Linchang, and Linshu and instructed them with great severity.

sentences.zh: 持家政，肅而恕。

translations.literal: She managed the household: stern yet forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: In running the household she was austere yet forbearing.

sentences.zh: 嘗擬列女傳為蘭閨寶錄。

translations.literal: She once modeled the Biographies of Exemplary Women as the Treasured Records of the Orchid Boudoir.
translations.idiomatic: She once drafted a work modeled on the Biographies of Exemplary Women, titled Treasured Records of the Orchid Boudoir.

sentences.zh: 撰定清女子詩，為國朝女士正始集。

translations.literal: She compiled Qing women's poetry into the Correct Beginnings Collection of Ladies of the Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: She compiled poetry by Qing women into the Correct Beginnings Anthology of Ladies of Our Dynasty.

sentences.zh: 校刻壽平父日初遺書及李顒集，皆傳世。

translations.literal: She collated and printed the posthumous works of Shouping's father Richu and the collected works of Li Yong, all of which have been handed down.
translations.idiomatic: She edited and published the posthumous writings of Shouping's father Richu and the collected works of Li Yong, works still preserved today.

sentences.zh: 麟慶有傳。

translations.literal: Linqing has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Linqing has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 汪楷妻王、妾徐，蕭山人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Wang Kai, and concubine Xu were all from Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai's wife Wang and his concubine Xu were natives of Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 楷為河南淇縣典史，嘗廉民冤，白令為平反。

translations.literal: Kai served as clerk of Qi County in Henan; he once investigated a commoner's wrongful conviction and reported to the magistrate to secure reversal.
translations.idiomatic: As clerk of Qi County in Henan, Kai once took up a commoner's false conviction and persuaded the magistrate to reverse the case.

sentences.zh: 既去官，客死廣東。

translations.literal: After leaving office he died as a sojourner in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his post he died far from home in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 母七十，徐有子輝祖，幼。

translations.literal: His mother was seventy; Xu had a son Huizu, still young.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was seventy years old; Xu had borne a young son named Huizu.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，索債者至，王鬻田、出嫁時衣裝以償。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned home, creditors arrived; Wang sold fields and the garments from her bridal trousseau to pay them.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral party returned, creditors came calling; Wang sold land and her bridal finery to satisfy the debts.

sentences.zh: 楷弟不肖，恆求錢以博，甚或篡輝祖去，得錢乃歸之。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother was worthless and constantly demanded money for gambling; he even once abducted Huizu and only returned him after receiving payment.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's dissolute younger brother constantly extorted money for gambling and once even kidnapped Huizu, returning the boy only after he was paid.

sentences.zh: 已，將以母遷，王與徐力請留，奉侍甚謹。

translations.literal: Later, when they were about to move his mother away, Wang and Xu earnestly begged to keep her with them and waited upon her with great care.
translations.idiomatic: When the family planned to move the mother elsewhere, Wang and Xu pleaded to keep her and attended her with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 母垂歿，歎其賢孝。

translations.literal: As the mother neared death she sighed at their worthiness and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed the mother praised their virtue and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 教輝祖讀，或不中程，徐奉箠呼輝祖跪受教，王涕泣戒督，往往棄箠罷。

translations.literal: Teaching Huizu to read, when he failed to meet expectations Xu would take the rod and call Huizu to kneel for instruction; Wang, weeping, would warn and urge discipline but often threw down the rod and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizu's lessons fell short, Xu would take the stick and make him kneel for correction; Wang would weep and plead for mercy, and often the rod was cast aside unfinished.

sentences.zh: 貧益甚，互稱疾減食食輝祖。

translations.literal: Poverty grew worse; they each claimed illness and reduced their own food to feed Huizu.
translations.idiomatic: As poverty worsened, each would feign illness and eat less so that Huizu might have more.

sentences.zh: 輝祖長，出遊，佐州縣治刑名，王戒之曰：「汝父嘗言生人慘怛，無過囹圄中，偶撲一人，輒數日不怡，曰：'彼得無恚恨戕其生乎？

translations.literal: When Huizu grew up he went out to serve, assisting prefectures and counties in criminal matters; Wang admonished him: "Your father once said that among the miseries of the living none surpass those in prison; if he struck even one person he would be unhappy for days, saying, 'Might he harbor resentment and harm his life?'
translations.idiomatic: When Huizu came of age he went out to assist prefectures and counties in criminal cases. Wang warned him: "Your father used to say that among human miseries none surpass those in prison; if he punished even one man he would be troubled for days, asking, 'Will he bear resentment and throw away his life?'

sentences.zh: '汝佐人當知此意。

translations.literal: You who assist others must bear this meaning in mind."
translations.idiomatic: You who assist others must keep this in mind."

sentences.zh: 」輝祖自外歸，必問：「不入人死罪否？

translations.literal: Whenever Huizu returned from outside she inevitably asked: "Have you not imposed the death penalty on anyone?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huizu returned from his work she would ask: "Have you condemned anyone to death?

sentences.zh: 破人家否？

translations.literal: Have you not ruined any household?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you ruined any household?"

translations.literal: He would say: "No."
translations.idiomatic: If he answered no,

sentences.zh: 」則喜。

translations.literal: Then she rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: she rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 即言法不免，王與徐輒相視為流涕。

translations.literal: If he said the law left no alternative, Wang and Xu would look at each other and weep.
translations.idiomatic: If he said the law left no choice, Wang and Xu would look at each other and weep.

sentences.zh: 王尤不喜言人過，輝祖或偶及之，必曰：「汝能不爾即佳，此何與汝事？

translations.literal: Wang especially disliked hearing others' faults mentioned; if Huizu chanced to speak of them she would say: "It is enough that you do not act so—what business is this of yours?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang especially disliked gossip about others' faults; if Huizu chanced to mention them she would say: "It is enough that you do not act so yourself—what concern is it of yours?"

sentences.zh: 」徐居常布衣操作，歲饑，日織布一疋，易三斗粟，雖瘧不為止。

translations.literal: Xu ordinarily wore plain cloth and worked with her hands; in famine years she wove one bolt of cloth each day to exchange for three dou of grain, and did not stop even when stricken with malaria.
translations.idiomatic: Xu always wore plain cloth and worked with her own hands; in famine years she wove one bolt of cloth a day to trade for three dou of grain, and would not stop even when stricken with malaria.

sentences.zh: 一絮被，餘二十年，輝祖請易，曰：「此汝父所予，不可易也！

translations.literal: One cotton-quilted coverlet had lasted more than twenty years; when Huizu asked to replace it she said: "This was given you by your father—it cannot be exchanged!"
translations.idiomatic: A single cotton quilt had lasted more than twenty years; when Huizu asked to replace it she said: "Your father gave you this—it must not be exchanged!"

sentences.zh: 」徐病，輝祖進蓡，卻之，曰：「汝父客死，吾不獲以此進，吾何忍飲？

translations.literal: When Xu fell ill Huizu offered ginseng; she refused it, saying: "Your father died abroad and I could not offer this to him—how could I bear to drink it?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xu fell ill Huizu brought her ginseng; she refused it, saying: "Your father died far from home and I could not offer this to him—how could I bear to take it?"

sentences.zh: 」王強之，微啜而罷。

translations.literal: Wang pressed her; she sipped slightly and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang pressed her until she took a small sip and would take no more.

sentences.zh: 徐卒十餘年，輝祖成進士而王卒。

translations.literal: More than ten years after Xu's death, Huizu passed the metropolitan examination; then Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years after Xu died, Huizu passed the metropolitan examination; Wang died afterward.

sentences.zh: 輝祖有傳。

translations.literal: Huizu has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Huizu has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 馮智懋妻謝，智懋，長洲人；

translations.literal: Xie, wife of Feng Zhimao; Zhimao was from Changzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Xie, wife of Feng Zhimao; Zhimao was from Changzhou;

sentences.zh: 謝，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Xie was from Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 智懋家中落，再遇火，謝處貧，黽勉無所恨。

translations.literal: Zhimao's family declined; they suffered fire twice; Xie bore poverty and strove diligently without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng household fell on hard times and twice lost everything to fire; Xie endured poverty with tireless effort and no resentment.

sentences.zh: 子桂芬，入學為諸生，謝喜曰：「汝家久無秀才，汝繼之，甚善。

translations.literal: Their son Guifen entered school and became a licentiate; Xie rejoiced: "Your family has long been without a xiucai; you have succeeded to it—very well.
translations.idiomatic: Their son Guifen entered school and became a licentiate; Xie rejoiced: "Your family has long lacked a xiucai; you have taken up that place—very well.

sentences.zh: 原世世為秀才，毋覬科第也！

translations.literal: I only wish that generation after generation you remain xiucai—do not covet the examination ranks!"
translations.idiomatic: I only wish that generation after generation you remain xiucai—do not set your heart on higher degrees!"

sentences.zh: 」及得第，訓之曰：「人必有職，女紅中饋，婦職也，易盡耳；

translations.literal: When he earned a higher degree she admonished him: "Every person must have his duty; needlework and provision of meals are a woman's duty, soon exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: When he passed a higher examination she admonished him: "Every person must have a calling; needlework and household provision are a woman's work, and soon done;

sentences.zh: 汝當思盡其職。

translations.literal: you must think to fulfill yours fully."
translations.idiomatic: you must think how to fulfill yours to the full."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「好官不過多得錢，然則商賈耳，何名官也？

translations.literal: She also said: "A 'good official' amounts to no more than amassing money—then he is but a merchant; what is he called an official for?
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "A 'good official' is no more than one who amasses money—then he is but a merchant; what does he deserve to be called an official for?

sentences.zh: 汝謹，當不至是，勉旃！

translations.literal: You are cautious and ought not come to that—strive on!"
translations.idiomatic: You are careful and should not come to that—strive on!"

sentences.zh: 」蘇州、嘉興，皆困重賦，謝氏以催科破家。

translations.literal: Suzhou and Jiaxing were both crushed by heavy taxation; the Xie clan had been ruined by tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Jiaxing were both crushed by heavy land tax; the Xie family had been ruined by tax collection.

sentences.zh: 謝每謂桂芬：「汝他日為言官，此第一事也！

translations.literal: Xie often told Guifen: "When you one day become a censor, this must be your first concern!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie often told Guifen: "When you one day become a censor, this must be your first concern!"

sentences.zh: 」同治初，江、浙初定，桂芬佐江蘇巡撫李鴻章幕，成減賦之議。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi era, when Jiangsu and Zhejiang had just been pacified, Guifen served on Governor Li Hongzhang's staff in Jiangsu and helped frame proposals to reduce land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi era, after Jiangsu and Zhejiang had been pacified, Guifen served on Governor Li Hongzhang's staff in Jiangsu and helped draft proposals to reduce land tax.

sentences.zh: 蘇州、松江、太倉三府、州，減三之一；

translations.literal: In the three prefectures and departments of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang, tax was reduced by one third;
translations.idiomatic: In the three prefectures and departments of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Taicang, the levy was cut by one third;

sentences.zh: 常州、鎮江減十之一。

translations.literal: in Changzhou and Zhenjiang by one tenth.
translations.idiomatic: in Changzhou and Zhenjiang by one tenth.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫左宗棠繼請嘉興亦得量減，時謝已前卒。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Zuo Zongtang afterward petitioned that Jiaxing also receive proportional reduction—but by then Xie had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Zuo Zongtang later petitioned that Jiaxing receive a proportional reduction as well—but by then Xie had already died.

sentences.zh: 桂芬有傳。

translations.literal: Guifen has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Guifen has a biography elsewhere in the histories.

sentences.zh: 鄭文清妻黎，遵義人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Zheng Wenqing, was from Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li, wife of Zheng Wenqing, was from Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 事祖姑及姑能得其歡心。

translations.literal: In serving her husband's grandmother and mother-in-law she won their affection.
translations.idiomatic: She won the affection of both her husband's grandmother and her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 貧，令長子珍就傅，諸子力田，教督之甚肅。

translations.literal: Though poor, she sent the eldest son Zhen to study with a teacher while the other sons worked the fields; she taught and supervised them very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Though the family was poor, she sent her eldest son Zhen to a teacher while the other sons worked the fields, instructing them with great strictness.

sentences.zh: 珍錄平生所訓誡為母教錄。

translations.literal: Zhen recorded her lifelong admonitions as Records of a Mother's Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen compiled her lifelong teachings into Records of a Mother's Instruction.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「婦人舍言、容、工，無所謂德。

translations.literal: She once said: "Apart from speech, bearing, and handicraft, a woman has nothing that may be called virtue.
translations.idiomatic: She once said: "Apart from speech, bearing, and handicraft, a woman has nothing that may be called virtue.

sentences.zh: 言只柔聲下氣，容只衣飾整潔，工則針黹、紡績、酒漿、葅醢，終身不能盡。

translations.literal: Speech is only gentle voice and humble tone; bearing is only neat dress and adornment; handicraft is needlework, spinning, wine and pickles—a lifetime cannot exhaust it."
translations.idiomatic: Speech means a gentle voice and humble manner; bearing means neat dress and adornment; handicraft means needlework, spinning, wine, and pickles—work that can never be finished in a lifetime."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「人雖貧，禮不可不富；

translations.literal: She also said: "Though one be poor, ritual must not be poor;
translations.idiomatic: She also said: "Though one be poor, ritual observance must not be poor;

sentences.zh: 禮不富，是謂真貧。

translations.literal: when ritual is not rich, that is true poverty."
translations.idiomatic: when ritual is impoverished, that is true poverty."

sentences.zh: 」珍，儒林有傳。

translations.literal: Zhen has a biography in the Confucian scholars section.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen has a biography in the section on Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 程世雄妻萬，衡陽人。

translations.literal: Wan, wife of Cheng Shixiong, was from Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, wife of Cheng Shixiong, was from Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 世雄兄世英早卒，妻何無子，世雄旋亦卒。

translations.literal: Shixiong's elder brother Shiying died early; Shiying's wife He had no son; Shixiong soon also died.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong's elder brother Shiying died young; Shiying's wife He was childless; Shixiong soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 子學伊弱，族有爭嗣者，萬以學伊兼承世英後。

translations.literal: The son Xueyi was weak; clansmen disputed the succession; Wan had Xueyi also inherit Shiying's line.
translations.idiomatic: Their son Xueyi was still young; when kinsmen fought over the succession, Wan had Xueyi inherit Shiying's line as well.

sentences.zh: 姑喪未殯，火發，何、萬與諸婢號泣奉柩出，火為之止。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law's corpse had not yet been buried when fire broke out; He, Wan, and the maidservants wept as they bore the coffin out, and the fire ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Before her mother-in-law could be interred, fire broke out; He and Wan, with the servant girls weeping, carried the coffin from the house—and the flames died away.

sentences.zh: 萬善治家，學伊長，家漸起。

translations.literal: Wan was skilled at managing the household; as Xueyi grew up the family gradually prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Wan managed the household well; as Xueyi came of age the family slowly recovered its fortunes.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間軍興，諸將唐訓方、陳士傑、彭玉麟皆倚學伊籌兵食。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng era when military campaigns arose, the generals Tang Xunfang, Chen Shijie, and Peng Yulin all relied on Xueyi to provision troops and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng period, generals Tang Xunfang, Chen Shijie, and Peng Yulin all relied on Xueyi to supply their armies.

sentences.zh: 萬日具

translations.literal: Wan daily prepared
translations.idiomatic: Each day Wan provided

sentences.zh: 百人饌，為規畫周至，賢母名益聞。

translations.literal: meals for a hundred men, planning with thorough care; her fame as a worthy mother spread still further.
translations.idiomatic: food for a hundred men, arranging every detail with care, and her renown as a virtuous mother spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 力施與，贍諸戚族，教孫曾，皆成立。

translations.literal: She gave generously, supported various kinsmen, taught grandchildren and great-grandchildren—all achieved establishment.
translations.idiomatic: She gave liberally, supported kinsmen, and taught her grandchildren and great-grandchildren until each made his way in the world.

sentences.zh: 年八十九卒。

translations.literal: She died at eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高學山妻王，瀘州人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Gao Xueshan, was from Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, wife of Gao Xueshan, was from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 王歸學山，視前室子四皆羸弱，鞠育甚至。

translations.literal: When Wang married Xueshan she saw that the four sons of his first wife were all frail; she nursed and raised them with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: After marrying Xueshan, Wang found the four sons of his first wife all frail and weak; she reared them with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 長子病且死，泣語申母恩，原再來為母子。

translations.literal: The eldest son, falling ill and near death, wept and spoke of her motherly kindness, wishing to be mother and son again in a future life.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, dying of illness, wept and praised her kindness as a mother and prayed they might be mother and son again in the next life.

sentences.zh: 第三子病，亦如之。

translations.literal: The third son, when ill, did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The third son, when he fell ill, did the same.

sentences.zh: 逾年，學山夢二子者至，即夕，王孿生二子。

translations.literal: More than a year later Xueshan dreamed that the two sons came; that very night Wang bore twin sons.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Xueshan dreamed the two sons had returned; that same night Wang gave birth to twins.

sentences.zh: 王教諸子讀書、擇友有法度，多取科目，孿生子同舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Wang taught the sons to read and to choose friends with propriety; many passed the examinations; the twin sons both passed the provincial examination in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Wang taught her sons to study and choose companions with discretion; many entered officialdom through the examinations, and the twins passed the provincial examination together.

sentences.zh: 王氏女娥，九江屠者女也。

translations.literal: Wang's daughter E was daughter of a butcher in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang's daughter E was the daughter of a butcher in Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年，火，屠者方醉臥，娥奔火中，呼不起，遂並焚死。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi there was a fire; the butcher lay drunk asleep; E ran into the flames and could not rouse him; both perished in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 14 a fire broke out while the butcher lay drunk; E rushed into the flames but could not wake him, and both were burned to death.

sentences.zh: 張天相女巧姑，儀徵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxiang's daughter Qiaogu was from Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxiang's daughter Qiaogu was from Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年正月庚寅，火，天相方病，巧姑年十四，負父欲出，同死。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the first month of the tenth year of Qianlong, fire broke out; Tianxiang was ill; Qiaogu, aged fourteen, carried her father intending to flee but perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengyin day in the first month of Qianlong 10, fire broke out; Tianxiang was ill; fourteen-year-old Qiaogu bore her father toward the exit and died with him.

sentences.zh: 明日得其屍，猶負父也。

translations.literal: The next day when their corpses were found she was still bearing her father.
translations.idiomatic: When their bodies were found the next day she was still carrying her father on her back.

sentences.zh: 周氏女，六安人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Zhou clan, from Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the Zhou clan, from Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 父瞽，女八歲，火作，母抱女出，問：「父胡不出？

translations.literal: Her father was blind; the girl was eight; when fire broke out the mother carried the girl out; the girl asked: "Why has Father not come out?"
translations.idiomatic: Her father was blind; the girl was eight years old; when fire broke out the mother carried her out, and the girl asked: "Why hasn't Father come out?"

sentences.zh: 」母曰：「父瞽不能行，奈何？

translations.literal: The mother said: "Father is blind and cannot walk—what can be done?"
