translations.idiomatic: The mother said: "Your father is blind and cannot walk—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」女入火中，導父行，火烈迷路，俱死。

translations.literal: The girl entered the fire, guided her father as he walked; the blaze was fierce and they lost their way; both died.
translations.idiomatic: The girl went back into the flames and led her father by the hand; the fire was fierce, they lost their way, and both perished.

sentences.zh: 王孜女，慈谿人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi's daughter was from Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Wang Zhi was from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年七月乙未，乙夜慈谿火。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day of the seventh month of the sixteenth year of Kangxi, at the second watch, Cixi caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On an yiwei day in the seventh month of Kangxi 16, during the second watch, fire swept Cixi.

sentences.zh: 女方居母喪，停棺於堂。

translations.literal: The girl was in mourning for her mother; the coffin rested in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The girl was mourning her mother; the coffin still lay in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 火至，女呼舁棺，無應者，伏棺上泣。

translations.literal: When fire arrived the girl called for the coffin to be lifted; no one answered; she lay upon the coffin weeping.
translations.idiomatic: As the flames drew near she called for help to lift the coffin, but no one came; she clung to the coffin weeping.

sentences.zh: 父從火光中遙見之，抱之出，則已死。

translations.literal: Her father saw her from afar through the firelight, carried her out, but she was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Her father glimpsed her through the fire, pulled her out, but she was already dead.

sentences.zh: 灌以礬水，稍甦，聲出喉間，僅屬。

translations.literal: They poured alum water over her; she revived slightly; sound came from her throat but barely held.
translations.idiomatic: They poured alum water on her; she revived slightly, but her voice was no more than a thread in her throat.

sentences.zh: 問：「母棺出否？

translations.literal: She asked: "Has Mother's coffin been brought out?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked: "Has my mother's coffin been carried out?"

sentences.zh: 」家人不答，遂哽咽而絕。

translations.literal: The household gave no answer; she then choked with sobs and expired.
translations.idiomatic: Her family did not answer; she choked on a sob and died.

sentences.zh: 女年十五。

translations.literal: The girl was fifteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: The girl was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 薩玉瑞妻許，閩人。

translations.literal: Xu, wife of Sa Yurui, a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, wife of Sa Yurui, was from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 夫亡，姑初喪，火發，護姑柩不去，同燼。

translations.literal: Her husband died; her mother-in-law had just died; fire broke out; she guarded the mother-in-law's coffin and would not leave; together they were consumed in the flames.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband died and her mother-in-law had only just been laid in her coffin, fire broke out; she would not leave the bier and perished with it in the flames.

sentences.zh: 繆滸妻蔡，名蕙，泰州人。

translations.literal: Cai, wife of Miao Hu, named Hui, a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, wife of Miao Hu and called Hui, was from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 父孕琦，生五女，而蕙為長。

translations.literal: Her father Yun Qi had five daughters; Hui was the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yun Qi had five daughters; Hui was the oldest.

sentences.zh: 字滸，未行，孕琦坐法論死，繫獄待決。

translations.literal: Betrothed to Hu, not yet married; Yun Qi was convicted by law and sentenced to death, imprisoned awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to Hu but had not yet married when Yun Qi was convicted and condemned to death, held in prison awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 蕙絕嗜好，屏服飾，寢不解衣，嚴寒不設爐火。

translations.literal: Hui gave up all indulgences, put aside dress and ornaments, slept without removing her clothes, and in severe cold did not set up a brazier.
translations.idiomatic: Hui renounced every pleasure, laid aside fine dress, slept fully clothed, and would not light a brazier even in bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 居四年，滸請婚，蕙謝不行。

translations.literal: After four years Hu requested the marriage; Hui declined and would not go through with it.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on, Hu asked to complete the marriage, but Hui refused and would not go to him.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十八年，聖祖巡江南，蕙伏道旁上疏，略云：「妾聞在昔淳于緹縈為父鳴冤贖罪，漢文帝憐而釋之，載之前史，傳為盛典。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor toured Jiangnan; Hui prostrated herself beside the road and submitted a memorial, stating in brief: "Your handmaid has heard that in antiquity Chunyu Tiying pleaded her father's wrong and ransom for his crime; Emperor Wen of Han pitied her and released him; it is recorded in former histories and handed down as a grand precedent."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28, when the emperor toured the south, Hui knelt by the roadside and submitted a petition that began: "I have read how long ago Chunyu Tiying cried out her father's innocence and offered herself in his stead; Emperor Wen of Han took pity and set him free—a story the histories praise as a noble precedent."

sentences.zh: 今妾父孕琦被仇害，自逮獄以來，妾日夜悲號，籥天無路。

translations.literal: Now your handmaid's father Yun Qi was harmed by enemies; since he was seized and imprisoned, your handmaid has wept and wailed day and night, her voice sealed from heaven with no way through.
translations.idiomatic: Now my father Yun Qi has been destroyed by his foes; from the day he was taken I have cried out day and night, yet heaven seems barred against me.

sentences.zh: 每夕遙望宸闕，禮拜數千，於今三年，寒暑靡輟。

translations.literal: Each night she gazed toward the imperial palace and bowed in worship thousands of times; for three years now, through cold and heat, she has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Every night I turn toward the palace and bow thousands of times; for three years, through winter and summer alike, I have not stopped.

sentences.zh: 今幸駕臨淮海，是誠千載奇逢，妾原效緹縈之故事，冒死鳴哀，伏維天鑑。

translations.literal: Now, fortunate that Your Majesty's carriage has come to the Huai-Hai region, this is truly a once-in-a-thousand-years meeting; your handmaid wishes to follow Tiying's example, risking death to cry out her grief, prostrate and begging Heaven's discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has come to the Huai-Hai coast, this is a chance that comes once in a thousand years; I beg to follow Tiying's example, risking my life to plead, and trust that Heaven will see.

sentences.zh: 」上下其疏江南江西總督覆讞，二十九年，讞上，孕琦得減死。

translations.literal: The memorial was forwarded up and down; the Governor-General of Jiangnan and Jiangxi reviewed the case; in the twenty-ninth year the review was submitted; Yun Qi received commutation of death.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was sent up and down the bureaucracy; the governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi reheard the case; in the twenty-ninth year the review was submitted and Yun Qi's sentence was reduced from death.

sentences.zh: 蕙歸滸，未一年，卒。

translations.literal: Hui returned to Hu; before a year had passed, she died.
translations.idiomatic: Hui went to Hu as his wife; within the year she was dead.

sentences.zh: 濮氏女，桐鄉人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Pu clan, a native of Tongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the Pu family, from Tongxiang.

sentences.zh: 其父無子，而母妒，不使置媵侍，家萬金悉畀女。

translations.literal: Her father had no son; the mother was jealous and would not allow him to take concubines; the family's wealth of ten thousand in gold all went to the daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had no son, but her mother, jealous, would not let him take a concubine; the family's entire fortune of ten thousand in gold passed to the daughter.

sentences.zh: 嫁吳生，予田宅、奴婢、什物皆具。

translations.literal: She married a Wu gentleman; fields, houses, slaves, maids, and every article were provided in full.
translations.idiomatic: She married a man of the Wu clan, who received fields, a house, servants, and a full household outfit.

sentences.zh: 女獨愍父未有子，嘗從容諫母，母怒，罵曰：「吾萬金餉汝，犬豕猶知人意，況人乎？

translations.literal: The daughter alone pitied that her father still had no son; she once gently remonstrated with her mother; the mother was angry and cursed: "I have fed you ten thousand in gold; even dogs and pigs know another's mind—how much more a person?"
translations.idiomatic: The girl alone grieved that her father still had no heir; once she gently urged her mother, who flew into a rage and shouted: "I have poured ten thousand in gold into you—dogs and pigs know gratitude; are you less than they?"

sentences.zh: 」女不敢復言。

translations.literal: The daughter dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: The girl dared not speak again.

sentences.zh: 乃為父置婢其家，時父至，使侍父。

translations.literal: Thereupon she placed a maid in her father's house; when her father came, she had the maid attend him.
translations.idiomatic: So she secretly set a maid in her father's home and, whenever he visited, had the maid wait on him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，果生男，載而之母家，會濮氏長老，見男於廟。

translations.literal: After more than a year a boy was indeed born; she carried him to her mother's home, gathered the Pu clan elders, and presented the boy in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: After a year a son was born; she brought the child to her mother's house, summoned the Pu elders, and presented him in the clan temple.

sentences.zh: 具白母，賀母有子，母憾女，盡收田宅、奴婢、什物，驅就他舍，屏勿復相見。

translations.literal: She fully told her mother, congratulating her that she had a son; the mother resented the daughter, reclaimed all fields, houses, slaves, maids, and goods, drove her to another dwelling, and barred her from meeting again.
translations.idiomatic: She told her mother everything and congratulated her on having a son; the mother, furious at the daughter, seized back every field, house, servant, and possession, drove her into another lodging, and forbade her ever to return.

sentences.zh: 吳生既以婦富，乃驟貧，憤恚欲殺女，女度無所容，自經死。

translations.literal: Wu, having grown rich through his wife, suddenly became poor; enraged he wished to kill the daughter; seeing nowhere to turn, she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, who had grown wealthy through his wife, was suddenly ruined; in rage he meant to kill her, and seeing no refuge she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 李氏女，鹿邑人，次三。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Li clan of Luyi, called San, the third daughter.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the Li family of Luyi, the third child, called San.

sentences.zh: 父麒生與族人礎、挺九有隙，挺九語礎，若與麒生有殺姊仇，不先之，終為害。

translations.literal: Her father Qisheng had a grudge with kinsmen Chu and Tingjiu; Tingjiu told Chu, "If you and Qisheng have the grievance of his killing your elder sister, if you do not strike first, in the end he will harm you."
translations.idiomatic: Her father Qisheng was at odds with kinsmen Chu and Tingjiu; Tingjiu urged Chu, "Qisheng killed your elder sister—if you do not strike first, he will destroy you in the end."

sentences.zh: 礎與其子兆龍行求麒生，共毆之，垂死，乃棄去。

translations.literal: Chu with his son Zhaolong went out seeking Qisheng, together beat him; near death, they then abandoned him and left.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and his son Zhaolong went out after Qisheng, beat him together, and left him for dead.

sentences.zh: 三時年十九，麒生將死，唶曰：「仇殺我，我無子能報者，尚何言！

translations.literal: San was then nineteen; as Qisheng was dying he hissed: "Enemies have killed me; I have no son who can take revenge—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: San was nineteen; as Qisheng lay dying he groaned: "My enemies have killed me, and I have no son to avenge me—what is left to say!"

translations.literal: He cried: "Heaven! Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He cried, "Heaven! Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」遂絕。

translations.literal: And expired.
translations.idiomatic: And breathed his last.

sentences.zh: 三請於母，訟縣及府，皆不省。

translations.literal: San petitioned her mother, sued at the district and prefecture; none took notice.
translations.idiomatic: San begged her mother's leave and brought suit at the district and prefectural yamens, but no one would hear her.

sentences.zh: 訟巡撫，下開封府同知治，挺九好語三，原養母，請得息訟，三扼其吭，齧面盡壞，卒脫去。

translations.literal: She sued before the provincial governor; the case was sent to the Kaifeng sub-prefect for judgment; Tingjiu spoke kindly to San, offering to support her mother, asking to settle the suit; San seized his throat and bit his face until it was ruined, but he escaped in the end.
translations.idiomatic: She appealed to the governor; the case was sent to the Kaifeng vice-prefect. Tingjiu spoke her fair words, promising to support her mother if she would drop the suit; San seized him by the throat and tore his face to shreds before he broke free.

sentences.zh: 獄上，當礎死，礎自殺。

translations.literal: The case went up; Chu was liable for death; Chu killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported upward Chu was condemned to death; he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 兆龍杖，創甚，亦死。

translations.literal: Zhaolong received the cudgel punishment; his wounds were severe; he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolong was beaten with the rod; his wounds were grave and he died as well.

sentences.zh: 三以禍始挺九，顧無罪，走京師，擊登聞院鼓自列。

translations.literal: San held that the trouble began with Tingjiu, who yet went unpunished; she fled to the capital, struck the drum at the Court of Memorials, and presented her own account.
translations.idiomatic: San held that Tingjiu had started the feud yet gone free; she fled to the capital, beat the drum at the Memorials Gate, and laid out her case herself.

sentences.zh: 下巡撫覆按，會挺九亦死。

translations.literal: The order went down for the governor to reinvestigate; it happened that Tingjiu also died.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the governor to reinvestigate; by then Tingjiu was dead as well.

sentences.zh: 三泣告父墓曰：「仇雖盡，然不棄於市，恨未雪也！

translations.literal: San wept before her father's tomb saying: "Though the enemies are all gone, yet they were not exposed in the marketplace—my grievance is not yet washed away!"
translations.idiomatic: San wept at her father's grave: "My enemies are gone, yet none was executed and exposed in the market—my vengeance is still incomplete!"

sentences.zh: 」乃不嫁養母。

translations.literal: Thereupon she did not marry and nourished her mother.
translations.idiomatic: She never married and devoted herself to caring for her mother.

sentences.zh: 居十五年，康熙三十七年八月，母卒，三治喪葬竟，自經死。

translations.literal: She lived thus fifteen years; in the eighth month of the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi her mother died; when San had finished the mourning and burial, she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years passed; in the eighth month of Kangxi 37 her mother died; when the mourning and burial were done, San hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，知縣海寧許菼表其墓，環墓為之田，曰「李孝女墓田」。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, Haijing magistrate Xu Shan marked her tomb, circled the tomb with fields for its upkeep, named them "Fields of the Li Filial Daughter's Tomb."
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong era the Haijing magistrate Xu Shan marked her tomb and set aside encircling fields for its upkeep, called the "Fields of the Li Filial Daughter's Tomb."

sentences.zh: 來氏二女，蕭山人。

translations.literal: Two daughters of the Lai clan, natives of Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters of the Lai family, from Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 姊曰鳳筠，年十四。

translations.literal: The elder sister was named Fengyun, aged fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: The elder sister was called Fengyun; she was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 父客福建，從渡古田篛洋。

translations.literal: Their father was a sojourner in Fujian; crossing from Gutian through Zhuoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Their father was working in Fujian and was crossing from Gutian by way of Zhuoyang.

sentences.zh: 父墮水，鳳筠方臥病，聞遽起，躍入水，呼救。

translations.literal: Father fell into the water; Fengyun was lying ill; hearing it she rose at once, leaped into the water, and called for help.
translations.idiomatic: Their father fell into the river; Fengyun, though bedridden, heard the cry, sprang up, plunged in after him, and shouted for help.

sentences.zh: 魚舟集，援出水，鳳筠栗無人色，猶為父易衣。

translations.literal: Fishing boats gathered; they pulled him from the water; Fengyun trembled, her face like no living person's, yet still changed her father's clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Fishing boats came; they hauled him out. Fengyun shook, her face drained of color, yet she still changed her father's wet clothes.

sentences.zh: 夜半，遂死。

translations.literal: At midnight she died.
translations.idiomatic: By midnight she was dead.

sentences.zh: 鳳蓀，其女弟也。

translations.literal: Fengsun was her younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsun was her younger sister.

sentences.zh: 父病，露禱百餘夕，不勝寒，亦死。

translations.literal: Father was ill; she prayed in the open dew for more than a hundred nights; unable to bear the cold, she too died.
translations.idiomatic: When their father fell ill she prayed outdoors for more than a hundred nights; she could not endure the cold and died as well.

sentences.zh: 曾尚增女衍綸，長清人。

translations.literal: Yanlun, daughter of Zeng Shangzeng, a native of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlun, daughter of Zeng Shangzeng, was from Changqing.

sentences.zh: 尚增以庶吉士改官，遷知郴州，衍綸從。

translations.literal: Shangzeng, having shifted from Hanlin probationer to another post, was transferred to magistrate of Chenzhou; Yanlun accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzeng left the Hanlin academy for regular office and was appointed magistrate of Chenzhou; Yanlun went with him.

sentences.zh: 母病瘓不能起，衍綸日夜侍。

translations.literal: Mother was paralyzed and could not rise; Yanlun attended day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was paralyzed and could not rise; Yanlun waited on her day and night.

sentences.zh: 居四年，一夕，母命衍綸少休，女傭就床下熏衣，遺火灼帷。

translations.literal: After four years, one night the mother told Yanlun to rest a little; a maidservant warmed clothes beneath the bed; a stray flame scorched the curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on, one night her mother urged Yanlun to rest; a maid was steaming clothes under the bed and a spark set the curtains ablaze.

sentences.zh: 衍綸突火入抱母號，救者以衍綸出，復入，哭且呼曰：「速救夫人！

translations.literal: Yanlun dashed through fire in to embrace her mother crying; rescuers pulled Yanlun out; she went back in, weeping and calling: "Save the Lady quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanlun rushed through the flames to her mother, wailing; rescuers dragged her out, but she ran back in, crying: "Save my mother first!"

sentences.zh: 夫人出，我乃出。

translations.literal: When the Lady is out, then I will come out.
translations.idiomatic: Only when my mother is safe will I leave.

sentences.zh: 」火冪床，救者不得入，尚增厲聲呼衍綸出，不應，火益熾，遂殉。

translations.literal: Fire covered the bed; rescuers could not enter; Shangzeng shouted harshly for Yanlun to come out; she did not answer; the fire grew fiercer; she perished with her mother.
translations.idiomatic: Flames engulfed the bed and no one could reach them; Shangzeng shouted for Yanlun to come out, but she would not answer; the fire roared on and she died with her mother.

sentences.zh: 既滅火，見衍綸身覆母，兩體膠結不可解。

translations.literal: Once the fire was out, they saw Yanlun's body covering her mother; the two bodies were glued together and could not be separated.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire was out they found Yanlun sprawled over her mother; the two bodies had fused and could not be pulled apart.

sentences.zh: 時乾隆二十三年十二月乙亥，衍綸年十五。

translations.literal: It was the yihai day of the twelfth month of the twenty-third year of Qianlong; Yanlun was fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: This was on a yihai day in the twelfth month of Qianlong 23; Yanlun was fifteen.

sentences.zh: 又有王氏女，懷遠人，母亦病瘓，火作，女突火入負母，俱燼。

translations.literal: There was also a Wang clanswoman of Huaiyuan; her mother too was paralyzed; when fire broke out the girl dashed through fire in, carrying her mother on her back; both were reduced to ash.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Wang girl of Huaiyuan whose mother was likewise paralyzed; when fire broke out she charged in, lifted her mother on her back, and both were burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 劉魁妻徐，霍丘人。

translations.literal: Xu, wife of Liu Kui, a native of Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, wife of Liu Kui, was from Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 既嫁而歸省，火作，負父出，復入負母，病瘓不能起，俱焚。

translations.literal: Having married she returned to visit her parents; fire broke out; she carried her father out, went back in to carry her mother; paralyzed, unable to rise, both were burned.
translations.idiomatic: Married, she had come home on a visit when fire broke out; she carried her father out, went back for her mother, who was paralyzed and could not rise, and all three perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 火熄，見徐跪床下，猶執母手。

translations.literal: When the fire died, they found Xu kneeling beneath the bed, still holding her mother's hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the flames died they found Xu kneeling under the bed, still clutching her mother's hand.

sentences.zh: 薛中奇女，宿州人。

translations.literal: A daughter of Xue Zhongqi, a native of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of Xue Zhongqi, from Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 侍祖母，火作，扶祖母出，樑折，承以肩，焚死，祖母得免。

translations.literal: She was attending her grandmother; fire broke out; she supported grandmother out; a beam broke; she bore it on her shoulder, was burned to death; grandmother was spared.
translations.idiomatic: She was caring for her grandmother when fire broke out; as she helped her out a beam gave way; she took the weight on her shoulder, was burned to death, and her grandmother escaped.

sentences.zh: 呂氏女，平陸人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Lü clan, a native of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the Lü family, from Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 父卒，母且嫁，女生七年，痛哭諫其母，母不聽，則日長跽母前，且哭且言，母意終不回。

translations.literal: Father died; mother was about to remarry; the girl was seven; she wept bitterly and remonstrated; mother would not listen; then each day she knelt long before her mother, weeping and speaking; mother's resolve never turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Her father died and her mother meant to remarry; the girl was seven. She wept and pleaded, but her mother would not listen; day after day she knelt before her, weeping and begging, yet her mother's mind never changed.

sentences.zh: 一日晨，潛出，家人求之勿得；

translations.literal: One morning she slipped out secretly; the family sought her but could not find her;
translations.idiomatic: One morning she slipped away; the family searched but could not find her;

sentences.zh: 暮，途人或言墦間有幼女死焉。

translations.literal: At dusk a passerby said that beside a mound a young girl lay dead.
translations.idiomatic: at evening a traveler said a little girl lay dead beside a burial mound.

sentences.zh: 家人就視，則女哭父瘞所，死矣，淚血溢兩眶，遍地盡碧。

translations.literal: The family went to look; the girl was weeping at her father's burial place; she was dead; tear-blood overflowed both eye sockets; the ground everywhere was green.
translations.idiomatic: They went to look and found her at her father's grave, already dead; blood and tears had filled both eyes, and the ground around her was green with it.

sentences.zh: 及斂，視其寢處，枕上血深漬數重。

translations.literal: When they prepared her for burial, they looked at where she had slept; on the pillow blood had soaked through many layers deep.
translations.idiomatic: When they laid her out they saw that her pillow at home was soaked through with blood in layer upon layer.

sentences.zh: 佘長安女，名酉州，四川重慶人。

translations.literal: Youzhou, daughter of She Chang'an, a native of Chongqing, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou, daughter of She Chang'an, was from Chongqing in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 長安妄訟人聚博宰耕牛，坐誣，戍湖北。

translations.literal: Chang'an falsely accused someone of gathering to gamble and slaughtering a plow ox; he was convicted of false accusation and exiled to serve in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an had falsely charged a man with gambling and butchering a plow ox; convicted of malicious prosecution, he was banished to labor in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年，酉州走京師，詣都察院，自陳祖父、母年皆逾八十，乞赦其父得侍養。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing, Youzhou ran to the capital, went to the Censorate, stated herself that grandfather and mother were both over eighty, begged pardon for her father so he might return to serve and nourish them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 16, Youzhou fled to the capital and petitioned the Censorate, declaring that her grandfather and mother were both past eighty and begging that her father be pardoned so he could come home to support them.

sentences.zh: 事聞，仁宗以長安罪非常赦所不原，至配所已九年，其女年甫十一，不遠數千里匍匐奔訴，情可愍，命赦長安。

translations.literal: The matter was reported; Emperor Renzong held that Chang'an's crime was of the sort ordinary amnesties do not remit, yet he had already been at his place of assignment nine years; his daughter was only eleven; crawling not far short of a thousand li to plead—her feeling could be pitied; he ordered Chang'an pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the case reached the throne, Emperor Renzong noted that Chang'an's offense was not one ordinary amnesties covered, yet he had already served nine years in exile and his daughter, only eleven, had crawled nearly a thousand li to plead—her devotion moved him, and he ordered Chang'an released.

sentences.zh: 王法夔女，名淑春，揚州人。

translations.literal: Shuchun, daughter of Wang Fakui, a native of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shuchun, daughter of Wang Fakui, was from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 法夔老而貧，淑春誓不嫁，力針黹為養。

translations.literal: Fakui was old and poor; Shuchun vowed not to marry, strove at needlework to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Fakui grew old and poor; Shuchun vowed never to marry and supported him by tireless needlework.

sentences.zh: 方冬，手龜身寒顫，工不輟。

translations.literal: In mid-winter her hands cracked with cold and her body shivered, yet she did not stop her work.
translations.idiomatic: In deep winter her hands split with cold and her body shook, yet she never laid down her work.

sentences.zh: 法夔至七十餘卒，淑春以首觸壁，額裂死。

translations.literal: Fakui lived to over seventy and died; Shuchun struck her head against the wall; her forehead split and she died.
translations.idiomatic: Fakui lived past seventy and died; Shuchun dashed her head against the wall until her forehead split open and she died.

sentences.zh: 武仁女，名端，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Duan, daughter of Wu Ren, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, daughter of Wu Ren, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 能讀書，原不嫁事父母，父母不可。

translations.literal: She could read; she wished not to marry but to serve her parents; her parents would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: She could read and wished to remain unmarried to serve her parents, but they would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 少長，母偶疾，夜求藥，墜樓，折脊，則喜曰：「吾今形殘，不可匹人，吾自是得終事父母矣！

translations.literal: When she grew a little older, mother had an occasional illness; at night seeking medicine she fell from a building and broke her spine; then she rejoiced saying: "Now my form is ruined; I cannot be matched to a man—I can at last spend my life serving my parents!"
translations.idiomatic: As she grew, her mother fell briefly ill; going out at night for medicine she fell from a stair and broke her spine. She rejoiced: "Now I am maimed and no man will have me—I may at last devote my life to my parents!"

sentences.zh: 」仁客死貴州，端從母迎喪，至則貲已盡，力針黹奉母，而蓄其餘。

translations.literal: Ren died abroad in Guizhou; Duan followed her mother to meet the coffin; when they arrived their funds were gone; she strove at needlework to support her mother while saving the surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Ren died far from home in Guizhou; Duan went with her mother to fetch the body, but their money was spent by the time they arrived; she sewed to support her mother and saved every spare coin.

sentences.zh: 居十有七年，始克以喪歸。

translations.literal: After seventeen years she was able at last to bring the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years later she was finally able to bring his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 唐氏女，名素，無錫人。

translations.literal: Su, a daughter of the Tang clan, a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Su, a daughter of the Tang family, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 貧無昆弟，亦不嫁，鬻畫以贍父母。

translations.literal: Poor, without brothers, she also did not marry; she sold paintings to support her parents.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and without brothers, she too refused to marry and sold her paintings to support her parents.

sentences.zh: 張桐女，名富，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Fu, daughter of Zhang Tong, a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, daughter of Zhang Tong, was from Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，山水暴發，家人皆走避。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang mountain floods burst forth violently; the household all fled for safety.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 9 a sudden mountain flood struck and the whole household fled.

sentences.zh: 桐方病臥，富將負父出，弱不勝。

translations.literal: Tong was lying ill; Fu was about to carry her father out but was too weak to bear him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong lay sick in bed; Fu tried to carry him out but was too frail.

sentences.zh: 水大至，父揮之去，號泣，俱溺。

translations.literal: The flood came great; father waved her away; weeping and calling, both drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The torrent rose; her father waved her away, but she clung to him, wailing, and both drowned.

sentences.zh: 水退，家人至，見富兩手猶握父臂不釋。

translations.literal: When the water receded the family came; they saw Fu's two hands still gripping her father's arm and not releasing.
translations.idiomatic: When the water fell the family returned and found Fu's hands still locked on her father's arm.

sentences.zh: 汪儼聘妻周，劉氏女名密，吳某聘妻周，皆六安人。

translations.literal: Zhou, betrothed wife of Wang Yi; a Liu clanswoman named Mi; Zhou, betrothed wife of a certain Wu—all natives of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, betrothed to Wang Yi; a Liu girl named Mi; and another Zhou, betrothed to a Wu—all were from Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 儼卒，周歸注氏，事舅姑，水至，周從姑乘屋，攀樹，姑墮水，周躍下拯之，與俱死。

translations.literal: Yi died; Zhou returned to the Zhu household and served her parents-in-law; when flood came Zhou with her mother-in-law climbed onto the roof, clambered onto a tree; the mother-in-law fell into the water; Zhou leaped down to save her and died with her.
translations.idiomatic: Yi died and Zhou went to live with the Zhu family and serve her in-laws; when the flood came she climbed onto the roof with her mother-in-law and then into a tree; when the older woman fell into the water Zhou leaped after her and both drowned.

sentences.zh: 密與母同墮，得板扉，緣以上，扉欹屢墮。

translations.literal: Mi and her mother fell in together; they got a plank door, climbed up along it; the door tilted and repeatedly nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: Mi and her mother fell in together, seized a plank door, and tried to climb on it, but it tipped and nearly capsized again and again.

sentences.zh: 母呼密速上，密曰：「扉狹不足全我母女，冀活母，兒不上矣！

translations.literal: Mother called Mi to climb up quickly; Mi said: "The door is narrow—not enough to save both mother and daughter; I hope Mother may live; your daughter will not go up!"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother urged Mi to climb up at once; Mi said, "The plank is too narrow for both of us—I pray you live, Mother; I will not climb up!"

sentences.zh: 」遂死。

translations.literal: And she died.
translations.idiomatic: And she drowned.

sentences.zh: 週既入水，或援之登舟，問：「父母存否？

translations.literal: Zhou had already entered the water; someone pulled her onto a boat and asked: "Are your parents alive?"
translations.idiomatic: The other Zhou was already in the water when someone hauled her into a boat and asked whether her parents still lived.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「不知。

translations.literal: All said: "We do not know."
translations.idiomatic: No one could tell her.

sentences.zh: 」復躍入水死。

translations.literal: She leaped into the water again and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself back into the flood and died.

sentences.zh: 李荐一聘妻曾，南豐人。

translations.literal: Zeng, betrothed wife of Li Jianyi, a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng, betrothed to Li Jianyi, was from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 未行，遇水，室盡圮，母投水死。

translations.literal: Not yet married; they met with flood; the house was entirely destroyed; mother threw herself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the marriage could take place a flood destroyed their home; her mother threw herself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 女援不及，入水殉。

translations.literal: The daughter could not save her in time; she entered the water and died with her.
translations.idiomatic: The girl could not reach her in time and followed her into the water to die.

sentences.zh: 袁斯鳳女璱，字儀貞，江蘇華亭人。

translations.literal: Yuan Si-feng's daughter Se, courtesy name Yizhen, was a native of Huating in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Se, daughter of Yuan Si-feng and known by the courtesy name Yizhen, came from Huating in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 斯鳳官河南懷慶府黃沁同知，璱事父母孝，視疾尤謹。

translations.literal: Si-feng served as Tongzhi of Huangqin in Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan; Se served her parents with filial piety and was especially careful when watching over illness.
translations.idiomatic: Si-feng held the post of subprefect of Huangqin in Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan. Se was devoted to her parents and exceptionally attentive in nursing them through illness.

sentences.zh: 母陳有寒疾，璱榻母側，視起居。

translations.literal: Her mother Chen had a cold affliction; Se set her couch beside her mother and watched over her daily comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother Chen fell ill with a chronic chill, Se slept on a pallet at her bedside and attended to her every movement.

sentences.zh: 母命之臥，頃輒起。

translations.literal: Her mother ordered her to lie down; presently she would rise again.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother urged her to rest, she would lie down only briefly before rising again.

sentences.zh: 八年，陳疾少瘥，璱乃曰：「世無不可治之疾，人力未至，而委之天命，則以為不可治爾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chen's illness improved somewhat; Se then said: "In the world there is no illness that cannot be treated; when human effort has not been expended and one ascribes it to Heaven's mandate, then one says it cannot be treated—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Chen's illness eased a little, and Se said, "There is no sickness under heaven that cannot be cured. When effort has not been tried and men call it fate, they only mean they have given up."

sentences.zh: 」斯鳳疾作，乍劇乍瘥，夜靜或大雪，璱嚴立窗外，伺聲息，往往不眠。

translations.literal: Si-feng's illness arose, now severe now eased; on still nights when snow fell thick, Se stood rigorously outside the window, listening for breath and movement, often going without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: When Si-feng fell ill, his condition shifted between crisis and respite. On quiet nights when snow piled deep, Se would stand rigidly outside his window, listening for his breathing, often until dawn without sleep.

sentences.zh: 道光十四年，斯鳳疾大作，醫謝不治。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of the Daoguang reign Si-feng's illness flared greatly; physicians declined, saying it could not be cured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Daoguang (1834), Si-feng's illness grew desperate. The doctors gave him up.

sentences.zh: 璱聞涕泣，已而怒曰：「誰謂不可愈，吾必欲愈之！

translations.literal: Se heard this and wept; presently she said angrily: "Who says he cannot recover? I must recover him!"
translations.idiomatic: Se wept when she heard it, then cried in anger, "Who says he cannot be saved? I will save him!"

sentences.zh: 」而斯鳳竟卒。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Si-feng died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Si-feng died all the same.

sentences.zh: 後四日，璱闔扉欲自經，嫂過而勸之，璱泣誓死。

translations.literal: Four days later Se closed the door intending to hang herself; her sister-in-law passed by and persuaded her; Se wept and vowed to die.
translations.idiomatic: Four days later Se barred her door to hang herself. Her sister-in-law came upon her and pleaded with her; Se wept and swore she would die.

sentences.zh: 嫂喻以殺身非孝，璱作色曰：「吾自欲死，此時雖孔子、硃子以吾為不孝，吾亦惟死爾！

translations.literal: Her sister-in-law reasoned that killing oneself was not filial; Se showed anger and said: "I wish to die of my own will; even if at this time Confucius and Zhu Xi called me unfilial, I would still have only death!"
translations.idiomatic: Her sister-in-law argued that suicide was not filial piety. Se flushed and said, "I mean to die. Even if Confucius and Zhu Xi himself stood here and called me unfilial, I would die all the same."

sentences.zh: 」嫂曰：「獨不念病母乎？

translations.literal: Her sister-in-law said: "Do you alone not consider your ailing mother?"
translations.idiomatic: "Have you no thought for your sick mother?" her sister-in-law asked.

sentences.zh: 」璱曰：「有汝在。

translations.literal: Se said: "With you here."
translations.idiomatic: Se said, "You are here."

sentences.zh: 」乃告其母，共諭慰之。

translations.literal: Then they told her mother and together admonished and comforted her.
translations.idiomatic: They told her mother, and mother and daughter-in-law together pleaded with her until she yielded.

sentences.zh: 又二日，璱竟死。

translations.literal: Two days more and Se died in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later she was dead.

sentences.zh: 死後，母察奩具，得斷釧。

translations.literal: After her death her mother inspected the toilet case and found a broken bracelet.
translations.idiomatic: After her death her mother searched her dresser and found a bracelet snapped in two—the trace of her suicide.

sentences.zh: 丁氏女，鶴慶人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Ding clan, a native of Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: A daughter of the Ding family, from Heqing.

sentences.zh: 父貧，段石為灰以自給，女助之。

translations.literal: Her father was poor; he cut stone into lime to support himself, and the daughter helped.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was poor. He quarried stone and burned it to lime to live; his daughter worked beside him.

sentences.zh: 年十六，父卒，女力作養母。

translations.literal: At age sixteen her father died; the daughter labored strenuously to support her mother.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen her father died. She took up hard labor to support her mother.

sentences.zh: 嘗負重而躓，遂痀僂。

translations.literal: Once she bore a heavy load and stumbled, and became hunchbacked.
translations.idiomatic: Once she stumbled under a heavy load and was left hunchbacked for life.

sentences.zh: 為傭，食於傭家​​，每飯思母，輒哽咽。

translations.literal: Working as a hired hand, she ate at the employer's house; at every meal she thought of her mother and would choke with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Hired out as a laborer, she ate at her employer's table; at every meal she thought of her mother and could not swallow without weeping.

sentences.zh: 人憐之，許其分食以遺。

translations.literal: People pitied her and allowed her to set aside food to take home.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pitied her let her set aside part of her meal to carry home.

sentences.zh: 否必為母炊竟乃出傭。

translations.literal: If not permitted she would cook for her mother first and only then go out to work.
translations.idiomatic: When they would not allow it, she cooked for her mother first and only then went out to hire herself.

sentences.zh: 居四十餘年，母卒女亦卒。

translations.literal: After more than forty years her mother died and the daughter died too.
translations.idiomatic: After more than forty years her mother died; the daughter died soon after.

sentences.zh: 硃棫之女，武清人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yu's daughter, a native of Wuqing.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Zhu Yu, of Wuqing.

sentences.zh: 字縣諸生曹文甲。

translations.literal: Betrothed to Cao Wenjia, a district student.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to Cao Wenjia, a licentiate of the district school.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，母病，奉事良謹。

translations.literal: Her father died early; her mother fell ill; she served with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Her father died while she was young. When her mother fell ill, she waited on her with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 將婚，女堅請留侍母。

translations.literal: When the marriage was near, the girl firmly requested to remain and attend her mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the wedding drew near, she begged to stay home and nurse her mother.

sentences.zh: 母卒，治喪葬，請旌母節，奉母主入祠，見祠有孝女，為低徊甚久，歸遂自裁。

translations.literal: When her mother died she managed the funeral, petitioned to have her mother's chastity enshrined, placed her mother's spirit tablet in the shrine; seeing in the shrine filial daughters, she lingered long in hesitation, returned home and thereupon cut her own throat.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother died she arranged the funeral, petitioned for an official commendation of her mother's virtue, and installed her mother's spirit tablet in the shrine of chaste women. There she saw the tablets of other filial daughters. She lingered a long while, went home, and cut her throat.

sentences.zh: 遺書告文甲曰：「君家孝娥以身殉父，兒愚祗知有母，深負舅姑慈，原更得賢婦奉饔飧也。

translations.literal: She left a letter telling Wenjia: "In your household the filial daughter died for her father; I in my folly know only my mother, and deeply fail the kindness of parents-in-law; I pray you may find again a worthy wife to serve the meals."
translations.idiomatic: She left a letter for Wenjia: "Your house has its filial daughter who gave her life for her father. I, foolish girl that I am, knew only my mother and have failed your parents' kindness. I pray you find a worthy wife to keep your hearth."

sentences.zh: 杜仲梅女末姑，安徽太平人。

translations.literal: Du Zhongmei's daughter Mozhu, a native of Taiping in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhu, daughter of Du Zhongmei, from Taiping in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 賊至，刃其母，抱持乞代，刃及，終不釋。

translations.literal: When bandits came they slashed her mother; she embraced and held her begging to take her place; blades struck; she would not release until the end.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came they slashed at her mother. She threw her arms around her and begged them to take her instead. The blades cut her; she would not let go.

sentences.zh: 賊去，母創死，女抱母屍泣，達旦，尋毀卒。

translations.literal: The bandits left; her mother died of her wounds; the girl held her mother's corpse weeping until dawn, and soon thereafter died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits left. Her mother died of her wounds. The girl held the body and wept until dawn, then died of grief herself.

sentences.zh: 同時二方氏女，一年十四，一方九歲，皆代母死。

translations.literal: At the same time two daughters of the Fang clan, one fourteen, one nine, both died in place of their mothers.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time two daughters of the Fang clan—one fourteen, one nine—also died in their mothers' stead.

sentences.zh: 又有劉可求女，亦太平人。

translations.literal: There was also the daughter of Liu Keqiu, also of Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the daughter of Liu Keqiu, likewise of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 弟被掠，女請於父易弟歸，即夕自殺。

translations.literal: Her younger brother was seized; the girl requested of her father to exchange the brother's return for herself; that very night she killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother was taken captive. She asked her father to ransom the boy by surrendering her in his place, and that night she killed herself.

sentences.zh: 楊泰初女徽德，孫承沂女錦宜，皆休寧人。

translations.literal: Yang Taichu's daughter Huide and Sun Chengyi's daughter Jinyi, both of Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Huide, daughter of Yang Taichu, and Jinyi, daughter of Sun Chengyi—both from Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 徽德年十二，母死寇，抱屍不食死。

translations.literal: Huide at twelve; her mother died at the hands of bandits; she embraced the corpse and refused food until she died.
translations.idiomatic: Huide was twelve when bandits killed her mother. She clung to the body, refused all food, and starved to death.

sentences.zh: 錦宜七歲，寇殺其祖母，守屍側五日，賊與食，卻之，餓死。

translations.literal: Jinyi at seven; bandits killed her grandmother; she guarded the corpse's side for five days; when bandits offered food she refused and starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyi was seven when bandits killed her grandmother. She kept vigil beside the corpse for five days. When the bandits offered her food she refused it and died of hunger.

sentences.zh: 趙承穀聘妻丁，名畹芬，武進人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chenggu's betrothed Ding, named Wanfen, a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wanfen of Wujin was betrothed to Zhao Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 父士衍，官蠡縣知縣，母趙及畹芬從。

translations.literal: Her father Shiyan served as magistrate of Li County; mother Zhao and Wanfen followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shiyan was magistrate of Li County; her mother, née Zhao, and Wanfen accompanied him to his post.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，洪秀全兵破常州，承穀大父起殉焉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng Hong Xiuquan's army broke Changzhou; Chenggu's great-grandfather Qi died a martyr.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), the armies of Hong Xiuquan took Changzhou. Chenggu's great-grandfather Qi died defending the city.

sentences.zh: 或傳承穀亦見執，母感傷發病卒。

translations.literal: Some reported Chenggu was also taken captive; the mother died of grief and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor spread that Chenggu too had been captured. His mother fell ill with grief and died.

sentences.zh: 明年二月壬子夕，畹芬自經死。

translations.literal: On the evening of renzi in the second month of the following year Wanfen hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: On the evening of the renzi day in the second month of the following year, Wanfen hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 將死，書所為思親賦及詞六篇，字畫端靜如平時。

translations.literal: Before dying she wrote her "Rhapsody on Longing for Kin" and six lyrics; the characters and strokes were composed and quiet as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Before she died she wrote out her "Rhapsody on Longing for Kin" and six song lyrics. The hand was as steady and graceful as on any ordinary day.

sentences.zh: 彭爵麒女，名詠春，懷寧人；

translations.literal: Peng Jueqi's daughter, named Yongchun, a native of Huaining;
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun, daughter of Peng Jueqi, of Huaining;

sentences.zh: 陳寶廉二女慧莊、慧敬，侯官人：皆殉母。

translations.literal: Chen Baolian's two daughters Huizhuang and Huijing, of Houguan: all died for their mothers.
translations.idiomatic: and Huizhuang and Huijing, daughters of Chen Baolian, of Houguan—all died with their mothers.

sentences.zh: 詠春哭母殯僧寺，登浮屠自投死。

translations.literal: Yongchun weeping at her mother's coffin at a Buddhist temple climbed a pagoda and threw herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun wept beside her mother's coffin in a Buddhist temple, climbed the pagoda, and cast herself down to her death.

sentences.zh: 慧敬請以身代母，慧莊居母喪，皆仰藥死。

translations.literal: Huijing asked to take her mother's place in death; Huizhuang observed mourning for her mother; both took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing offered her own life in her mother's stead; Huizhuang kept mourning at her mother's side. Both took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 吳士仁女，獻縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Shiren's daughter, a native of Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Wu Shiren, of Xian County.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，無兄弟，誓不嫁養母。

translations.literal: Her father died in childhood; she had no brothers; she vowed not to marry and nourished her mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her father died when she was young. She had no brothers. She vowed never to marry and devoted herself to supporting her mother.

sentences.zh: 會寇至，女求利刃置袖中，扶母出避，遇二寇，擠母僕，母怒詈，寇持刃欲斫，女急呼曰：「毋殺我母！

translations.literal: When bandits came the girl sought a sharp blade and placed it in her sleeve; she supported her mother to flee; they met two bandits who pushed her mother down; her mother cursed in anger; a bandit raised a blade to chop; the girl cried urgently: "Do not kill my mother!"
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came she secured a sharp blade and hid it in her sleeve, then helped her mother flee. They met two raiders who knocked her mother down. Her mother cursed them. One raised his blade to strike. The girl cried out, "Do not kill my mother!"

sentences.zh: 我從若，不則死。

translations.literal: "I will follow you; otherwise I die."
translations.idiomatic: "I will go with you—or I die here."

sentences.zh: 」寇乃止。

translations.literal: The bandits then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits held their blades.

sentences.zh: 扶母還其家，藏母於室，出問寇飢否？

translations.literal: She supported her mother back home, hid her mother in a room, went out and asked the bandits whether they were hungry.
translations.idiomatic: She led her mother home, hid her in an inner room, and went out to ask whether the bandits were hungry.

sentences.zh: 具食使食。

translations.literal: She prepared food and made them eat.
translations.idiomatic: She set out food and made them eat.

sentences.zh: 食畢，一方飲，一出臥他室中，女躡飲者後，挾刃刺其頸，貫喉，嘶而僕。

translations.literal: When they had finished eating, one drank while another went to lie in another room; the girl crept behind the drinker and stabbed his neck with a blade, piercing the throat; he hissed and fell.
translations.idiomatic: When they had eaten, one drank wine while the other lay down in another room. The girl stole up behind the drinker and drove her blade through his neck and throat. He gurgled and fell.

sentences.zh: 女陽為嬉笑，拔所佩刀至他室，臥者方起立，遽前剚其胸，亦死，乃負母出走。

translations.literal: The girl pretended laughter; she drew the knife at her waist and went to the other room; the one lying down had just risen when she suddenly came forward and stabbed his chest—he too died; then she carried her mother on her back and fled.
translations.idiomatic: She laughed as if at ease, drew the knife at her belt, and went to the other room. The second man was just rising when she lunged and stabbed him through the chest. He too died. Then she carried her mother on her back and fled.

sentences.zh: 王濟源女，棗強人。

translations.literal: Wang Jiyuan's daughter, a native of Zaoqiang.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Wang Jiyuan, of Zaoqiang.

sentences.zh: 幼即能事父母。

translations.literal: From childhood she could serve her parents well.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she knew how to serve her parents.

sentences.zh: 寡兄弟，遂矢不嫁。

translations.literal: With few brothers she then swore never to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers were few; she swore never to marry.

sentences.zh: 嘗有盜，夜破門入，女持火槍立暗陬，擊一盜斃，盜乃去。

translations.literal: Once there were thieves; at night they broke the door; the girl stood in a dark nook holding a fire-lance, struck one thief dead, and the thieves left.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when thieves broke in at night, she stood in the dark with a fire-lance, killed one of them, and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 喪父母，葬祭皆如禮，為立後。

translations.literal: When her parents died burial and sacrifice were all according to rite; she established an heir.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents died she buried and mourned them according to every rite and adopted an heir for the family line.

sentences.zh: 同治間，寇至，負父母木主行避寇。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi years when bandits came she carried her parents' spirit tablets on her back fleeing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi era, when bandits came, she fled with her parents' spirit tablets strapped to her back.

sentences.zh: 逾六十，父母忌日，歲時祭墓，猶號泣哽咽。

translations.literal: Past sixty, on her parents' death anniversaries she still went yearly to sacrifice at the tomb, weeping and choking with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty, on her parents' death anniversaries she still went to their graves each year, weeping until she could not speak.

sentences.zh: 董桂林女，樂亭人。

translations.literal: Dong Guilin's daughter, a native of Leting.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Dong Guilin, of Leting.

sentences.zh: 桂林卒，女十二，矢不嫁，耕織以養母。

translations.literal: Guilin died; the girl was twelve; she swore not to marry; she farmed and wove to nourish her mother.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin died when she was twelve. She swore never to marry, farmed and wove, and supported her mother.

sentences.zh: 昌黎富家子，聞其賢，請婚，原代之養，女堅拒不許。

translations.literal: A wealthy son of Changli, hearing of her virtue, asked for marriage, offering to nourish her mother in her place; the girl steadfastly refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: A rich young man of Changli, hearing of her virtue, asked for her hand and offered to support her mother in her stead. She refused him firmly.

sentences.zh: 母卒，女五十餘矣，鬻田以為斂，存屋數椽，田一畝，杏五樹，女即牖外置母棺，手畚土以封。

translations.literal: When her mother died the girl was already past fifty; she sold fields for the encoffining; she kept several rafters of house, one mu of field, five apricot trees; she placed her mother's coffin outside the window, and with her own hands filled with a basket scooped earth to seal it.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother died she was past fifty. She sold her fields to pay for the funeral, keeping only a few roof-beams of house, one mu of land, and five apricot trees. She set her mother's coffin outside her window and sealed the mound herself, basket by basket of earth.

sentences.zh: 獨處，晝夜懸刀自衛。

translations.literal: Living alone day and night she hung a knife for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: She lived alone and kept a knife hung at her side day and night.

sentences.zh: 又十餘年，鄰里高其義，醵金為營葬。

translations.literal: After more than ten years the neighbors honored her righteousness and collected money to provide burial.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later the neighbors, honoring her devotion, pooled money to give her mother a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 耿恂女，名一圭，望都人。

translations.literal: Geng Xun's daughter, named Yigui, a native of Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui, daughter of Geng Xun, of Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 恂舉人，無子，客授保定。

translations.literal: Xun was a provincial graduate; he had no son; he taught as a guest lecturer in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was a provincial graduate with no son. He earned his living teaching in Baoding as a guest lecturer.

sentences.zh: 母劉病痺，一圭按摩抑搔，嘗六七晝夜不少休。

translations.literal: Mother Liu suffered paralysis; Yigui massaged, pressed, and scratched; sometimes six or seven days and nights without a break.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Liu was paralyzed. Yigui rubbed, pressed, and scratched her limbs, sometimes six or seven days and nights without rest.

sentences.zh: 母少間，因臥床下，恂自外至，誤踐其手，指甲脫，血流至肘，倦不自知也。

translations.literal: When her mother had a brief respite she would lie beneath the bed; Xun came from outside, accidentally stepped on her hand; a fingernail came off, blood flowed to the elbow; worn out she was unaware.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother slept she lay under the bed within reach. Once Xun came in from outside and stepped on her hand by mistake. A nail tore off and blood ran to her elbow; exhausted, she did not even feel it.

sentences.zh: 嘗議婚某氏子，未聘而某氏子夭，女聞泣曰：「我得終事父母矣！

translations.literal: Once marriage to a certain family's son was discussed; before betrothal that family's son died young; the girl heard and wept saying: "I can serve my parents to the end!"
translations.idiomatic: Marriage to a certain family's son had been discussed, but before betrothal the young man died. When she heard, she wept and said, "Now I can serve my parents to the end of their days!"

sentences.zh: 」遂矢不字。

translations.literal: Then she swore never to accept a betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: She swore never to accept another betrothal.

sentences.zh: 劉病垂二十年，哽噎不能食，食必女口哺。

translations.literal: Liu's illness lasted nearly twenty years; she choked and could not eat; whenever she ate it had to be fed from the girl's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Liu's illness lasted nearly twenty years. She could not swallow; whenever she ate, Yigui fed her from her own mouth.

sentences.zh: 恂卒，持喪奉病母歸里。

translations.literal: Xun died; she observed mourning and supported her ailing mother returning home.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun died she observed mourning, took her ailing mother home, and cared for her there.

sentences.zh: 逾年，劉亦卒，一圭營喪葬，自為文以表於阡。

translations.literal: After a year Liu also died; Yigui arranged funeral and burial and composed a text herself to set up as an inscription at the graveside.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Liu died as well. Yigui arranged the funeral and wrote the epitaph herself to set up at the graveside.

sentences.zh: 一圭嘗以生日上塚，掬土以益墓，憊僕墓側，家人掖以歸，數日卒。

translations.literal: Once on her birthday Yigui went up to the tomb, scooped earth to add to the mound; exhausted she collapsed beside the tomb; family helped her home; several days later she died.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on her birthday, she went to the tomb and scooped earth to mend the mound. She collapsed beside the grave from exhaustion. Her family helped her home; she died a few days later.

sentences.zh: 吳芬女，開縣人，女次第二。

translations.literal: Wu Fen's daughter, a native of Kai County, the second daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The second daughter of Wu Fen, of Kai County.

sentences.zh: 芬，光緒二十三年拔貢生，以知縣發山東，女留侍母。

translations.literal: Fen in the twenty-third year of Guangxu was a selected tribute student, sent out as magistrate to Shandong; the daughter remained to attend her mother.
translations.idiomatic: Fen, selected as a tribute student in the twenty-third year of Guangxu (1897), was appointed magistrate and sent to Shandong. His daughter stayed behind to wait on her mother.

sentences.zh: 芬病，女聞，夜輒焚香露禱。

translations.literal: When Fen fell ill the daughter heard and each night burned incense and prayed in the open dew.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard her father was ill, she burned incense each night and prayed under the open sky.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，芬卒，女聞大悲，且恚曰：「人謂天有眼，我夜焚香露禱，叩頭至數百，乃漠然不一顧耶？

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Fen died; the daughter heard and grieved greatly, and said angrily: "Men say Heaven has eyes; I burned incense and prayed in the open night after night, knocking my head hundreds of times—yet it was indifferent and never once looked this way?"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year (1905) Fen died. When she heard, she grieved bitterly and cried in anger, "Men say Heaven sees. Night after night I burned incense and prayed in the dew, knocking my head hundreds of times—and Heaven never once looked my way?"

sentences.zh: 」越日飲藥死，時年十三。

translations.literal: The next day she drank poison and died; she was thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she took poison and died. She was thirteen.

sentences.zh: 邵氏二女，黟人，長名媚，十五；

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Shao clan, natives of Yi, the elder named Mei, fifteen;
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters of the Shao family, of Yi—the elder named Mei, fifteen;

sentences.zh: 次名揚，十三。

translations.literal: the younger named Yang, thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: the younger named Yang, thirteen.

sentences.zh: 從父入山樵，虎出噬其父，媚持父揮樵斧斫虎，虎負創去，父女皆不死。

translations.literal: Following their father into the hills to gather firewood, a tiger came out and seized their father; Mei held her father and swung the firewood axe to chop the tiger; the tiger fled wounded; father and daughter both did not die.
translations.idiomatic: They followed their father into the hills to cut firewood. A tiger sprang out and seized him. Mei clung to her father and swung the woodcutter's axe at the tiger. Wounded, the beast fled. Father and daughter both lived.

sentences.zh: 蔣遂良女，城步人，虎挾其母去，女奪以還。

translations.literal: Jiang Suiliang's daughter, a native of Chengbu; a tiger seized her mother and carried her off; the girl snatched her back.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Jiang Suiliang, of Chengbu—a tiger seized her mother and dragged her away. The girl fought the beast and won her mother back.

sentences.zh: 徐氏二女，淑雲、淑英，溫江人。

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Xu clan, Shuyun and Shuying, natives of Wenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters of the Xu family, Shuyun and Shuying, of Wenjiang.

sentences.zh: 父瞽，兄登雲早卒。

translations.literal: Their father was blind; elder brother Dengyun died early.
translations.idiomatic: Their father was blind. Their elder brother Dengyun had died young.

sentences.zh: 嫂凌疾革，撫子成龍而泣，淑雲、淑英在側，曰：「我二人在，當扶持以長，嫂何虞？

translations.literal: Sister-in-law Ling was critically ill; embracing her son Chenglong she wept; Shuyun and Shuying at her side said: "With us two here we shall support him to grow up—what worry need you have?"
translations.idiomatic: Their sister-in-law Ling lay dying. She held her son Chenglong and wept. Shuyun and Shuying said at her side, "While we two live we will raise him. What have you to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」時成龍方二歲，淑雲、淑英皆不嫁，以女紅事蓄，卒扶持以長。

translations.literal: Chenglong was then two; Shuyun and Shuying both did not marry; by needlework they saved; in the end they supported him to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong was then two years old. Shuyun and Shuying never married. They saved from needlework and in the end raised him to manhood.

sentences.zh: 李鴻普妻郭，禹州人。

translations.literal: Li Hongpu's wife Guo, a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, wife of Li Hongpu, of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鴻普母王，明季流賊破州，自經死，失其屍。

translations.literal: Hongpu's mother Wang—in the Ming season when wandering bandits broke the prefecture—hanged herself and her corpse was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Hongpu's mother Wang, in the closing years of the Ming when roving bandits overran the prefecture, hanged herself. Her body was never found.

sentences.zh: 鴻普將斫檀為之像，未成而卒。

translations.literal: Hongpu was about to carve a sandalwood image of her; before it was finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: Hongpu had begun to carve a sandalwood image of her, but died before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 郭力紡織，奉其舅及後姑。

translations.literal: Guo labored at spinning and weaving, supporting her father-in-law and stepmother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Guo spun and wove to support her father-in-law and stepmother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 子以達，稍長，喻以父意。

translations.literal: Son Yida, when somewhat grown, was instructed in his father's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When their son Yida grew old enough, she told him of his father's wish.

sentences.zh: 求檀，輒不中像材。

translations.literal: They sought sandalwood, but again and again none suited the image material.
translations.idiomatic: They searched for sandalwood, yet no piece proved fit for carving the statue.

sentences.zh: 郭乃刺左腕，出血盈盂，和香屑為像，复剪髮飾其首。

translations.literal: Guo then pierced her left wrist; blood filled a bowl. Mixing it with incense powder she made an image, and again cut her hair to adorn its head.
translations.idiomatic: Guo pierced her left wrist until a bowl brimmed with blood, mixed the blood with incense powder to form a statue, and cut her own hair to crown it.

sentences.zh: 以達驚，叩首泣，郭曰：「我姑以節死，我何愛發若血不以奉姑？

translations.literal: Yida was alarmed; kowtowing he wept. Guo said: "My mother-in-law died preserving her chastity—how could I cherish hair or blood and not offer them to serve Mother?"
translations.idiomatic: Yida was horrified and kowtowed, weeping. Guo said, "My mother-in-law died faithful to her vows. Why should I spare my hair or my blood when they are meant for her?"

sentences.zh: 吾無恙，汝又何悲？

translations.literal: I am unharmed—why then do you grieve?
translations.idiomatic: I am well. Why do you weep?

sentences.zh: 」像成，藏潔室，日上飲膳，事如生。

translations.literal: " When the image was complete, she stored it in a clean chamber; each day she set out food and drink, serving it as though she lived.
translations.idiomatic: When the statue was finished, she enshrined it in a clean room and every day set out meals, tending it as if her mother-in-law still lived.

sentences.zh: 其後又有牛輔世妻張，太原人。

translations.literal: Later there was also Zhang, wife of Niu Fushi, a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Zhang, wife of Niu Fushi, of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 姑卒，刻木祀之，飲食必祭。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law died, she carved wood to worship her; food and drink were always offered in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died, she carved a wooden image for her and never took a meal without first making an offering.

sentences.zh: 高位妻段，宛平人。

translations.literal: Duan, wife of Gao Wei, a native of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, wife of Gao Wei, of Wanping.

sentences.zh: 位卒，段年十七，二子幼，依其兄以居。

translations.literal: When Wei died, Duan was seventeen; her two sons were young—she relied on her elder brother for residence.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died when Duan was seventeen, leaving two small sons. She went to live with her brother.

sentences.zh: 兄勸改嫁，段不可，攜二子徙居小市板屋中。

translations.literal: Her brother urged remarriage; Duan would not consent. She took her two sons and moved to dwell in a plank house in the small market.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother urged her to remarry, but she refused and moved with her sons into a plank shack on the edge of the market town.

sentences.zh: 長子早死，次子為吏，以罪徙遼左，乃復撫諸孫。

translations.literal: The elder son died early; the second son became an official and, for a crime, was banished to the Liao east—thereupon she again raised the grandchildren.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder son died young; her younger son entered government service but was banished to the far northeast for a crime, and she took up raising her grandchildren again.

sentences.zh: 段年九十，孫裔成進士，贖其父以歸。

translations.literal: Duan was ninety; grandson Yi passed the jinshi examination and ransomed his father to return.
translations.idiomatic: Duan lived to ninety. Her grandson Yi became a jinshi and secured his father's release, bringing him home from exile.

sentences.zh: 裔母谷，事姑孝。

translations.literal: Yi's mother Gu, in serving her mother-in-law was filial.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's mother Gu was devoted in her service to her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 始處賤，躬灑掃。

translations.literal: At first in a low station, she personally swept and sprinkled.
translations.idiomatic: While they still lived in humble circumstances, she herself swept and cleaned the rooms.

sentences.zh: 晨侍盥櫛，食時，就灶下作羹，親上之。

translations.literal: In the morning she attended hand-washing and combing; at mealtime she went to the kitchen hearth to make broth and personally served it.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning she helped her wash and dress; at mealtimes she cooked at the kitchen hearth and brought the food up herself.

sentences.zh: 食畢，然後退，日以為常。

translations.literal: Only after the meal was finished did she withdraw—day by day it was her constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: She withdrew only after her mother-in-law had finished eating, and did this day after day without fail.

sentences.zh: 既貴，終不改。

translations.literal: Once they had grown eminent, she never altered it.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the family rose to prosperity, she never changed her ways.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，谷曰：「若毋言，吾與姑故寒苦，姑習我，非我供事，姑終不適。

translations.literal: Some spoke to her about it; Gu said: "Say no more. My mother-in-law and I were once cold and poor together. She accustomed me to this—had I not served her, she would never have been at ease."
translations.idiomatic: When others remarked on it, Gu said, "Say nothing. My mother-in-law and I knew poverty together. She taught me these ways—without my service she could never have been content."

sentences.zh: 吾老矣！

translations.literal: I am old now!
translations.idiomatic: I am old now!

sentences.zh: 灑掃盥饋以事我姑，此日可多得耶？

translations.literal: To sweep, sprinkle, wash, comb, and feed in serving my mother-in-law—how many more such days can one obtain?
translations.idiomatic: How many more days will I have to sweep rooms, wash her hands, and set her meals before my mother-in-law?

sentences.zh: 」康熙二十七年，段卒，年九十六。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi, Duan died, aged ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign, Duan died at ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 鄭光春妻葉，莆田人。

translations.literal: Ye, wife of Zheng Guangchun, a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, wife of Zheng Guangchun, of Putian.

sentences.zh: 光春遊湖南，久不歸，葉以紡績養姑。

translations.literal: Guangchun traveled in Hunan and long did not return; Ye with spinning and weaving supported her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchun went to Hunan and stayed away for years. Ye spun and wove to support her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 子文炳幼，或不率教，輒拊心號天，文炳懼，向學。

translations.literal: Son Wenbing was young; at times he would not follow teaching—she would beat her breast and cry to Heaven; Wenbing feared this and turned to study.
translations.idiomatic: Their son Wenbing was still a boy and sometimes unruly. She would clap her breast and cry to Heaven until Wenbing, frightened, applied himself to his books.

sentences.zh: 姑老病痺，葉負以出入。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law grew old and ill with paralysis; Ye carried her on her back to go in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law grew old and crippled with paralysis, Ye carried her on her back wherever she needed to go.

sentences.zh: 七年，姑乃卒。

translations.literal: After seven years, her mother-in-law at last died.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later her mother-in-law died.

sentences.zh: 文炳長，娶於吳，念父不歸，婚夕惘惘無歡。

translations.literal: When Wenbing grew up, he married a woman of Wu. Mindful that his father had not returned, on the wedding night he was absent-minded and joyless.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbing came of age he married a woman named Wu. His father still had not returned, and on their wedding night he was lost in grief, unable to rejoice.

sentences.zh: 吳逡巡得其故，勸文炳行求父，曰：「事姑，我任之！

translations.literal: Wu by degrees learned the reason and urged Wenbing to go travel to seek his father, saying: "Serving Mother-in-law—I take that charge!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu gradually learned why and urged him to go find his father. "Leave your mother to me," she said.

sentences.zh: 」文炳行求得父以歸，吳已卒，猶處子。

translations.literal: " Wenbing traveled and found his father and returned with him; Wu had already died, still a virgin.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing set out, found his father, and brought him home—but Wu had already died, still untouched as a bride.

sentences.zh: 文炳子任仁，婦張，能繩其孝。

translations.literal: Wenbing's son Renren; wife Zhang—able to continue her filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing's son Renren married Zhang, who carried on Wu's devotion to the family.

sentences.zh: 屈崇山妻劉，鄠縣人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Qu Chongshan, a native of Huxian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Qu Chongshan, of Huxian.

sentences.zh: 崇山卒，劉奉姑以居。

translations.literal: When Chongshan died, Liu supported her mother-in-law and lived with her.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongshan died, Liu lived with and cared for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十年，歲兇，姑勸之嫁，不從。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Kangxi there was a famine year; Mother-in-law urged her to remarry—she would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of the Kangxi reign famine struck. Her mother-in-law urged her to remarry, but she refused.

sentences.zh: 飢益甚，姑泣語劉曰：「我旦暮且死，盍自鬻，尚可活我！

translations.literal: Hunger grew yet worse. Mother-in-law weeping spoke to Liu: "I am soon to die morning or evening—why not sell yourself? You could still keep me alive!"
translations.idiomatic: Famine deepened. Her mother-in-law wept and said to Liu, "I will not live much longer. Sell yourself—you could still save my life."

sentences.zh: 」劉泣不應。

translations.literal: " Liu wept and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu wept and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 姑大慟曰：「死耳，夫何言！

translations.literal: Mother-in-law greatly mourned and said: "Death—that is all. What more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law cried out in anguish, "Death is all that awaits us. What is there left to say?"

sentences.zh: 」劉哽咽久之，乃曰：「如姑命。

translations.literal: " Liu sobbed for a long while, then said: "As Mother commands."
translations.idiomatic: Liu choked back tears for a long time, then said, "I will do as you say."

sentences.zh: 」自鬻於豪家，得金畀姑，號泣登車去。

translations.literal: " She sold herself to a powerful household, obtained gold and gave it to Mother-in-law, wailing as she mounted the carriage to depart.
translations.idiomatic: She sold herself to a wealthy family, gave the money to her mother-in-law, and left wailing in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 豪家方具酒食為賀，劉入廁自經死。

translations.literal: The powerful household was just preparing wine and food to celebrate; Liu entered the privy and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: The household was preparing a feast to celebrate when Liu slipped into the privy and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 豪家大恨，以敝藁裹屍棄野外。

translations.literal: The powerful household was greatly resentful; wrapping the corpse in worn straw matting they cast it out in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the family wrapped her body in tattered matting and cast it out beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 謝以炳妻路，仲秀妻鄭，季純妻吳，湖口人。

translations.literal: Lu, wife of Xie Yibing; Zheng, wife of Zhongxiu; Wu, wife of Jichun—all natives of Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, wife of Xie Yibing; Zheng, wife of Zhongxiu; and Wu, wife of Jichun—all of Hukou.

sentences.zh: 以炳兄弟並早卒，三婦勵節事姑，姑病癰，迭吮之，良愈。

translations.literal: Yibing's brothers all died early; the three daughters-in-law encouraged chastity in serving Mother-in-law. When she had a carbuncle, they took turns sucking it, and she was completely cured.
translations.idiomatic: Yibing's brothers had all died young. The three daughters-in-law upheld their vows and cared for their mother-in-law. When she developed a festering sore, they took turns drawing out the poison with their mouths until she recovered.

sentences.zh: 王鉅妻施，鉅，蕭山人；

translations.literal: Shi, wife of Wang Ju; Ju, a native of Xiaoshan;
translations.idiomatic: Shi, wife of Wang Ju. Ju was from Xiaoshan;

sentences.zh: 施，富陽人。

translations.literal: Shi, a native of Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was from Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 姑嚴，小不當意，輒呵斥，施屏息不敢聲。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law was stern; the least displeasure and she would scold—Shi held her breath and dared not make a sound.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was severe and scolded her at the slightest fault. Shi held her breath and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 姑病反胃甚，醫以為不治，施刲股和藥進，病良已，姑遇施如故。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law was gravely ill with vomiting; physicians deemed it incurable. Shi cut her thigh flesh and mixed it with medicine to present; the illness was completely cured—yet Mother-in-law treated Shi as before.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell gravely ill with vomiting and the doctors gave up hope, Shi cut flesh from her thigh, mixed it into medicine, and fed it to her. The illness passed—but her mother-in-law treated her no better than before.

sentences.zh: 鉅疾作，施視疾憊，病瘵卒，姑猶不善施。

translations.literal: Ju fell ill; Shi attended the illness until exhausted, contracted consumption and died—Mother-in-law still did not treat Shi kindly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju fell ill, Shi nursed him until she was worn out, then herself sickened with consumption and died. Her mother-in-law still showed her no kindness.

sentences.zh: 鉅以刲股事告，視其屍，信，乃大慟曰：「吾負孝婦！

translations.literal: Ju told of the cut-thigh affair; viewing her corpse he believed it, then greatly mourned: "I have wronged a filial wife!"
translations.idiomatic: Ju told her about the thigh-cutting. Seeing the wound on her body, he believed it and cried out in anguish, "I have wronged a devoted wife!"

sentences.zh: 」及疾篤，出珠花付鉅曰：「汝婦孝，以此志吾痛，使汝子孫勿忘。

translations.literal: " When her illness grew critical, she brought out pearl flowers and gave them to Ju, saying: "Your wife was filial—take these to record my pain, and let your descendants not forget."
translations.idiomatic: When her own illness turned grave, she took out pearl hair ornaments and gave them to Ju. "Your wife was devoted," she said. "Keep these in memory of my grief, and let your descendants never forget."

sentences.zh: 」蕭山人因稱鉅後為珠花王氏。

translations.literal: " The people of Xiaoshan therefore called Ju's descendants the Pearl-Flower Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiaoshan thereafter called Ju's line the Pearl-Flower Wang family.

sentences.zh: 陳文世妻劉，鄖人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Chen Wenshi, a native of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Chen Wenshi, of Yun.

sentences.zh: 陳、劉皆農家，劉待年於陳。

translations.literal: Chen and Liu were both farming families; Liu waited the years at Chen's home before marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Chen and Liu families were farmers. Liu had been betrothed to Chen as a child and lived in his household awaiting the wedding.

sentences.zh: 既婚，姑年七十二，病噎，劉割臂和藥以進，疾少間；

translations.literal: After marriage, Mother-in-law was seventy-two, ill with choking; Liu cut her arm and mixed it with medicine to present—the illness eased somewhat;
translations.idiomatic: After they wed, her seventy-two-year-old mother-in-law fell ill with choking sickness. Liu cut her arm, mixed the blood into medicine, and fed it to her. The illness eased for a time;

sentences.zh: 既而復作，不食已十日，垂盡矣。

translations.literal: then it returned; she had not eaten for ten days and was near the end.
translations.idiomatic: then returned. She had eaten nothing for ten days and was near death.

sentences.zh: 劉夜屏人，殺雞誓於神，持小刀自劙其胸二寸許，出肝刲半，取布束創，以肝與雞同瀹湯奉姑。

translations.literal: Liu at night sent people away, killed a chicken and swore to the spirits, took a small knife and cut open her own chest about two inches, took out the liver and sliced half, took cloth to bind the wound, and boiled the liver with the chicken in broth to present to Mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: That night Liu sent everyone away, slaughtered a chicken, and vowed to the gods. With a small knife she cut open her chest nearly two inches, took out her liver and sliced off half, bound the wound with cloth, and boiled the liver with the chicken into a broth for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑久不言，忽曰：「湯香甚！

translations.literal: Mother-in-law long did not speak, then suddenly said: "The broth is very fragrant!"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law had been silent for a long while, then suddenly said, "How fragrant this broth is!"

sentences.zh: 」飲之竟，病良愈，劉亦旋平。

translations.literal: " She drank it to the end; the illness was completely cured, and Liu also soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: She drank it all. The illness lifted completely, and Liu soon healed as well.

sentences.zh: 為乾隆四十四年夏六月事。

translations.literal: This was an affair of the sixth month of summer in the forty-fourth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the sixth month of summer in the forty-fourth year of the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 知縣嘉興李集出俸為買田宅，宅北有大陂，幾三頃，因命曰孝婦陂。

translations.literal: Magistrate Li Ji of Jiaxing contributed his salary to buy fields and a residence; north of the residence was a great pond of nearly three qing—therefore it was named Filial Wife Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Ji of Jiaxing used his own salary to buy fields and a house for her. North of the house lay a great pond of nearly three qing, which he named Filial Wife Pond.

sentences.zh: 張守仁妻梁，獻縣人。

translations.literal: Liang, wife of Zhang Shouren, a native of Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, wife of Zhang Shouren, of Xian County.

sentences.zh: 守仁卒，祖姑穆，耄而瞽且痿，日偃仰床蓐，梁傭力以養。
