translations.literal: When Shouren died, great-grandmother-in-law Mu, in extreme old age, was blind and paralyzed, day by day lying on bed mats—Liang hired out her labor to support her.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouren died, his great-grandmother Mu was very old, blind, and paralyzed, confined day and night to her bed. Liang hired herself out as a laborer to support her.

sentences.zh: 或諷梁嫁，梁曰：「我今日嫁，明日祖姑飢且死，義不忍。

translations.literal: Some urged Liang to remarry; Liang said: "If I marry today, tomorrow Great-grandmother will starve and die—I cannot bear it by right."
translations.idiomatic: When others urged her to remarry, Liang said, "If I wed today, my great-grandmother-in-law will starve tomorrow. I cannot bring myself to do it."

sentences.zh: 」祖姑善恚，小不當意，則怒詈，或攫其面，血出，梁事之自若。

translations.literal: " Great-grandmother was prone to anger; the least displeasure and she would rage and revile, sometimes clawing her face until blood came forth—Liang served her as before.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was quick to anger. At the slightest fault she would rage and curse, sometimes clawing Liang's face until it bled. Liang served her without change.

sentences.zh: 祖姑卒，依其女以終。

translations.literal: When Great-grandmother died, she relied on her daughter to see out her days.
translations.idiomatic: After Mu died, Liang went to live with her daughter until the end of her life.

sentences.zh: 縣又有韓守立妻俞，祖姑及姑皆瞽，或妄言割肉以燃燈可愈，守立原試之，俞請代，刲右股燃之，盡十餘日，祖姑目復明。

translations.literal: In the county there was also Yu, wife of Han Shouli; great-grandmother-in-law and mother-in-law were both blind. Some falsely said cutting flesh to burn as lamp oil could cure it—Shouli wished to try; Yu asked to take her place, cut her right thigh and burned it. After more than ten days, Great-grandmother's eyes saw again.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county was Yu, wife of Han Shouli. Both his great-grandmother and mother were blind. Someone claimed that cutting flesh to fuel a lamp could restore sight. Shouli meant to try it himself, but Yu insisted on taking his place, cut flesh from her right thigh, and burned it. After more than ten days his great-grandmother's eyes could see again.

sentences.zh: 路和生妻吳，靖遠人。

translations.literal: Wu, wife of Lu Hesheng, a native of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of Lu Hesheng, of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 善事姑。

translations.literal: She was good at serving her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She was devoted in her care for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑喪明，吳侍左右，非整衣不入。

translations.literal: When Mother-in-law lost her sight, Wu attended at her side; unless properly dressed she would not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law went blind, Wu stayed at her side and would not enter her presence unless fully dressed.

sentences.zh: 或言姑無見也，吳曰：「吾心自不可欺耳。

translations.literal: Someone said Mother-in-law cannot see; Wu said: "My own heart—I cannot deceive it."
translations.idiomatic: When someone said her mother-in-law could not see, Wu replied, "My own heart is not something I can deceive."

sentences.zh: 諸君祿妻唐，零陵人。

translations.literal: Tang, wife of Zhu Junlu, a native of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, wife of Zhu Junlu, of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 姑胡，老無齒，兼病痺，唐日操作畢，輒跪而乳之。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law Hu, old and toothless, also ill with paralysis—each day when Tang finished her work she would kneel and nurse her.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law Hu was old and toothless and crippled with paralysis. Each day after her chores Tang would kneel and nurse her from her own breast.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「坐可也。

translations.literal: Someone said: "You may sit."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "You could sit to do that."

sentences.zh: 」唐曰：「是乳小兒也，乳姑不可。

translations.literal: " Tang said: "That is nursing a small child—nursing Mother-in-law, one may not."
translations.idiomatic: Tang replied, "One sits to nurse a child. One does not sit to nurse a mother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 牛允度妻張，通渭人。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Niu Yundu, a native of Tongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Niu Yundu, of Tongwei.

sentences.zh: 三十而寡，奉姑謹。

translations.literal: Widowed at thirty, she supported her mother-in-law with care.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed at thirty, she cared for her mother-in-law with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年，大祲，求野菜以食。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing there was a great famine; they sought wild vegetables to eat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign a great famine struck, and they lived on wild greens gathered from the fields.

sentences.zh: 姑老病，久之，不能復食。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law was old and ill; after a long while she could no longer eat.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was old and sick. In time she could no longer keep food down.

sentences.zh: 張貸錢得市脯進姑。

translations.literal: Zhang borrowed money, obtained dried meat at market, and presented it to Mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang borrowed money and bought dried meat at market for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 又久之，貸不繼，姑病欲絕，張慰之曰：「姑稍待，婦制草笠，可得錢數十，猶足為數日供也。

translations.literal: After yet more time, borrowing could not continue; Mother-in-law's illness was near the end. Zhang comforted her: "Mother, wait a little—I am making straw hats; I can get several tens in cash, still enough for several days' provision."
translations.idiomatic: Before long she could borrow no more. Her mother-in-law was failing fast. Zhang comforted her, "Wait a little longer. I am weaving straw hats—I can earn a few dozen cash, enough to feed you for several days yet."

sentences.zh: 」笠成，賣得錢，姑已死。

translations.literal: " When the hats were finished and sold for money, Mother-in-law had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When the hats were done and sold, her mother-in-law was already dead.

sentences.zh: 乃求市脯祭，朝夕哭，以馂餘活夫弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon she sought dried meat at market for sacrifice, wept morning and evening, and with leftover offerings from the feast sustained her husband's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: She bought dried meat for the funeral offerings and wept morning and night. With what remained from the sacrificial food she kept her husband's younger brother alive.

sentences.zh: 遊應標妻蕭，新都人。

translations.literal: Xiao, wife of You Yingbiao, a native of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, wife of You Yingbiao, of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 應標出耘，蕭居績。

translations.literal: Yingbiao went out to hoe; Xiao stayed home spinning.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingbiao was out in the fields, Xiao stayed home at her loom.

sentences.zh: 火發翁室，翁老病不能行，蕭冒火入，負翁，將及門，門焚，俱死。

translations.literal: Fire broke out in the old man's room; the old man was aged and ill and could not walk—Xiao braved the fire to enter, carried the old man on her back, was about to reach the door when the door burned—both died.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in her father-in-law's room. He was old and sick and could not walk. Xiao rushed into the flames, lifted him on her back, and had nearly reached the door when it collapsed in fire. Both perished.

sentences.zh: 蔣廣居妻伍，桐城人。

translations.literal: Wu, wife of Jiang Guangju, a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of Jiang Guangju, of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 寡，奉姑徐。

translations.literal: Widowed, she supported Mother-in-law Xu.
translations.idiomatic: A widow, she cared for her mother-in-law Xu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十四年，火作，徐年九十六矣，臥不能起。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing fire broke out; Xu was ninety-six, lying down and unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the Jiaqing reign fire broke out. Xu was ninety-six and bedridden.

sentences.zh: 伍自火中奔赴，負徐至灶前，火逼，俱死。

translations.literal: Wu rushed from within the fire, carried Xu to before the stove; the fire pressed close—both died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu ran into the blaze, carried Xu to the kitchen hearth, and was overtaken by the flames. Both died.

sentences.zh: 伍屍倚牆，背負徐，俱僵立不僕，面如生。

translations.literal: Wu's corpse leaned against the wall, on her back carrying Xu—both rigid, standing without falling, faces as in life.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's body was found leaning against a wall with Xu on her back. Both stood rigid, neither fallen, their faces serene as in life.

sentences.zh: 又有扶溝蔣有廣妻陳，救翁；

translations.literal: There was also Chen, wife of Jiang Youguang of Fugou, who rescued her father-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chen, wife of Jiang Youguang of Fugou, who died saving her father-in-law;

sentences.zh: 洧川閻惠妻李，救姑：皆火死。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Yan Hui of Weichuan, who rescued her mother-in-law—all died by fire.
translations.idiomatic: and Li, wife of Yan Hui of Weichuan, who died saving her mother-in-law—all perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 週學臣妻柳，湖口人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Zhou Xuechen, a native of Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, wife of Zhou Xuechen, of Hukou.

sentences.zh: 早寡。

translations.literal: Widowed early.
translations.idiomatic: She was widowed young.

sentences.zh: 夜，虎突門，翁出視，驚僕。

translations.literal: At night a tiger burst through the gate; the old man went out to look and, startled, fell prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: One night a tiger burst through the gate. Her father-in-law went out to look and collapsed in fright.

sentences.zh: 柳徒手擊虎，虎自去。

translations.literal: Liu with bare hands struck the tiger; the tiger of itself departed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu beat the tiger with her bare hands until it fled.

sentences.zh: 王德駿妻盛，益陽人。

translations.literal: Sheng, wife of Wang Dejun, a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, wife of Wang Dejun, of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 事祖姑孝，病噎，哺以乳。

translations.literal: In serving her great-grandmother-in-law she was filial; when she was ill with choking, she nursed her with her milk.
translations.idiomatic: She was devoted to her great-grandmother-in-law. When the old woman fell ill with choking sickness, Sheng nursed her from her own breast.

sentences.zh: 寇掠縣，負姑夜遁，墮虎穴，禱於虎，虎不咥。

translations.literal: When bandits raided the county, she carried Mother-in-law on her back to flee by night, fell into a tiger's den, prayed to the tiger—the tiger did not bite.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders overran the county she fled by night with her mother-in-law on her back, fell into a tiger's lair, and prayed to the beast. It did not harm them.

sentences.zh: 張茂信妻方，茂信，河津人；

translations.literal: Fang, wife of Zhang Maoxin; Maoxin, a native of Hejin;
translations.idiomatic: Fang, wife of Zhang Maoxin. Maoxin was from Hejin;

sentences.zh: 方儀徵人。

translations.literal: Fang, a native of Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was from Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 方嘗割股愈舅疾，舅與茂信皆卒，奉姑劉。

translations.literal: Fang had once cut thigh flesh to cure her uncle's illness; uncle and Maoxin both died—she supported Mother-in-law Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had once cut flesh from her thigh to cure her uncle's illness. After both uncle and husband died, she cared for her mother-in-law Liu.

sentences.zh: 姑嚴，方事之謹。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law was stern; Fang served her with care.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was severe, and Fang served her with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 當夏，姑病暴下，方躬滌茵席，不以為穢。

translations.literal: In summer Mother-in-law was gravely ill with dysentery; Fang personally washed bedding and mats, not deeming it filth.
translations.idiomatic: One summer her mother-in-law fell gravely ill with dysentery. Fang washed the bedding herself and thought nothing of the filth.

sentences.zh: 夜與姑共枕寢，微呻輒起，撫摩抑搔五十餘日，姑愈，亟稱其孝。

translations.literal: At night she shared a pillow with Mother-in-law; at the slightest groan she rose to stroke, massage, and scratch—for more than fifty days until Mother-in-law recovered, when she eagerly praised her filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: She slept beside her mother-in-law at night, rising at the slightest groan to stroke and massage her. After more than fifty days the old woman recovered and praised her devotion without end.

sentences.zh: 林經妻陳，連江人，姑盲性卞，常臆婦藐己，陳斷三指自明，姑為之悔。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of Lin Jing, of Lianjiang—Mother-in-law was blind and irascible, often suspecting the daughter-in-law looked down on her; Chen severed three fingers to prove her sincerity, and Mother-in-law repented.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of Lin Jing, of Lianjiang, had a blind and irascible mother-in-law who constantly suspected her daughter-in-law despised her. Chen cut off three fingers to prove her loyalty, and her mother-in-law repented.

sentences.zh: 經病，刲股；

translations.literal: When Jing fell ill, she cut her thigh flesh;
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell ill, she cut flesh from her thigh;

sentences.zh: 經卒，以節終。

translations.literal: Jing died; she preserved her chastity to the end.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing died, she remained a widow to the end of her days.

sentences.zh: 張德鄰妻李，遷安人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Zhang Delin, a native of Qian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li, wife of Zhang Delin, of Qian'an.

sentences.zh: 寡，從弟欲奪其志，力拒。

translations.literal: Widowed, her cousin wished to break her resolve—she forcefully refused.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed, she was pressed by a cousin to remarry and refused with all her strength.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，驅驢鬻石灰易米以養姑。

translations.literal: In a famine year she drove a donkey to sell lime for rice to support Mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine she drove a donkey to sell lime for rice to feed her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 一日遇盜，泣曰：「驢可將去，丐留囊中物俾我姑，不即餓死！

translations.literal: One day she met bandits and wept: "Take the donkey, but I beg you leave what is in the bag for my mother-in-law—she will starve at once otherwise!"
translations.idiomatic: One day she met bandits and wept, "Take the donkey, but leave what is in the bag for my mother-in-law—without it she will starve at once!"

sentences.zh: 」盜舍之去。

translations.literal: " The bandits let her go.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits let her go.

sentences.zh: 武烈妻趙，烈，永年人；

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of Wu Lie; Lie, a native of Yongnian;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of Wu Lie. Lie was from Yongnian;

sentences.zh: 趙，宣化人。

translations.literal: Zhao, a native of Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was from Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 趙事姑孝，姑病，夜露禱，得寒嗽疾。

translations.literal: Zhao served Mother-in-law filially; when she fell ill Zhao prayed outdoors by night and contracted a chill cough.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was devoted to her mother-in-law. When the old woman fell ill, Zhao prayed outdoors through the night and caught a chill that left her coughing.

sentences.zh: 烈病疫，或謂口吮胸，汗出則愈，而吮者當病，趙曰：「果爾，死不恤。

translations.literal: Lie fell ill with plague; some said sucking the chest until sweat came would cure it, but the one who sucked would fall ill—Zhao said: "If it is so, I do not care if I die."
translations.idiomatic: Lie contracted plague. Some said sucking the pus from his chest until he sweated would cure him—but the one who sucked would fall ill. Zhao said, "If that is so, I do not care if I die."

sentences.zh: 」卒吮之，烈竟卒，趙病幾殆。

translations.literal: " She sucked at last; Lie died nevertheless, and Zhao nearly died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: She did as they said. Lie died anyway, and Zhao herself nearly died of the illness.

sentences.zh: 貧，操作紡績，諸子成進士，自奉恆觳。

translations.literal: Poor, she worked spinning and weaving; her sons all became jinshi; she herself was always sparing in provision.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, she spun and wove. All her sons became jinshi, yet she lived always in frugal restraint.

sentences.zh: 親族有緩急，往往傾其貲。

translations.literal: When kin had urgent need she often poured out her whole fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When kin fell on hard times she often gave away everything she had.

sentences.zh: 出千金置義學，卒，遂祠焉。

translations.literal: She gave a thousand in gold to establish a charitable school; when she died, she was enshrined there.
translations.idiomatic: She gave a thousand taels of gold to found a charity school. When she died, she was enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 孫朗人妻吳，連江人。

translations.literal: Wu, wife of Sun Langren, a native of Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, wife of Sun Langren, of Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 姑陳，早寡，遺腹生朗人。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law Chen, widowed early, bore Langren posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law Chen was widowed young and bore Langren after her husband's death.

sentences.zh: 性嚴急，有不當意，輒堅臥，朗人偕吳跪床下，俟意解，命之起，乃起。

translations.literal: She was stern and impatient; when displeased she would lie rigidly in bed—Langren and Wu knelt at the bedside until her mood eased and she bade them rise, then they rose.
translations.idiomatic: She was stern and quick-tempered. When displeased she would lie rigid in bed. Langren and Wu knelt at her bedside until her mood softened and she told them to rise—only then would they stand.

sentences.zh: 朗人卒，吳以節終。

translations.literal: Langren died; Wu preserved her chastity to the end.
translations.idiomatic: After Langren died, Wu remained a widow to the end of her days.

sentences.zh: 李天挺妻申，日照人。

translations.literal: Shen, wife of Li Tianting, a native of Rizhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, wife of Li Tianting, of Rizhao.

sentences.zh: 天挺早卒，姑嚴，申年六十，猶終日跪庭中。

translations.literal: Tianting died early; Mother-in-law was stern; Shen at sixty still knelt in the courtyard all day.
translations.idiomatic: Tianting died young. Her mother-in-law was severe, and even at sixty Shen still knelt in the courtyard all day long.

sentences.zh: 居姑喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: During Mother-in-law's mourning she died from grief-worn exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: During her mother-in-law's mourning she wore herself to death with grief.

sentences.zh: 劉與齊妻魏，秦州人。

translations.literal: Wei, wife of Liu Yuqi, a native of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, wife of Liu Yuqi, of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 既寡，事姑，日被笞罵，歡顏受之。

translations.literal: Once widowed she served Mother-in-law, daily beaten and reviled, receiving it with a smiling face.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed, she served her mother-in-law and was beaten and reviled every day, yet received it all with a smiling face.

sentences.zh: 躬薉賤，十餘年不怠。

translations.literal: She personally did the foulest tasks for more than ten years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: She did the foulest chores herself for more than ten years without slackening.

sentences.zh: 周志桂妻馮，湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Feng, wife of Zhou Zhigui, a native of Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, wife of Zhou Zhigui, of Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 姑暴，忍飢以養，猶時時加箠楚。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law was violent; she endured hunger to support her, yet was still often beaten with the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was violent. Feng went hungry to support her and was still beaten with the rod from time to time.

sentences.zh: 姑病瘓，不能舉杖，叱馮跪自撾，流血，不敢怨。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law fell ill with paralysis and could not raise the staff; she ordered Feng to kneel and beat herself until blood flowed—Feng dared not complain.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell paralyzed and could no longer raise the staff, she ordered Feng to kneel and beat herself until she bled. Feng dared not complain.

sentences.zh: 曆三十餘年，人名其里曰孝婦村。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years people named her lane Filial Wife Village.
translations.idiomatic: After more than thirty years the people named her lane Filial Wife Village.

sentences.zh: 歐陽玉光妻蔡，湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Cai, wife of Ouyang Yuguang, a native of Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, wife of Ouyang Yuguang, of Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 玉光母劉，治家有法度。

translations.literal: Yuguang's mother Liu governed the household with method.
translations.idiomatic: Yuguang's mother Liu ran the household with strict order.

sentences.zh: 玉光居父喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: Yuguang observed his father's mourning and died from grief-worn exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuguang mourned his father and wore himself to death with grief.

sentences.zh: 蔡承姑教，董家事，率妯娌，與子侄傭奴，各有專職，家漸起。

translations.literal: Cai received Mother-in-law's teaching, managed household affairs, led sisters-in-law—and with sons, nephews, hired servants and slaves each had fixed duties; the family gradually prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Cai followed her mother-in-law's teachings, managed the household, and led her sisters-in-law. Sons, nephews, hired hands, and servants each had fixed duties, and the family gradually prospered.

sentences.zh: 子惟本，亦娶於蔡。

translations.literal: Son Weiben also married a woman of the Cai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Their son Weiben also married a woman of the Cai clan.

sentences.zh: 婦家貧，將嫁，宗族週焉，得錢三千有奇，陰置稈薦中，而係鑰其端。

translations.literal: The bride's family was poor; when she was to marry the clan contributed, obtaining somewhat more than three thousand cash; she secretly placed it in straw matting and tied a string to the end as a key.
translations.idiomatic: The bride's family was poor. When she was to marry, the clan raised a little over three thousand cash for her. She hid the money inside a straw mat and tied a string to one end.

sentences.zh: 父送女還，入室，引鑰，則錢在焉。

translations.literal: Father escorted his daughter home; entering the room she pulled the string—and the money was there.
translations.idiomatic: Her father escorted her home. She entered the room, pulled the string, and found the money still there.

sentences.zh: 曰：「孝哉我女，留此以活我！

translations.literal: He said: "How filial my daughter—she left this to keep me alive!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "How filial my daughter is—she left this to keep me alive!"

sentences.zh: 」惟本亦早卒，從姑敬事祖姑，祖姑興，姑執笄侍左，婦自右為約發。

translations.literal: " Weiben also died early; following Mother-in-law she reverently served Great-grandmother—in the morning Great-grandmother rose, Mother-in-law held the hairpin on the left, the wife on the right bound her hair.
translations.idiomatic: Weiben also died young. Following her mother-in-law, the younger Cai reverently served the great-grandmother. Each morning when the old woman rose, the mother-in-law held the hairpin on the left while the wife bound her hair on the right.

sentences.zh: 盥，姑奉水，婦奉槃。

translations.literal: At washing, Mother-in-law held the water, the wife the basin.
translations.idiomatic: At her washing, the mother-in-law held the water and the wife the basin.

sentences.zh: 及食，婦具饌，姑侑之。

translations.literal: At meals the wife prepared food, Mother-in-law presented it.
translations.idiomatic: At meals the wife prepared the food and the mother-in-law served it.

sentences.zh: 寢，三世連床。

translations.literal: At sleep, three generations shared one bed.
translations.idiomatic: At night all three generations shared one bed.

sentences.zh: 一夕，姑起，墮床折肋，婦號泣就援，姑戒勿聲，毋令祖姑驚也。

translations.literal: One night Mother-in-law rose, fell from the bed and broke a rib—the wife wailed and rushed to help; Mother-in-law warned her not to cry out, lest Great-grandmother be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: One night the mother-in-law rose, fell from the bed, and broke a rib. The wife rushed to her wailing, but the mother-in-law hushed her—do not alarm the great-grandmother.

sentences.zh: 祖姑晚喪明，手足痿痺，挽箯輿，日遊庭中，姑肩前，婦肩後。

translations.literal: Great-grandmother in old age lost her sight; hands and feet withered— they pulled a sedan chair and each day roamed the courtyard, Mother-in-law shouldering the front, the wife the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandmother went blind in old age and her limbs withered. They pulled a bamboo sedan and each day walked her through the courtyard—the mother-in-law at the front, the wife at the rear.

sentences.zh: 祖姑劉，年至九十，姑蔡，九十六，婦蔡，八十三。

translations.literal: Great-grandmother Liu reached ninety, Mother-in-law Cai ninety-six, the wife Cai eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandmother Liu lived to ninety, mother-in-law Cai to ninety-six, and the wife Cai to eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓為之傳，謂：「歐陽姑、婦，雖似庸行無殊絕者，而純孝兢兢，事姑至六十年、五十年之久而不渝，天下之至難，無以逾此。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan wrote their biography, saying: "Ouyang mother-in-law and daughter-in-law—though their conduct seems ordinary without marvels, in pure filial devotion, careful and earnest, serving Mother-in-law for sixty and fifty years without wavering—nothing under heaven is harder; none surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan wrote their biography, saying, "The Ouyang mother-in-law and daughter-in-law seem to perform only ordinary deeds without marvels—but in pure, earnest devotion they served their mother-in-law for sixty and fifty years without wavering. Nothing under heaven is harder; nothing surpasses this."

sentences.zh: 蕭學華妻賀，湖南安化人。

translations.literal: He, wife of Xiao Xuehua, of Anhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He, wife of Xiao Xuehua, of Anhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 賀父徙陝西，學華贅其家。

translations.literal: He's father moved to Shaanxi; Xuehua married into the family as uxorilocal son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He's father moved to Shaanxi, and Xuehua married into the household as a live-in son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 年餘，學華歸省母，賀欲與俱，父不許，賀割股肉付夫以奉姑。

translations.literal: After more than a year Xuehua returned to visit his mother; He wished to go with him but Father would not allow it—He cut thigh flesh and gave it to her husband to present to Mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Xuehua went home to visit his mother. He wished to take her with him, but her father refused. He cut flesh from her thigh and gave it to her husband to present to his mother.

sentences.zh: 姑適病，學華烹肉進，病良已。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law happened to be ill; Xuehua cooked the flesh and presented it—the illness was completely cured.
translations.idiomatic: His mother happened to be ill. Xuehua cooked the flesh and fed it to her, and she recovered completely.

sentences.zh: 後學華攜賀歸，事姑以孝稱。

translations.literal: Later Xuehua brought He home; she was famed for filial service to Mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xuehua brought He home, and she became renowned for her devotion to her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 張友儀妻陳，福建永定人。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of Zhang Youyi, of Yongding in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of Zhang Youyi, of Yongding in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 事姑孝，姑嘗稱曰：「諸婦汝最樸訥，然酒漿筐篋瑣碎無不治，得吾意者，汝也！

translations.literal: Filial in serving Mother-in-law—Mother-in-law once praised her: "Among all daughters-in-law you are the plainest and most taciturn, yet wine, broth, baskets and boxes—nothing trifling goes untended; you alone understand my mind!"
translations.idiomatic: She was devoted to her mother-in-law, who once said, "Of all my daughters-in-law you are the plainest and most taciturn—yet wine, broth, baskets, and boxes, nothing however small escapes you. You alone understand what I want!"

sentences.zh: 」友儀早卒，陳未三十，勉痛事姑，撫孤子。

translations.literal: " Youyi died early; Chen was not yet thirty—she braced herself through grief to serve Mother-in-law and raise the orphaned son.
translations.idiomatic: Youyi died young. Chen was not yet thirty. She mastered her grief to serve her mother-in-law and raise their orphaned son.

sentences.zh: 同治初，寇至，負姑入山避，徒行數十里，踵裂血流，屢踣屢起。

translations.literal: At the start of the Tongzhi reign bandits came; she carried Mother-in-law into the mountains to flee, walking on foot several tens of li—heels split, blood flowing, repeatedly falling and rising.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tongzhi reign bandits came. She carried her mother-in-law into the mountains on foot for dozens of li, heels split and bleeding, falling again and again yet rising each time.

sentences.zh: 匿深林中，燃枯枝，採野蓛以活，卒得免。

translations.literal: They hid in deep forest, burned dead branches, gathered wild herbs to live—and at last escaped.
translations.idiomatic: They hid deep in the forest, burned dead branches, and gathered wild greens to survive until at last they escaped.

sentences.zh: 子日焜妻李，嘗刲股愈母病，事祖姑及姑孝。

translations.literal: Li, wife of son Rikun—she had cut thigh flesh to cure her mother's illness; filial to great-grandmother-in-law and mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Li, wife of their son Rikun, had once cut flesh from her thigh to cure her own mother's illness and was devoted to both her great-grandmother-in-law and her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 姑病，割臂進，病目，舐以舌，良已。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law fell ill; she cut her arm and presented it; the illness struck the eyes—she licked with her tongue and it was cured.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill she cut her arm and offered the flesh. The illness afflicted the eyes; she licked them with her tongue and they healed.

sentences.zh: 嘗赴族人飯，心動，歸，正姑病。

translations.literal: Once she went to a kinsman's feast; her heart stirred, she returned—and Mother-in-law was indeed ill.
translations.idiomatic: Once she went to a kinsman's feast, felt a sudden unease, and returned—to find her mother-in-law indeed ill.

sentences.zh: 又嘗宿姻家，夜半，索輿還。

translations.literal: Again she lodged at an in-law's house; at midnight she called for a sedan chair to return.
translations.idiomatic: Another time she stayed overnight at a relative's house and at midnight called for a sedan chair to take her home.

sentences.zh: 姑曰：「吾正念汝，知汝必念我速歸也。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law said: "I was just thinking of you—I knew you must be thinking of me and would hurry back."
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law said, "I was just thinking of you—I knew you would be thinking of me and hurry home."

sentences.zh: 馮氏，武進人。

translations.literal: The Feng clan, of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Feng clan, of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 嫁吉龍大，事舅姑謹。

translations.literal: Married Ji Longda; served father-in-law and mother-in-law with care.
translations.idiomatic: She married Ji Longda and served her parents-in-law with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 姑病偏廢，飲食臥起皆需馮，而龍大遊蕩，欲衒馮以媒估客，馮不可。

translations.literal: Mother-in-law was paralyzed on one side—eating, drinking, lying down and rising all required Feng; yet Longda wandered idle and wished to display Feng to broker merchant guests—Feng would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was half-paralyzed and needed Feng for every meal and every movement. Longda idled about and wished to parade Feng before merchant guests to broker deals. Feng refused.

sentences.zh: 龍大引外婦入室，舅怒而逐之，馮曰：「姑病，婦終日侍，苦為他事閒，得一人分其勞，甚善。

translations.literal: Longda brought an outside woman into the house; Father-in-law was angry and drove her out—Feng said: "Mother-in-law is ill; the wife attends all day. Wearying oneself with other affairs is hard—getting one person to share the labor is very good."
translations.idiomatic: Longda brought another woman into the house. Her father-in-law was furious and drove her out. Feng said, "Mother is ill and I attend her all day. Other duties wear me thin—having someone share the labor would be a blessing."

sentences.zh: 」因持臥具從姑寢。

translations.literal: " She took bedding and slept with Mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She took her bedding and slept beside her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 龍大時時毆辱馮，馮未嘗有怨色。

translations.literal: Longda from time to time beat and reviled Feng—Feng never showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Longda beat and reviled her from time to time, yet Feng never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 舅病，龍大市毒藥授馮，令飲其父，馮擲藥，跪諫數日，龍大別市藥，毆而逼之，馮歎曰：「我所以不死，為舅姑耳，今無冀矣！

translations.literal: Father-in-law fell ill; Longda bought poison and gave it to Feng, ordering her to give it to his father—Feng cast away the medicine and knelt pleading for days; Longda bought other medicine elsewhere, beat and pressed her—Feng sighed: "The reason I did not die was for father-in-law and mother-in-law—now there is no hope!"
translations.idiomatic: When her father-in-law fell ill, Longda bought poison and ordered Feng to give it to his father. Feng threw the medicine away and knelt pleading for days. Longda bought poison elsewhere and beat her into compliance. Feng sighed, "The only reason I have stayed alive is for my parents-in-law. Now there is no hope."

sentences.zh: 」入視姑寢，至龍大所，舉藥盡飲之。

translations.literal: " She went in to see Mother-in-law asleep, then went to Longda's place and drank the medicine to the last.
translations.idiomatic: She looked in on her sleeping mother-in-law, then went to Longda's room and drank every drop of the poison.

sentences.zh: 謂龍大曰：「我代舅矣，後毋萌此念！

translations.literal: She said to Longda: "I have taken Father-in-law's place—hereafter do not harbor this thought!"
translations.idiomatic: She told Longda, "I have taken Father's place. Never think this way again."

sentences.zh: 」須臾毒發死。

translations.literal: " In a moment the poison took effect and she died.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the poison took hold and she died.

sentences.zh: 王鉞妻隋，諸城人。

translations.literal: Sui, wife of Wang Yue, a native of Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, wife of Wang Yue, of Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 敏而有定識。

translations.literal: Quick-witted and with firm judgment.
translations.idiomatic: She was quick-witted and resolute.

sentences.zh: 明季，奉姑避兵，航海行數千里。

translations.literal: In late Ming she supported Mother-in-law fleeing war, traveling by sea several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming she escorted her mother-in-law away from the wars, traveling thousands of li by sea.

sentences.zh: 寇至，負姑夜踰垣匿谷中以免。

translations.literal: When raiders came she carried Mother-in-law by night over walls to hide in a valley and escape.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders came she carried her mother-in-law over the wall by night and hid with her in a valley until they were safe.

sentences.zh: 鉞成進士，為廣東西寧知縣。

translations.literal: Yue passed the jinshi examination and became magistrate of Xining in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue became a jinshi and served as magistrate of Xining in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，吳三桂反，鉞城守，賊至，鉞謂隋：「當奈何？

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi Wu Sangui rebelled; Yue defended the city; rebels arrived—Yue said to Sui: "What shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Kangxi reign Wu Sangui rebelled. Yue defended the city. When rebels arrived he asked Sui, "What shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 」隋出匕首曰：「有此何懼！

translations.literal: " Sui produced a dagger: "With this, what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Sui drew a dagger and said, "With this, what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」賊去，鉞行取主事，隋請以諸子先行。

translations.literal: " The rebels departed; Yue was promoted to director of a ministry; Sui asked that the sons go ahead first.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew. Yue was promoted to director in the ministries. Sui asked that their sons travel ahead first.

sentences.zh: 是時賊方盛，行人道絕，隋得敝舟，挾幼子經肇慶、度大庾、入鄱陽湖，水陸行數千里，率僕婢佩刀晝夜警備。

translations.literal: At that time rebels were powerful and travel routes were cut off—Sui obtained a worn boat, took her young son through Zhaoqing, crossed Dayu, entered Poyang Lake—by water and land several thousand li—leading servants and maids with daggers at belt, alert day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still held sway and the roads were cut. Sui found a battered boat, took her young son through Zhaoqing, over Dayu Pass, and into Poyang Lake—thousands of li by water and land—with servants and maids belted with daggers, alert day and night.

sentences.zh: 家居，地震，自樓墮，血淋漓，持子泣，地搖搖未已，子請避，隋曰：「諸婢壓其下，吾去，死矣！

translations.literal: At home, earthquake—she fell from the building, blood streaming; holding her son she wept; the earth still shook; the son asked to flee—Sui said: "The maidservants are pinned beneath—I go, they die!"
translations.idiomatic: At home an earthquake struck. She fell from the upper story, blood streaming, clutching her son and weeping while the ground still shook. Her son begged to flee. Sui said, "The maidservants are pinned beneath—if I leave, they die!"

sentences.zh: 」督家僮發磚石出之，皆復活。

translations.literal: " She directed household servants to dig out brick and stone; all were saved alive.
translations.idiomatic: She directed the household servants to dig through the brick and stone. All were brought out alive.

sentences.zh: 火發於樓，煙蔽梯不可登，命以水濡被予諸婢，身持濕衣障火先登，諸婢汲水次第上，火遂得熸。

translations.literal: Fire broke out in the building; smoke covered the ladder so it could not be climbed—she ordered wet quilts given to the maidservants, herself held wet clothing to block fire and climbed first; the maids drew water and ascended in turn—the fire was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the building. Smoke choked the stair so no one could climb. She ordered wet quilts for the maidservants, wrapped herself in wet clothes to shield against the flames, and went up first while the maids drew water and followed one by one until the fire was put out.

sentences.zh: 子沛恩、沛憻、沛恂，皆成進士，官於朝，隋益勤儉自斂抑，鄉人稱老實王家。

translations.literal: Sons Peien, Peixian, and Peixun all became jinshi and served at court—Sui grew still more frugal and self-restrained; villagers called them the Honest Wang family.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Peien, Peixian, and Peixun all became jinshi and served at court. Sui grew still more frugal and restrained. The villagers called them the Honest Wang family.

sentences.zh: 林雲銘妻蔡，雲銘，閩人；

translations.literal: Cai, wife of Lin Yunming; Yunming, a native of Fujian;
translations.idiomatic: Cai, wife of Lin Yunming. Yunming was from Fujian;

sentences.zh: 蔡名捷，字步仙，侯官人。

translations.literal: Cai was named Jie, styled Buxian, of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was named Jie, styled Buxian, of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 雲銘，順治十五年進士，授江南徽州推官。

translations.literal: Yunming, jinshi in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, was appointed investigating censor of Huizhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming became a jinshi in the fifteenth year of the Shunzhi reign and was appointed investigating censor of Huizhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功兵入江，徽州兵叛，蔡矢死不去。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong's troops entered the Yangtze; Huizhou soldiers mutinied—Cai swore to die and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Chenggong's troops entered the Yangtze and the Huizhou garrison mutinied, Cai swore to die rather than flee.

sentences.zh: 官省，還居建寧。

translations.literal: He left office and returned to Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office and returned to live in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠反，下云銘獄，蔡憂之，嘔血殷紫，女瑛佩剜臂肉入藥，旋蘇。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong rebelled and cast Yunming into prison—Cai grieved, vomiting blood dark purple; daughter Yingpei scraped arm flesh to mix into medicine, and she soon revived.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled and threw Yunming into prison, Cai grieved until she vomited dark purple blood. Her daughter Yingpei scraped flesh from her arm to mix into medicine, and Cai soon revived.

sentences.zh: 師至，雲銘乃出獄。

translations.literal: When the army arrived Yunming was released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived, Yunming was released from prison.

sentences.zh: 雲銘無子，蔡為買妾七，乃生子。

translations.literal: Yunming had no son; Cai bought seven concubines for him, and at last sons were born.
translations.idiomatic: Yunming had no sons. Cai bought him seven concubines, and at last sons were born.

sentences.zh: 蔡禦諸妾有恩，所親有婦妒，而五十無子者，蔡延至家，與處三日，歸為夫買妾生子。

translations.literal: Cai treated all concubines with grace; among her kin was a wife jealous [of concubines] who at fifty had no son—Cai invited her to stay at home, dwelt with her three days, returned and bought a concubine for her husband to bear a son.
translations.idiomatic: Cai treated all the concubines with kindness. Among her kin was a wife consumed by jealousy who at fifty still had no son. Cai invited her to stay at the house and kept her company for three days, then returned home and bought a concubine for her husband so she might at last bear a son.

sentences.zh: 裡婦忤其夫，共指蔡以勸，曰：「毋令林孺人知。

translations.literal: Village wives who defied their husbands together pointed to Cai to admonish, saying: "Do not let Lady Lin know."
translations.idiomatic: When village wives defied their husbands, others would point to Cai as an example and say, "Do not let Lady Lin find out."

sentences.zh: 」瑛佩為閩清鄭郯妻。

translations.literal: " Yingpei was wife of Zheng Tan of Minqing.
translations.idiomatic: Yingpei was the wife of Zheng Tan of Minqing.

sentences.zh: 陳龍妻胡，龍溪人。

translations.literal: Hu, wife of Chen Long, a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu, wife of Chen Long, was from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 龍少恃勇，為暴於鄉里，父老群謀去害。

translations.literal: Long in youth relied on courage and was violent in the village; elders together plotted to remove the harm.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Long trusted in his strength and terrorized the countryside; the village elders together plotted to rid themselves of him.

sentences.zh: 時胡未嫁，使密勸乘時立

translations.literal: When Hu was not yet married she sent someone secretly to urge him to seize the moment and establish
translations.idiomatic: Before she was married, Hu sent someone in secret to urge him to seize the moment and establish

sentences.zh: 功名。

translations.literal: fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 龍亡命為盜海島，父母將別字，胡堅拒。

translations.literal: Long fled as outlaw and became pirate on sea islands; parents were about to betroth her elsewhere—Hu firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Long fled and became a pirate on the islands; when her parents were about to betroth her elsewhere, Hu steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 聞龍娶，不貳。

translations.literal: Hearing Long had married, she did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard Long had married, she did not waver in her devotion.

sentences.zh: 龍降，官金門總兵，知胡猶未字，乃成婚。

translations.literal: Long submitted, was appointed Jinmen commander-in-chief; learning Hu was still unbetrothed, they then married.
translations.idiomatic: Long surrendered and was appointed commander-in-chief at Jinmen. Learning that Hu was still unbetrothed, they were married at last.

sentences.zh: 海澄許貞嘗以逋餉繫獄，胡告龍代償其負，釋使去，貞卒為名將。

translations.literal: Xu Zhen of Haicheng was once imprisoned for arrears in rations payments; Hu told Long to repay his debt, had him released—Zhen eventually became a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhen of Haicheng had once been imprisoned for unpaid rations. Hu urged Long to pay his debt and have him released; Zhen eventually became a renowned general.

sentences.zh: 王懃妻岳，曲周人。

translations.literal: Yue, wife of Wang Qin, a native of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, wife of Wang Qin, was from Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 岳奉舅姑篤謹，若不能言。

translations.literal: Yue served her parents-in-law with devoted care, as if she could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yue served her parents-in-law with devoted, reticent care, as though she scarcely spoke at all.

sentences.zh: 懃移家臨清，而商於天津。

translations.literal: Qin moved the family to Linqing while trading in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Qin moved the household to Linqing while he traded in Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 王倫為亂，將攻臨清，臨清民爭走避，岳請於舅姑曰：「賊將以臨清為窟，必不剪居民以自弱。

translations.literal: Wang Lun rebelled and was about to attack Linqing; the people rushed to flee—Yue asked her parents-in-law: "The rebels will use Linqing as their lair—they surely will not slaughter residents and weaken themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lun rose in rebellion and was about to attack Linqing. The townspeople rushed to flee. Yue said to her parents-in-law, "The rebels will make Linqing their stronghold—they will not slaughter the populace and weaken themselves."

sentences.zh: 從眾以行，不死於奔竄，必死於蹂藉，宜若可緩然。

translations.literal: "If we follow the crowd fleeing, we die not in flight but in trampling—it seems we may afford to wait."
translations.idiomatic: "If we join the fleeing crowd, we will die not in flight but underfoot. It seems we can afford to wait."

sentences.zh: 」舅姑用其言，出者爭道，多擠入水死。

translations.literal: " Her parents-in-law took her advice; those who fled crowded the roads, many crushed into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law took her advice. Those who fled crowded the roads, and many were crushed into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 岳曰：「乃今宜可徙，官軍且至，賊方謀出禦，不暇捕逃人。

translations.literal: Yue said: "Now we may move—the government troops are coming; the rebels are planning to go out to resist and have no leisure to hunt fugitives."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Now we may leave. The government troops are near, and the rebels are planning to march out against them—they have no time to hunt down fugitives."

sentences.zh: 且徙者已十八九，今行，無慮蹂藉；

translations.literal: "Moreover nineteen in twenty have already fled—if we go now, no worry of trampling;"
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, nine in ten have already fled. If we go now, there is little fear of being trampled;"

sentences.zh: 今不行，免於賊，或不免於官軍。

translations.literal: "if we do not go now, we escape the rebels but perhaps not the government troops."
translations.idiomatic: "if we stay, we may escape the rebels but not the government troops."

sentences.zh: 」遂相將潛出城，還曲周，懃亦歸。

translations.literal: " They stole out of the city together, returned to Quzhou; Qin also came home.
translations.idiomatic: They stole out of the city together and returned to Quzhou; Qin came home as well.

sentences.zh: 人稱其能量事，岳篤謹如故。

translations.literal: People praised her ability to manage affairs; Yue remained as devoted and careful as before.
translations.idiomatic: People praised her judgment in a crisis; Yue remained as devoted and careful as ever.

sentences.zh: 魯宗鎬妻硃，名如玉，字又寒，仁和人。

translations.literal: Zhu, wife of Lu Zonghao—named Ruyu, styled Youhan, of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, wife of Lu Zonghao, was named Ruyu and styled Youhan; she was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 事舅姑孝。

translations.literal: She was filial in serving her parents-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: She was filial in serving her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 或以賄幹宗鎬，有所關說，硃勸毋受。

translations.literal: Someone tried to bribe Zonghao with requests for favors—Zhu urged him not to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When someone tried to bribe Zonghao with a petition for favors, Zhu urged him to refuse.

sentences.zh: 宗鎬曰：「我度是無利害。

translations.literal: Zonghao said: "I judge this harmless."
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao said, "I judge this harmless."

sentences.zh: 」硃曰：「諸為不義事，皆以為無利害耳，奈何以貧隳素行！

translations.literal: " Zhu said: "All who do wrong deem it harmless—how can we let poverty ruin our upright conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said, "Everyone who does wrong thinks it harmless. How can we let poverty ruin a lifetime of upright conduct?"

sentences.zh: 」宗鎬悟，謝之。

translations.literal: " Zonghao understood and thanked her.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghao understood and thanked her.

sentences.zh: 馬叔籥妻丁，揚州舊城人，事舅姑甚謹。

translations.literal: Ding, wife of Ma Shuyue, of old Yangzhou city, served her parents-in-law with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Ding, wife of Ma Shuyue, was from old Yangzhou; she served her parents-in-law with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 叔籥兄弟三，既分，而伯兄以訟破家，丁義不

translations.literal: Shuyue had three brothers; after the division the elder brother lost the family in lawsuits—Ding held it wrong to
translations.idiomatic: Shuyue had three brothers. After they divided the estate, the eldest lost everything in litigation. Ding held it wrong to

sentences.zh: 己食，雖壺酒豆肉必以分。

translations.literal: eat alone—even a cup of wine or bit of meat she must share.
translations.idiomatic: eat alone; even a cup of wine or a scrap of meat she would share with them.

sentences.zh: 一日，語叔籥，請致家於伯氏，叔籥許之。

translations.literal: One day she told Shuyue and asked to transfer the household to the elder brother's line; he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: One day she spoke to Shuyue and asked to turn the household over to his elder brother's line. Shuyue agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁事伯如舅，姒如姑，米鹽纖悉一關姒，嫁時衣裝飾首約臂皆不私。

translations.literal: Ding served the elder brother as a father-in-law, the sister-in-law as a mother-in-law; grain, salt, and every trifle passed through the sister-in-law; bridal clothes, ornaments, bracelets—all withheld from private use.
translations.idiomatic: Ding served the elder brother as she would a father-in-law and the sister-in-law as a mother-in-law. Grain, salt, and every trifle went through the sister-in-law's hands; her bridal clothes, hair ornaments, and bracelets were never kept for herself alone.

sentences.zh: 家故賈也，叔籥兄善賈，遂以其家富。

translations.literal: The family had been merchants; Shuyue's elder brother was skilled at trade, and with it their household grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long been in trade. Shuyue's elder brother was a skilled merchant, and under his hand the household grew wealthy.

sentences.zh: 叔籥有所請於姒，姒不時給，叔籥怒曰：「乃我家所有，嫂何與？

translations.literal: Shuyue made a request of the sister-in-law who did not promptly comply—Shuyue angrily said: "This is our family's property—what business is it of yours, sister-in-law?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shuyue made a request of his sister-in-law and she did not promptly comply, he said in anger, "This is our family's property—what is it to you, sister-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 」丁曰：「始讓而終怒，人其謂我何？

translations.literal: " Ding said: "To yield at first then rage at the end—what will people say of me?"
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "To yield at first and rage at the end—what will people say of me?"

sentences.zh: 」勸叔籥毋校。

translations.literal: " She urged Shuyue not to quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: She urged Shuyue not to quarrel.

sentences.zh: 許光清妻陳，海寧人。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of Xu Guangqing, a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of Xu Guangqing, was from Haining.

sentences.zh: 善持家。

translations.literal: Skilled at managing the household.
translations.idiomatic: She was skilled at managing the household.

sentences.zh: 戚有鬻婦者，婦誓死不從，陳偕姒婦硃醵金畀其夫，要之署券。

translations.literal: A relative was selling his wife who swore death before consenting—Chen with her sister-in-law Zhu pooled money, gave it to the husband, required him to sign a deed.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman was selling his wife, who swore she would rather die than go. Chen and her sister-in-law Zhu pooled money, paid her husband, and required him to sign a deed of sale to them.

sentences.zh: 曰：「彼人遊蕩，金盡終且鬻婦，不如是，婦不免。

translations.literal: She said: "That man is dissolute; when the money is spent he will sell his wife in the end—in this way at least the wife is not lost."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "That man is dissolute. When the money is gone he will sell his wife in the end. This way, at least, she is not lost to him entirely."

sentences.zh: 」乃招婦至，善視之。

translations.literal: " They summoned the wife and treated her kindly.
translations.idiomatic: They brought the wife into their household and treated her with kindness.

sentences.zh: 其夫死，复醵金贖所居，遣婦還，並前券焚之。

translations.literal: When her husband died they again pooled money to redeem her dwelling, sent her home, and burned the earlier deed.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died they again pooled money to redeem her home, sent her back, and burned the deed.

sentences.zh: 鄰童入其室竊壺去，陳戒家人勿言，曰：「彼何以為人？

translations.literal: A neighbor's child stole a pot from the house—Chen forbade the household to speak of it, saying: "How is he to become a person?"
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor's child stole a pot from the house. Chen forbade the household to speak of it, saying, "How is he to grow into a decent person?"

sentences.zh: 」禦婢寬，聞有虐婢者，必以陶潛語勸曰：「彼亦人子也！

translations.literal: " She was lenient with maidservants; hearing of one abused she would cite Tao Qian: "He too is someone's son!"
translations.idiomatic: She was lenient with her maidservants. When she heard of one being abused, she would quote Tao Qian: "He too is someone's son!"

sentences.zh: 黃開鼇妻廖，開鼇，高安人；

translations.literal: Liao, wife of Huang Kai'ao; Kai'ao, a native of Gao'an;
translations.idiomatic: Liao, wife of Huang Kai'ao. Kai'ao was from Gao'an;

sentences.zh: 廖，沔陽人。

translations.literal: Liao was from Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liao was from Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 開鼇善為針，設肆衡州，廖佐以紡績。

translations.literal: Kai'ao was skilled at needle-making, set up shop in Hengzhou; Liao assisted with spinning and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: Kai'ao was skilled at making needles and opened a shop in Hengzhou; Liao helped with spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 開鼇病瘓，廖習為針，針成，置諸版，摩以掌，針乃澤，數以是創，不懈。

translations.literal: Kai'ao was paralyzed; Liao learned needle-making; when needles were done she placed them on the block, rubbed with her palm until they gleamed—often cut by this, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai'ao was paralyzed, Liao learned the craft herself. When a needle was finished she laid it on the block and polished it with her palm until it gleamed. She cut her hands again and again at the work but never slackened.

sentences.zh: 開鼇卒，子長發幼，婦劉，監利人，待年於姑氏。

translations.literal: Kai'ao died; son Changfa was young; daughter-in-law Liu of Jianli was awaiting marriage at her mother-in-law's.
translations.idiomatic: Kai'ao died, leaving a young son Changfa. His wife Liu of Jianli was still awaiting the wedding at her mother-in-law's home.

sentences.zh: 稍長，夫婦共為針，長發截鐵，圓本而銳末，持就段，睨火察純窳。

translations.literal: When older, the couple made needles together; Changfa cut iron, rounded the base and sharpened the tip, held it to the forge and by fire's glow judged purity and flaws.
translations.idiomatic: When he was older, husband and wife made needles together. Changfa cut the iron, rounded the base and sharpened the tip, held each piece to the forge, and by the fire's glow judged its purity and flaws.

sentences.zh: 劉削竹，綴以鋼，懸雙絙環竹，曳則竹轉以穿針鼻。

translations.literal: Liu shaved bamboo, fitted steel, suspended twin cords around bamboo—pull and the bamboo turned to thread the needle's eye.
translations.idiomatic: Liu shaved bamboo, fitted it with steel, and hung twin cords around it so that when pulled the bamboo would turn and thread the needle's eye.

sentences.zh: 針良，市者多，家漸裕。

translations.literal: Needles were good; buyers many; household gradually prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Their needles were excellent, buyers flocked to them, and the household gradually grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全之徒躪湖南，家破，長發治針益力。

translations.literal: Hong Xiuquan's followers trampled Hunan; family ruined; Changfa worked at needles all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan's followers ravaged Hunan their home was ruined, and Changfa worked at needles all the harder.

sentences.zh: 當冬，得敝​​羊裘奉廖，與劉皆敝

translations.literal: In winter he obtained a worn sheepskin coat for Liao; he and Liu wore worn
translations.idiomatic: That winter he obtained a worn sheepskin coat for Liao; he and Liu wore worn

sentences.zh: 褐短褌，手足龜，不敢怠。

translations.literal: brown short trousers; hands and feet cracked, never daring to slack.
translations.idiomatic: brown short trousers. Their hands and feet cracked with cold, yet they never dared to slacken.

sentences.zh: 長發旋卒，子才三歲，被火，家再破。

translations.literal: Changfa soon died; son only three; fire struck; family broken again.
translations.idiomatic: Changfa soon died, leaving a son of only three. Fire struck the house and the family was ruined again.

sentences.zh: 於是廖語劉曰：「天乎！

translations.literal: Then Liao said to Liu: "Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Then Liao said to Liu, "Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 此誠不可再活，盍同死？

translations.literal: "We truly cannot live through this again—shall we die together?"
translations.idiomatic: "We truly cannot endure this again. Shall we die together?"

sentences.zh: 」劉對曰：「火，亦常也，姑、婦惟當復食苦耳。

translations.literal: " Liu replied: "Fire is but common—the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law need only endure bitterness again."
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, "Fire is a common misfortune. Mother-in-law and daughter-in-law need only endure hardship again."

sentences.zh: 」鬻簪珥為貿遷，居賤鬻貴。

translations.literal: " They sold hairpins and earrings to trade goods, buying cheap and selling dear.
translations.idiomatic: They sold their hairpins and earrings to go into trade, buying cheap and selling dear.

sentences.zh: 廖持算，劉主議值。

translations.literal: Liao kept the accounts; Liu set the prices.
translations.idiomatic: Liao kept the accounts; Liu set the prices.

sentences.zh: 又數年，家复裕。

translations.literal: After some years the household prospered again.
translations.idiomatic: After a few more years the household was prosperous again.

sentences.zh: 廖老而卞，易怒，劉進淡巴菰，徐言他事輒解；

translations.literal: Liao grew old and stubborn, easily angered; Liu would offer tobacco, speak slowly of other things and she would soften;
translations.idiomatic: Liao grew old and obstinate, easily angered. Liu would offer her tobacco and speak gently of other matters until her mood softened;

sentences.zh: 不解，即跪謝，相持泣乃已。

translations.literal: if not, she knelt in apology; holding each other weeping until it passed.
translations.idiomatic: if not, she would kneel in apology; they would hold each other weeping until the anger passed.

sentences.zh: 廖七十六而卒。

translations.literal: Liao died at seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: Liao died at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 劉既善貿遷，鄰家就求術，劉為謀至詳，貧者貸以貲。

translations.literal: Liu was skilled at trade; neighbors came seeking her art; Liu planned in detail, lent capital to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was skilled at trade. Neighbors came to learn her methods; she advised them in detail and lent capital to the poor.

sentences.zh: 同巷居五十餘家，多以貿遷富。

translations.literal: More than fifty households in the same lane grew rich through trade.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty households on the same lane grew wealthy through trade.

sentences.zh: 開鼇初設肆，才錢六千四百，劉晚年積白金至十萬，督子孫就學，取科目，家益大，年七十九而卒。

translations.literal: When Kai'ao first opened shop he had only 6,400 cash; Liu in her later years accumulated 100,000 taels of silver, urged descendants to study, won examination degrees; family grew greater; she died at seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When Kai'ao first opened his shop he had only 6,400 cash. Liu in her later years amassed 100,000 taels of silver, urged her descendants to study, and saw them win degrees at the examinations. The family grew still greater. She died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 黃茂梧妻顧，名若璞，字和知，仁和人。

translations.literal: Gu, wife of Huang Maowu—named Ruopu, styled Hezhi, of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, wife of Huang Maowu, was named Ruopu and styled Hezhi; she was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 顧好言經世之學，為詩、古文辭，自為集序曰：「若璞不才，少不若於母訓，笄事東生，十有三年。

translations.literal: Gu loved discourse on statecraft, wrote poetry and ancient-style prose, and in her own preface to the collection said: "Ruopu is without talent; in youth I fell short of my mother's teaching; at hairpinning I married Dongsheng, thirteen years."
translations.idiomatic: Gu delighted in practical statecraft and wrote poetry and ancient-style prose. In her own preface to the collection she wrote, "Ruopu is without talent. In youth I fell short of my mother's teaching. At my hairpinning I married Dongsheng, and thirteen years followed."

sentences.zh: 閒事詠歌，大抵與東生相對憂苦之所為作也。

translations.literal: In leisure I turned to song—mostly what was composed facing Dongsheng in shared sorrow and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: In my spare moments I turned to song—mostly what was written as we faced each other in shared sorrow and hardship.

sentences.zh: 東生溘逝，帷殯而哭，不如死之久矣。

translations.literal: Dongsheng passed suddenly; weeping beside the bier, I have long wished for death.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongsheng passed suddenly, I wept beside his bier and felt I had long wished for death.

sentences.zh: 徒以藐諸孤在。

translations.literal: Only because the little orphans remain.
translations.idiomatic: Only because my little orphans still remained.

sentences.zh: 發藏書，日夜披覽，二子從外傅，入輒令隅坐，為陳說吾所明。

translations.literal: I opened the stored books and read day and night; the two sons studied with outside tutors—when they entered I had them sit in a corner and explained what I understood.
translations.idiomatic: I opened the family library and read day and night. My two sons studied with outside tutors; when they came in I had them sit to one side and explained what I had grasped.

sentences.zh: 日月漸多，聞見與積，聖賢經傳，旁及騷雅詞賦，冀以自發其哀思。

translations.literal: Days and months grew many; hearing and sight accumulated—the classics of sages, and beside them the Songs and elegant fu—hoping thereby to release my grief.
translations.idiomatic: As days and months passed, what I heard and saw accumulated—the classics of the sages, and beside them the Songs and elegant fu—hoping thereby to give voice to my grief.

sentences.zh: 題曰臥月軒稿。

translations.literal: I titled it Drafts of the Reclining Moon Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: I titled it Drafts of the Reclining Moon Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 軒為東生所嘗憇，志思也。

translations.literal: The pavilion was where Dongsheng once rested—a record of remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion was where Dongsheng had once rested—a memorial to longing.

sentences.zh: 」東生，茂梧字。

translations.literal: " Dongsheng was Maowu's style.
translations.idiomatic: Dongsheng was Maowu's style name.

sentences.zh: 顧至康熙中乃卒，年九十。

translations.literal: Gu did not die until the Kangxi era, at ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Gu lived until the Kangxi reign and died at ninety.

sentences.zh: 子燦妻丁，從顧學，亦好言經世，先顧卒。

translations.literal: Ding, wife of son Can, studied under Gu, also loved statecraft discourse, died before Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Ding, wife of their son Can, studied under Gu and likewise delighted in statecraft; she died before Gu.

sentences.zh: 高其倬妻蔡，名琬，字季玉，漢軍正白旗人，綏遠將軍毓榮女也。

translations.literal: Cai, wife of Gao Qipei—named Wan, styled Jiyu, Han Banner of Plain White, daughter of General Yurong of Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Wan, wife of Gao Qipei, styled Jiyu, was of the Han Banner of the Plain White; she was the daughter of General Yurong of Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 毓榮、其倬皆有傳。

translations.literal: Yurong and Qipei both have biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yurong and Qipei both have biographies in these annals.

sentences.zh: 琬諳政事，其倬章疏文檄每與商榷。

translations.literal: Wan understood state affairs; Qipei's memorials and proclamations she often discussed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan understood government affairs; Qipei often discussed his memorials and proclamations with her.

sentences.zh: 能詩，有蘊真軒詩鈔。

translations.literal: She could compose poetry; her collection was Yunzhen Xuan Poems.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote poetry; her collection was the Yunzhen Xuan Poems.

sentences.zh: 集中辰龍關、關鎖嶺、江西坡、九峰寺諸篇，追懷其父戰績，尤悲壯，為世傳誦。

translations.literal: In the collection pieces on Chenlong Pass, Guansuo Ridge, Jiangxi Slope, and Jiufeng Temple—commemorating her father's battle honors—are especially moving, widely recited.
translations.idiomatic: Among her poems, those on Chenlong Pass, Guansuo Ridge, Jiangxi Slope, and Jiufeng Temple, commemorating her father's campaigns, are especially stirring and widely recited.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間，鐵保錄滿洲、蒙古、漢軍旗人詩，為熙朝雅頌集，以琬為餘集首。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing Tie Bao collected Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner poetry as Elegant Odes of the Glorious Dynasty, placing Wan first in the supplement.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaqing era Tie Bao collected poetry by Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banner writers in the Elegant Odes of the Glorious Dynasty, placing Wan first in the supplement.

sentences.zh: 同入選者，珠亮妻、嵩山妻皆宗室女。

translations.literal: Also selected: wives of Zhuliang and Songshan, both Imperial Clan daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Also chosen were the wives of Zhuliang and Songshan, both daughters of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 張宗仁妻高，名景芳，詩最多。

translations.literal: Gao Jingfang, wife of Zhang Zongren—most prolific in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jingfang, wife of Zhang Zongren, was the most prolific poet among them.

sentences.zh: 珠亮妻有養易齋詩，嵩山妻有蘭軒詩，景芳有紅雪軒詩。

translations.literal: Zhuliang's wife had Yangyi Zhai Poems, Songshan's wife Orchid Pavilion Poems, Jingfang Scarlet Snow Pavilion Poems.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuliang's wife wrote the Yangyi Zhai Poems, Songshan's wife the Orchid Pavilion Poems, and Jingfang the Scarlet Snow Pavilion Poems.

sentences.zh: 陳之遴妻徐，名燦，字明霞，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Xu, wife of Chen Zhipin—named Can, styled Mingxia, of Wuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Can, wife of Chen Zhipin, styled Mingxia, was from Wuxian.

sentences.zh: 之遴自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhipin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhipin has his own biography elsewhere in these annals.

sentences.zh: 徐通書史，之遴得罪，再遣戍，徐從出塞。

translations.literal: Xu mastered books and histories; Zhipin offended and was exiled twice—Xu followed beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was versed in history and the classics. When Zhipin fell from favor and was exiled a second time, Xu followed him beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 之遴死戍所，諸子亦皆歿。

translations.literal: Zhipin died at the place of exile; all sons also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhipin died in exile, and all their sons perished as well.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，聖祖東巡，徐跪道旁自陳。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor toured east; Xu knelt by the road to plead her case.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Kangxi reign the Emperor toured the east. Xu knelt by the roadside to plead her case.

sentences.zh: 上問：「寧有冤乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "Is there injustice?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "Is there injustice in your case?"

sentences.zh: 」徐曰：「先臣惟知思過，豈敢言冤？

translations.literal: " Xu said: "My late husband knew only to reflect on his faults—how dare we speak of injustice?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "My late husband knew only to reflect on his faults. How dare we speak of injustice?"

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖上覆載之仁，許先臣歸骨。

translations.literal: We humbly beg Your Majesty's heaven-and-earth benevolence to permit my late husband's bones to return home.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg Your Majesty's heaven-enfolding mercy to permit my late husband's remains to return home for burial.

sentences.zh: 」上即命還葬。

translations.literal: " The Emperor at once ordered his remains brought back for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at once ordered his remains brought home for burial.

sentences.zh: 徐晚學佛，更號紫{言}，有拙政園詩詞集。

translations.literal: In her later years Xu studied Buddhism, changed her style to Ziyan, and had the Zhuzheng Garden Collection of Poetry and Lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: In her later years Xu turned to Buddhism, took the style name Ziyan, and left the Zhuzheng Garden Collection of Poetry and Lyrics.

sentences.zh: 詞尤工，陳維崧推為南宋後閨秀第一。

translations.literal: Her lyrics were especially accomplished; Chen Weisong ranked her first among talented women since the Southern Song.
translations.idiomatic: Her ci lyrics were especially accomplished; Chen Weisong hailed her as the foremost woman poet since the Southern Song.

sentences.zh: 畫得北宋法。

translations.literal: In painting she mastered Northern Song methods.
translations.idiomatic: In painting she mastered the methods of the Northern Song masters.

sentences.zh: 詹枚妻王，名貞儀，字德卿。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Zhan Mei—named Zhenyi, styled Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenyi, wife of Zhan Mei, styled Deqing.

sentences.zh: 枚，無為人；

translations.literal: Mei was a native of Wuwei;
translations.idiomatic: Mei was from Wuwei;

sentences.zh: 貞儀，泗州人，而家江寧，祖者輔，官宣化知府，坐事戍吉林，貞儀年十一。

translations.literal: Zhenyi was from Sizhou but her family lived in Jiangning; her grandfather Zhe Fu had served as prefect of Xuanhua and, implicated in a case, was exiled to Jilin when Zhenyi was eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyi was from Sizhou, though her family resided in Jiangning. Her grandfather Zhe Fu, who had served as prefect of Xuanhua, was punished and exiled to Jilin when Zhenyi was eleven.

sentences.zh: 者輔卒戍所，從父錫琛奔喪，因僑居吉林，侍祖母董，讀書學騎射。

translations.literal: When Zhe Fu died at the place of exile, her father's younger brother Xi Chen went to mourn and so they sojourned in Jilin; she attended her grandmother Dong, studying books and learning horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhe Fu died in exile, her uncle Xi Chen went to perform the funeral rites, and the family remained in Jilin. Zhenyi attended her grandmother Dong, studying the classics and learning riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 十六還江南，又從錫琛客京師，轉徙陝西、湖北、廣東，二十五歸於枚。

translations.literal: At sixteen she returned south of the Yangtze; she again followed Xi Chen as a guest in the capital, moving on through Shaanxi, Hubei, and Guangdong, and at twenty-five married Mei.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen she returned to the south. She again accompanied Xi Chen to the capital as his dependent, later moving through Shaanxi, Hubei, and Guangdong, and at twenty-five she married Mei.

sentences.zh: 後五年，嘉慶二年，卒。

translations.literal: Five years later, in the second year of the Jiaqing reign, she died.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, in the second year of the Jiaqing reign (1797), she died.

sentences.zh: 貞儀通天算之學，能測星象，旁及壬遁，且知醫。

translations.literal: Zhenyi penetrated the learning of celestial calculation, could observe stars and omens, and also studied renchen divination and medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyi mastered astronomy and mathematical astronomy, could observe the stars, and also studied renchen divination and medicine.

sentences.zh: 為詩文皆質實說事理，不為藻採。

translations.literal: Her poetry and prose were all plain and factual in stating matters, without ornamental flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Her poetry and prose were plain and factual, setting forth real matters without ornamental flourish.

sentences.zh: 撰星像圖釋二卷，曆算簡存五卷，籌算易知、重訂策算證訛、西洋籌算增刪，皆一卷，像數窺餘四卷，女蒙拾誦、沈痾囈語，皆一卷，繡紩餘箋、文選詩賦參評，皆十卷，德風亭集二十卷。

translations.literal: She wrote Explanations of Star Charts in two juan, Brief Preserved Notes on Calendar Calculation in five juan, Easy Introduction to Rod Calculation, Revised Collated Rod Calculation with Errors Corrected, and Additions and Deletions to Western Rod Calculation, each one juan, Glimpses of Image-Number Studies in four juan, Selected Chants for Girls' Education and Delirious Words in Deep Illness, each one juan, Embroidered Loom: Remaining Annotations and Critical Commentary on Wen Xuan Poetry and Fu, each ten juan, and Defeng Pavilion Collected Works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: She authored Explanations of Star Charts (2 juan), Brief Preserved Notes on Calendar Calculation (5 juan), Easy Introduction to Rod Calculation, Revised Collated Rod Calculation with Errors Corrected, and Additions and Deletions to Western Rod Calculation (each 1 juan), Glimpses of Image-Number Studies (4 juan), Selected Chants for Girls' Education and Delirious Words in Deep Illness (each 1 juan), Embroidered Loom: Remaining Annotations and Critical Commentary on Wen Xuan Poetry and Fu (each 10 juan), and Defeng Pavilion Collected Works (20 juan).

sentences.zh: 貞儀病且死，謂枚曰：「君門祚薄，無可為者。

translations.literal: When Zhenyi was ill and near death she said to Mei: "Your family's fortunes are meager; there is nothing to be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyi fell gravely ill and faced death, she told Mei, "Your family's fortunes are slender; there is little to be done.

sentences.zh: 我先君死，不為不幸。

translations.literal: That I die before you is no misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: That I die before you is no misfortune.

sentences.zh: 平生手稿，為我盡致蒯夫人，蒯夫人能彰我。

translations.literal: Take all my lifelong manuscripts and deliver them fully to Lady Kuai; Lady Kuai can make me known.
translations.idiomatic: Take all my lifelong manuscripts and deliver them in full to Lady Kuai—she can bring my work to light.

sentences.zh: 」蒯夫人者，吳江蒯嘉珍妻錢，附見曾伯母錢綸光妻陳傳中，時僑居江寧，貞儀與相習，枚以貞儀書歸焉。

translations.literal: " Lady Kuai was Qian, wife of Kuai Jiazhen of Wujiang, mentioned in the biography of Chen, wife of Qian Lunguang, her husband's grand-aunt; she was then sojourning in Jiangning. Zhenyi was on familiar terms with her, and Mei entrusted Zhenyi's books to her.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Kuai was Qian, wife of Kuai Jiazhen of Wujiang, who appears in the biography of Chen, wife of Qian Lunguang—the husband's grand-aunt by marriage. She was then living in Jiangning. Zhenyi knew her well, and Mei sent Zhenyi's manuscripts to her.

sentences.zh: 錢侄儀吉，為曆算簡存序，言：「貞儀有實學，不可沒，班惠姬後一人而已。

translations.literal: Qian's nephew Yiji wrote a preface to Brief Preserved Notes on Calendar Calculation, saying: "Zhenyi possessed real learning and must not be forgotten—since Ban Zhao there has been only one such as she.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's nephew Yiji wrote a preface to Brief Preserved Notes on Calendar Calculation, saying, "Zhenyi possessed genuine learning and must not be forgotten. Since Ban Zhao there has been only one such as she.

sentences.zh: 」女子治曆算蓋至鮮。

translations.literal: " Women who pursued calendar calculation were exceedingly rare.
translations.idiomatic: " Women who mastered calendar calculation have been exceedingly rare.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，膠州柯蘅妻李，名長霞，邃於選學，著文選詳校八卷。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng era, Li, wife of Ke Heng of Jiaozhou—named Changxia—was profound in Wen Xuan studies and wrote Detailed Collation of the Wen Xuan in eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era, Li Changxia, wife of Ke Heng of Jiaozhou, was deeply versed in Wen Xuan scholarship and wrote Detailed Collation of the Wen Xuan in eight juan.

sentences.zh: 工詩，有錡齋詩集。

translations.literal: She was skilled in poetry and had the Qizhai Collected Poems.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in poetry and left the Qizhai Collected Poems.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，濟陽艾​​紫東妻徐，名桂馨，治音韻之學，有切韻指南四卷。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu era, Xu, wife of Ai Zidong of Jiyang—named Guixin—studied phonology and had Guide to the Qieyun in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu era, Xu Guixin, wife of Ai Zidong of Jiyang, studied phonology and wrote Guide to the Qieyun in four juan.

sentences.zh: 郝懿行妻王，名照圓，字瑞玉，一字婉佺，福山人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Hao Yixing—named Zhaoyuan, styled Ruiyu, also styled Wanquan, of Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhaoyuan, wife of Hao Yixing, styled Ruiyu and also Wanquan, was from Fushan.

sentences.zh: 懿行見儒林傳。

translations.literal: Yixing appears in the Biographies of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing has his own entry in the Biographies of Scholars.

sentences.zh: 照圓文辭高曠，得六朝人遺意。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan's writing was lofty and expansive, catching the lingering spirit of the Six Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan's prose was lofty and expansive, catching something of the spirit of the Six Dynasties writers.

sentences.zh: 懿行有所述作，照圓每為寫定題識。

translations.literal: Whenever Yixing produced a work, Zhaoyuan would fair-copy it and write the colophon.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yixing completed a work, Zhaoyuan would fair-copy it and add the colophon.

sentences.zh: 其所自為書有列女傳補註八卷，序曰：「列女傳補註者，補曹大家註也。

translations.literal: Among her own books was Supplementary Commentary on the Biographies of Exemplary Women in eight juan. Her preface says: "Supplementary Commentary on the Biographies of Exemplary Women supplements the commentary of Lady Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Among her own works was Supplementary Commentary on the Biographies of Exemplary Women in eight juan. Her preface reads, "This Supplementary Commentary supplements the commentary of Lady Cao Ban.

sentences.zh: 照圓六歲而孤，母林夫人恩勤鞠育，教以讀書。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan was orphaned at six; her mother, Lady Lin, nurtured her with tireless kindness and taught her to read.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan lost her father at six. Her mother, Lady Lin, raised her with tireless devotion and taught her to read.

sentences.zh: 嘗從燕間，顧照圓而命之曰：'昔班氏註列女傳十五卷，今其書亡，如能補為之註，是餘所望於汝也。

translations.literal: Once in a leisurely moment she turned to Zhaoyuan and charged her: 'In former times the Ban family annotated the Biographies of Exemplary Women in fifteen juan; that book is now lost. If you can restore and annotate it, that is what I hope of you.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in a quiet moment at leisure, she turned to Zhaoyuan and said, "Long ago the Ban family annotated the Biographies of Exemplary Women in fifteen juan; that book is now lost. If you can restore and complete its commentary, that is what I ask of you.

sentences.zh: '照圓謹誌之不敢忘。

translations.literal: ' Zhaoyuan carefully recorded this and dared not forget.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoyuan recorded this carefully and never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 分陰遄邁，奄忽四七，寸草盟心，遂成銜卹。

translations.literal: Moments fled swiftly; suddenly she reached twenty-eight; with a blade of grass she pledged her heart, and grief for her mother took hold.
translations.idiomatic: The days flew by; before she knew it she was twenty-eight. With the humblest offering she had pledged her heart, and now she bore the weight of mourning.

sentences.zh: 追省前言，隕越滋懼。

translations.literal: Recalling her mother's earlier words, she was ever more fearful of falling short.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling her mother's charge, she feared more than ever that she might fall short.

sentences.zh: 不揣愚蒙，略依先師之詁，用達作者之意，凡所詮釋，將以通其隱滯，取供吟諷。

translations.literal: Not presuming on my dullness, I have followed in part my teachers' glosses to convey the authors' intent; all my explanations aim to clear obscurities for recitation and reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Despite my dullness, I have drawn on my teachers' glosses to convey the authors' intent. My explanations seek only to clear what is obscure, for reading and reflection.

sentences.zh: 至於義所常行，或傳記成文，舊人已註，則皆闕而弗論。

translations.literal: As for duties commonly practiced, or passages already formed in the biographies that earlier commentators have annotated, I leave them all out and do not discuss them.
translations.idiomatic: Where the moral is plain, or where earlier commentators have already glossed a passage, I omit comment altogether.

sentences.zh: 誠知疏陋，無能纂續前修，庶幾念昔先人，少酬明發之懷。

translations.literal: I truly know my work is crude and that I cannot continue the labors of former masters; yet I hope, remembering my late mother, to repay in small measure the charge she spoke at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I know my work is crude and that I cannot match the masters of old; yet I hope, remembering my mother, to repay in some small measure the charge she gave me at dawn.

sentences.zh: 補註成，請夫子辨析疑義，時加訂正，無隱乎爾，竊所慕焉！

translations.literal: When the supplementary commentary is finished, I beg my husband to resolve doubtful points and revise it from time to time without reserve—that is what I privately admire!
translations.idiomatic: When this supplementary commentary is done, I ask my husband to resolve doubtful points and revise it freely from time to time—that openness is what I most admire!

sentences.zh: 又校正列仙傳二卷，舊有贊，考以隋書經籍志，知為晉郭元祖撰，复別出為一卷。

translations.literal: She also collated the Biographies of Immortals in two juan; it had old encomia, and consulting the Sui History Bibliographic Treatise she learned they were by Guo Yuanzu of Jin, so she separated them out as one juan.
