translations.idiomatic: She also collated the Biographies of Immortals in two juan. The old encomia, she found by consulting the Sui History bibliography, were by Guo Yuanzu of Jin; she therefore published them separately in one juan.

sentences.zh: 又集傳記言占夢者為夢書一卷，皆自為序，附懿行書以行。

translations.literal: She also gathered biographical accounts of dream divination into Book of Dreams in one juan, wrote prefaces to all herself, and published them appended to Yixing's works.
translations.idiomatic: She also compiled biographical accounts of dream divination into Book of Dreams in one juan, wrote her own prefaces, and published the work together with Yixing's writings.

sentences.zh: 尤喜言詩，著葩經小記，書未成。

translations.literal: She especially delighted in discussing the Odes and began Notes on the Flowery Classic, but the book was never finished.
translations.idiomatic: She especially loved to discuss the Book of Odes and began Notes on the Flowery Classic, but never completed it.

sentences.zh: 懿行撰詩問，謂與照圓相問答，條其餘義，別為詩說，皆採照圓說為多。

translations.literal: Yixing wrote Inquiries on the Odes, saying he and Zhaoyuan questioned and answered each other, set forth remaining meanings, and separately made Ode Explanations—mostly adopting Zhaoyuan's views.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing wrote Inquiries on the Odes, recording his exchanges with Zhaoyuan, sorting out further meanings and setting them down as separate Ode Explanations—mostly drawn from Zhaoyuan's interpretations.

sentences.zh: 光緒間，其孫聯薇以書進，因誤為照圓著雲。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu era her grandson Lianwei presented the book to the throne, and it was mistakenly taken to be Zhaoyuan's own composition.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu era her grandson Lianwei presented the work at court, and it was mistakenly attributed to Zhaoyuan as author.

sentences.zh: 自照圓為列女傳補注，其後又有汪遠孫妻梁校注。

translations.literal: After Zhaoyuan's Supplementary Commentary on the Biographies of Exemplary Women, Liang, wife of Wang Yuansun, also collated and annotated the text.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaoyuan's Supplementary Commentary, Liang, wife of Wang Yuansun, also produced a collated annotation.

sentences.zh: 梁，名端，字無非，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Liang, named Duan, styled Wufei, of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Duan, styled Wufei, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 幼為祖玉繩所愛。

translations.literal: In childhood she was cherished by her grandfather Yu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: As a child she was cherished by her grandfather Yu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 元和顧之逵校刻列女傳，玉繩為審定，端輒臚其同異，退而筆之，玉繩為之折衷。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Gu Zhi-kui collated and printed the Biographies of Exemplary Women; Yu Sheng revised the edition, and Duan would set forth variant readings, retire and write them down, and Yu Sheng would reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Zhikui collated and printed the Biographies of Exemplary Women, Yu Sheng oversaw the edition. Duan would report variant readings, write them down afterward, and Yu Sheng would adjudicate between them.

sentences.zh: 既歸遠孫，與參酌增損。

translations.literal: After she married Yuansun, they deliberated together on additions and deletions.
translations.idiomatic: After she married Yuansun, they revised the text together, adding and cutting as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 端既卒，遠孫為刻行。

translations.literal: After Duan died, Yuansun had the work carved and published.
translations.idiomatic: After Duan's death, Yuansun had the work printed and published.

sentences.zh: 陳裴之妻汪，名端，字允莊。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Chen Peizhi—named Duan, styled Yunzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duan, wife of Chen Peizhi, styled Yunzhuang.

sentences.zh: 七歲賦春雪詩，擬以謝道韞，因又字小韞，錢塘人。

translations.literal: At seven she composed a poem on spring snow and was likened to Xie Daoyun, hence her additional style Xiaoyun; she was from Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: At seven she wrote a poem on spring snow and was compared to Xie Daoyun, for which reason she also took the style Xiaoyun. She was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 長為

translations.literal: When grown she devoted herself to
translations.idiomatic: When grown she devoted herself to

sentences.zh: 詩，旨遠而辭文，嘗撰定明詩初、二集，上始開國，下逮遺民，都三十家，附錄又七十人。

translations.literal: poetry; her meaning was far-reaching and her diction refined. She once compiled the First and Second Collections of Ming Poetry, from the founding of the dynasty down to loyalist survivors—thirty masters in all, with an appendix of seventy more.
translations.idiomatic: poetry. Her meaning ran deep and her diction was refined. She compiled the First and Second Collections of Ming Poetry, from the dynasty's founding down to the loyalist survivors—thirty principal poets in all, with an appendix of seventy more.

sentences.zh: 自定凡例，以為：「初集，猶主盟之晉、楚；

translations.literal: She set her own principles of selection, saying: "The first collection is like Jin and Chu when they held the hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: She laid down her own principles of selection, writing, "The first collection is like Jin and Chu when they held the hegemony;

sentences.zh: 二集，猶列國之宋、鄭、魯、衛；

translations.literal: the second collection is like the states of Song, Zheng, Lu, and Wei among the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: the second is like Song, Zheng, Lu, and Wei among the feudal states;

sentences.zh: 附錄，猶附庸之邾、莒、杞、薛。

translations.literal: the appendix is like the subordinate states of Zhu, Ju, Qi, and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: the appendix is like the subordinate states of Zhu, Ju, Qi, and Xue.

sentences.zh: 」梁德繩稱其宗尚清蒼雅正，能掃前後七子門徑。

translations.literal: " Liang Desheng praised her adherence to clarity, restraint, and correctness, and her power to sweep away the paths of the earlier and later Seven Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Desheng praised her taste for clarity, restraint, and correctness, and her ability to break free of the mannerisms of the earlier and later Seven Masters schools.

sentences.zh: 吳振棫稱其論一代升降正變，元元本本，縱橫莫當。

translations.literal: Wu Zhenshu praised her discussion of a generation's rise and fall, orthodoxy and change, as thorough and grounded, sweeping and irresistible.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhenshu praised her account of how a whole age rose and fell, of orthodoxy and change, as thorough, grounded, and altogether commanding.

sentences.zh: 端所自為詩，有自然好學齋集。

translations.literal: Among Duan's own poems is the Natural Love of Learning Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Her own poetry survives as the Natural Love of Learning Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 裴之卒，子又有疾，舅文述素奉道，端詩亦多為道家語。

translations.literal: After Peizhi died their son also fell ill; her uncle Wen Shu had long followed the Way, and Duan's poems too are largely in the language of Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: After Peizhi died their son fell ill as well. Her uncle Wen Shu was a lifelong follower of the Way, and much of Duan's later poetry takes the language of Daoism.

sentences.zh: 既卒，諸侄重定其集，盡刪晚作，二本並行於世。

translations.literal: After her death her nephews revised her collection, deleting all her late works; two versions circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: After her death her nephews revised her collected works, removing all her late compositions, and two editions circulated.

sentences.zh: 汪延澤妻趙，名棻，字儀姞。

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of Wang Yanze—named Fen, styled Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fen, wife of Wang Yanze, styled Yiji.

sentences.zh: 延澤，烏程人；

translations.literal: Yanze was a native of Wucheng;
translations.idiomatic: Yanze was from Wucheng;

sentences.zh: 趙，上海人，戶部侍郎秉衝女也。

translations.literal: Zhao was from Shanghai and was the daughter of Bing Chong, vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was from Shanghai, daughter of Bing Chong, vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 幼讀書，能詩文，有濾月軒詩集四卷，文集二卷，詞一卷。

translations.literal: She read from childhood and could write poetry and prose; she had Filtered Moon Studio Collected Poems in four juan, prose in two juan, and lyrics in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: She studied from childhood and wrote poetry and prose. Her works include Filtered Moon Studio Collected Poems (4 juan), prose (2 juan), and lyrics (1 juan).

sentences.zh: 自為序，略曰：「宋後儒者多言文章吟詠非女子所當為，故今世女子能詩者，輒自諱匿，以為吾謹守'內言不出於閫'之禮。

translations.literal: In her own preface she says in brief: "After the Song, Confucian scholars often said that literary composition and chanting were not what women should do, so women today who can write poetry hide it, thinking they are observing the rule that 'a woman's words do not pass beyond the inner gate.'
translations.idiomatic: In her own preface she writes, "Since the Song, scholars have often said that literary composition and verse are not women's proper work. Women who can write poetry therefore hide it, believing they uphold the rule that a woman's words must not pass beyond the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 反是，則迋欺炫鬻於世，以射利焉耳。

translations.literal: The opposite course is to parade and peddle oneself in the world merely to seek profit.
translations.idiomatic: The opposite is to parade and peddle one's talent in the world merely for profit.

sentences.zh: 是二者，胥失之也。

translations.literal: Both courses alike miss the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Both extremes miss the mark.

sentences.zh: 禮昏義女師之教，婦言居德之次，鄭君注云：'婦言，辭令也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Marriage explains the mistress's instruction: woman's speech ranks next to woman's virtue. Master Zheng's commentary says: 'Woman's speech means command of language.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Marriage teaches that a woman's speech ranks next to her virtue. Zheng Xuan's commentary says, "A woman's speech means command of language.

sentences.zh: '夫言之不文，行而不遠，文章吟詠，非言辭之遠鄙倍者歟？

translations.literal: ' If words lack refinement they do not travel far—are not literary composition and chanting the farthest reach of eloquent speech?
translations.idiomatic: " If words lack refinement they do not travel far. Are not literary composition and verse the fullest expression of eloquent speech?

sentences.zh: 何屑屑諱匿為！

translations.literal: Why fuss over hiding it!
translations.idiomatic: Why trouble oneself to hide it!

sentences.zh: 子曰楨，撰二十四史日月考，趙為之序，曰：「劉羲叟撰劉氏輯術，迄於五季，書久佚，僅存通鑑目錄。

translations.literal: Her son Zhen wrote Investigation of Dates in the Twenty-Four Histories, and Zhao wrote its preface, saying: "Liu Yisou compiled the Liu Clan Chronological Arts, reaching down to the Five Dynasties; the book has long been lost, surviving only in the Comprehensive Mirror catalogue.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Zhen wrote Investigation of Dates in the Twenty-Four Histories. Zhao wrote its preface, saying, "Liu Yisou compiled the Liu Clan Chronological Arts down to the Five Dynasties period. That book has long been lost, surviving only in the catalogue of the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 自宋迨明，六百餘年，未有續為之者。

translations.literal: From the Song through the Ming, more than six hundred years, no one has continued the work.
translations.idiomatic: From the Song through the Ming—more than six hundred years—no one has continued it.

sentences.zh: 曰楨好史學，習算，考當時行用本術，如法推步，得其朔閏。

translations.literal: Zhen loves historical studies and has practiced calculation; examining the calendrical methods then in use, he has computed by rule and obtained new and intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen loves historical studies and has mastered calculation. Working from the calendrical methods then in official use, he has computed by rule and determined the new and intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 自史記至新、舊唐書，屬草已一百餘卷，餘亟欲睹其成，預為此序，俾寫定冠諸簡端。

translations.literal: From the Records of the Historian through the New and Old Books of Tang, his draft already exceeds one hundred juan. I am eager to see it completed and write this preface in advance, that it may be fair-copied and placed at the head of the bamboo slips.
translations.idiomatic: From the Records of the Historian through the New and Old Books of Tang, his draft already runs to more than one hundred juan. I am eager to see it finished and write this preface in advance, to be copied at the head of the work when it is done.

sentences.zh: 吳廷珍妻張，廷珍，常熟人，道光六年進士，官至刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Wu Tingzhen—Tingzhen was a native of Changshu, a jinshi of the sixth year of Daoguang, and rose to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Wu Tingzhen of Changshu, who passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Daoguang (1826) and rose to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 張名䌌英，字孟緹，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Zhang was named Lunying, styled Mengti, of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: She was Zhang Lunying, styled Mengti, from Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 世父惠言，父琦，皆博通能文章。

translations.literal: Her father's elder brother Huaiyan and her father Qi were both broadly learned and accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Zhang Huaiyan and her father Zhang Qi were both broadly learned and accomplished writers.

sentences.zh: 䌌英與諸女弟承其教，咸有述作，皆能詩。

translations.literal: Lunying and her sisters received their instruction, all produced writings, and all could write poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Lunying and her sisters received their instruction, all left writings of their own, and all wrote poetry.

sentences.zh: 䌌英兼為詞，秀逸有王沂中、張炎遺意。

translations.literal: Lunying also wrote lyrics, graceful and unfettered with something of Wang Yizhong and Zhang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lunying also wrote ci lyrics, graceful and unfettered, with something of the spirit of Wang Yizhong and Zhang Yan.

sentences.zh: 妹惸英亦能詩詞；

translations.literal: Her younger sister Qiongying could also write poetry and lyrics;
translations.idiomatic: Her younger sister Qiongying could also write poetry and lyrics;

sentences.zh: 綸英尤工書，傳琦筆法，真書出入歐陽、顏、楊諸家，分書自北碑上溯晉、漢，遒麗沉厚；

translations.literal: Lunyin was especially skilled in calligraphy, inheriting Qi's brush methods; her regular script ranged among the schools of Ouyang, Yan, and Yang, and her clerical script, from Northern Steles back through Jin and Han, was forceful, beautiful, and weighty;
translations.idiomatic: Lunyin was especially accomplished in calligraphy, inheriting her father's brush methods. Her regular script drew on Ouyang, Yan, and Yang; her clerical script, tracing Northern Stele models back through Jin and Han, was forceful, beautiful, and weighty;

sentences.zh: 紈英兼治古文。

translations.literal: Wanying also studied ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: Wanying also studied ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 䌌英嘗編次國朝列女詩錄，紈英為作傳，簡雅合法度。

translations.literal: Lunying once compiled a Record of Exemplary Women's Poetry of Our Dynasty; Wanying wrote the biographies, concise, elegant, and within proper bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Lunying once compiled a Record of Exemplary Women's Poetry of Our Dynasty; Wanying wrote the biographical notices, concise, elegant, and within proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 惸英，江陰章政平妻；

translations.literal: Qiongying was wife of Zhang Zhengping of Jiangyin;
translations.idiomatic: Qiongying married Zhang Zhengping of Jiangyin;

sentences.zh: 綸英，同縣孫劼妻；

translations.literal: Lunyin was wife of Sun Jie of the same county;
translations.idiomatic: Lunyin married Sun Jie of the same county;

sentences.zh: 紈英，太倉王曦妻。

translations.literal: Wanying was wife of Wang Xi of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Wanying married Wang Xi of Taicang.

sentences.zh: 程鼎調妻汪，名嫈，字雅安，歙人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Cheng Dingdiao—named Yin, styled Ya'an, of She county.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, wife of Cheng Dingdiao, styled Ya'an, was from She county.

sentences.zh: 好學，通儒家言，詩文皆雅正。

translations.literal: She loved learning, mastered Confucian discourse, and her poetry and prose were all refined and correct.
translations.idiomatic: She loved learning, was versed in Confucian teaching, and wrote poetry and prose that were refined and correct.

sentences.zh: 病將卒，為詩曰：「秋風一葉落，餘亦歸荒墟。

translations.literal: When she was ill and near death she composed a poem: "An autumn wind blows and one leaf falls; I too return to the wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell gravely ill and faced death, she wrote a poem: "The autumn wind drops a single leaf; I too return to the wasteland.

sentences.zh: 」遺書戒其子葆，言家事至詳。

translations.literal: " She left a testament admonishing her son Bao, setting forth household affairs in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: " She left a final letter admonishing her son Bao, setting forth household affairs in meticulous detail.

sentences.zh: 复謂：「武侯著書，內有八務、七戒、六恐、五懼，武侯第一流人，務一，而戒恐懼居其三，可不識所致力耶！

translations.literal: She also said: "Marquis Wu wrote in his book of eight duties, seven admonitions, six fears, and five dreads. Marquis Wu was a man of the first rank: duties are one, yet admonitions, fears, and dreads make three—should one not know where to apply one's effort!
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote, "Zhuge Liang's book sets forth eight duties, seven admonitions, six fears, and five dreads. He was a man of the first rank: one section on duties, yet three on admonition and fear—should we not know where to fix our effort?"

sentences.zh: 」葆編其所作為雅安書屋詩文集。

translations.literal: " Bao compiled her writings as the Ya'an Studio Collected Poetry and Prose.
translations.idiomatic: Bao compiled her writings as the Ya'an Studio Collected Poetry and Prose.

sentences.zh: 陳瑞妻繆，名嘉蕙，字素筠，昆明人。

translations.literal: Miao, wife of Chen Rui—named Jiahui, styled Suyun, of Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jiahui, wife of Chen Rui, styled Suyun, was from Kunming.

sentences.zh: 工書、善畫。

translations.literal: She was skilled in calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，召入宮供奉，為皇太后嘉賞，特賜三品服。

translations.literal: During the Guangxu era she was summoned to serve in the palace; the Empress Dowager praised her and specially granted her third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu era she was summoned to serve at court. The Empress Dowager praised her work and specially granted her the robes of a third-rank official.

sentences.zh: 時同被召者，馬某妻阮，字蘋香，儀徵人，賜名玉芬。

translations.literal: Those summoned at the same time included Ruan, wife of a certain Ma, styled Pingxiang, of Yizheng, granted the name Yufen.
translations.idiomatic: Those summoned at the same time included Ruan, wife of a certain Ma, styled Pingxiang, from Yizheng, who was granted the name Yufen.

sentences.zh: 富樂賀妻王，名韶，字矞雲，杭州駐防滿洲人，著有冬青館詩。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Fulehe—named Shao, styled Yuyun, a Manchu garrison resident at Hangzhou—authored Winter Green Pavilion Poems.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, wife of Fulehe, styled Yuyun, was a Manchu bannerwoman stationed at Hangzhou and wrote Winter Green Pavilion Poems.

sentences.zh: 仁興妻瓜爾佳氏，名畫梁，亦杭州駐防滿洲人，著有超範室畫範。

translations.literal: A woman of the Guwalgiya clan, wife of Renxing—named Hualiang, also a Manchu garrison resident at Hangzhou—authored Models from the Transcendent Standards Studio.
translations.idiomatic: A Guwalgiya clanswoman, wife of Renxing, named Hualiang, was likewise a Manchu bannerwoman at Hangzhou and wrote Models from the Transcendent Standards Studio.

sentences.zh: 耀州三婦：一青嘉努妻，一納岱妻，一邁圖妻，所居寨曰蕎麥衝，在耀州城南。

translations.literal: The three wives of Yaozhou: the wife of Qingjianu, the wife of Nadai, and the wife of Maitu. Their stockade was called Buckwheat Pass and lay south of Yaozhou city.
translations.idiomatic: The three wives of Yaozhou were the wives of Qingjianu, Nadai, and Maitu. They lived at a stockade called Buckwheat Pass, south of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 天命十年六月癸卯，明將毛文龍遣兵三百夜薄寨，方踰牆入，寨兵未即出，三婦者見之，倚車轅於牆，以為梯，青嘉努妻持利刃先偕登城奮擊，三百人皆驚，墜牆走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Tianming, on guimao, the Ming general Mao Wenlong sent three hundred men to attack the stockade by night. Just as they climbed over the wall to enter, the garrison had not yet sallied forth. The three wives saw them, leaned cart shafts against the wall as a ladder, and Qingjianu's wife, grasping a sharp blade, was first to climb the wall together with them and strike fiercely. All three hundred men were startled and fell from the wall in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianming 10, on the guimao day, Ming general Mao Wenlong sent three hundred troops to storm the stockade at night. As they vaulted the wall, the garrison had not yet rushed out. The three wives spotted them, propped cart shafts against the wall for a ladder, and Qingjianu's wife—blade in hand—was the first up the rampart beside them, fighting with abandon. The three hundred attackers panicked and tumbled back over the wall in retreat.

sentences.zh: 耀州守將揚古利以兵至，追擊，盡殲之。

translations.literal: Yang Guli, the defending general of Yaozhou, arrived with troops, pursued them, and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhou's garrison commander Yang Guli arrived with his force, pursued the raiders, and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 太祖召三婦，賚金、帛、牛、馬，賜青嘉努、納岱妻備禦，邁圖妻千總。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor summoned the three wives, bestowed gold, silk, cattle, and horses, and granted Qingjianu's and Nadai's wives the rank of beiyu; Maitu's wife, the rank of qianzong.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor summoned the three wives and rewarded them with gold, silk, cattle, and horses. He gave Qingjianu's and Nadai's wives the military rank of beiyu, and Maitu's wife the rank of qianzong.

sentences.zh: 杉松郵卒婦，祿勸人，失其姓。

translations.literal: The wife of a postal courier at Shansong, from Luquan, had lost her surname [to record].
translations.idiomatic: The wife of a postal courier at Shansong was a native of Luquan; her surname was not recorded.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年正月，有常應運者為亂，逼杉松，諸郵卒方耕於山，無御者。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, one Chang Yingyun raised rebellion and pressed toward Shansong. The postal couriers were all farming in the hills, with no one to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 57, a rebel named Chang Yingyun rose in revolt and advanced on Shansong. The postal couriers were all farming in the hills; no one was left to defend the place.

sentences.zh: 婦曰：「此可計走也。

translations.literal: The wife said, "This can be made to drive them off."
translations.idiomatic: The wife said, "We can devise a way to make them retreat."

sentences.zh: 」挾鉦鳴山巔，若且集眾，賊引去，婦乃走告夫，州始為備。

translations.literal: " She took a gong to the mountain crest and struck it, as though mustering a crowd. The bandits withdrew; the wife then ran to tell her husband, and only then did the prefecture make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: She carried a gong to the mountaintop and beat it as if rallying a host. The rebels withdrew. She then ran to tell her husband, and the prefecture at last took defensive measures.

sentences.zh: 事定，知州李廷宰聚父老賚婦酒食，具鼓吹，簪勝披錦，以矜於市民。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Prefect Li Tingzai gathered the elders to present the wife with food and wine, set out drums and wind instruments, pinned victory flowers and draped her in brocade, and displayed her before the townspeople in honor.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored, Prefect Li Tingzai assembled the elders to reward the wife with food and wine. With drums and pipes sounding, victory flowers in her hair and brocade over her shoulders, she was paraded before the townspeople in public acclaim.

sentences.zh: 楊芳妻龍，芳，松桃廳人；

translations.literal: Long, wife of Yang Fang—Fang was a native of Songtao Subprefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Long, wife of Yang Fang: Fang was from Songtao Subprefecture;

sentences.zh: 龍，華陽人。

translations.literal: Long was a native of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Long came from Huayang.

sentences.zh: 芳有傳。

translations.literal: Fang has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fang has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 龍善鼓琴，工畫蘭。

translations.literal: Long was skilled at playing the qin and adept at painting orchids.
translations.idiomatic: Long was accomplished on the qin and skilled at painting orchids.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，芳自寧陝鎮總兵署固原提督，龍留寧陝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing, Fang went from General of Ningshan Garrison to Garrison Commander of Guyuan; Long remained at Ningshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 11, Fang was promoted from commander of the Ningshan garrison to provincial military commander of Guyuan, while Long stayed behind at Ningshan.

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，鎮兵以餉不給，將叛。

translations.literal: That autumn, the garrison troops, because pay was not issued, were about to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, the garrison troops, unpaid, were on the verge of mutiny.

sentences.zh: 龍使告署總兵楊之震，之震不之省。

translations.literal: Long sent someone to inform Acting General Yang Zhizhen; Zhizhen paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Long sent word to Acting General Yang Zhizhen, but he ignored the warning.

sentences.zh: 或請龍行避亂，龍曰：「不可，若我出而兵叛，是知其叛也，人其謂我何？

translations.literal: Some urged Long to flee and avoid the turmoil. Long said, "I cannot. If I leave and the troops then rebel, it will show I knew they meant to rebel—what will people say of me?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Long to flee the unrest. She refused: "I cannot. If I leave and the troops rebel, everyone will know I foresaw it—what would they think of me?

sentences.zh: 」七月辛亥夕，亂作，芳素得兵心，兵有以匪降者，尤感芳不殺，皆入署為龍衛。

translations.literal: " On the xinhai night of the seventh month the disturbance broke out. Fang had long won the soldiers' hearts; among the troops were men who had surrendered as bandits and were especially grateful that Fang had spared them—they all entered the yamen to guard Long.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai night of the seventh month, the mutiny erupted. Fang had always held the soldiers' trust; some in the ranks were former bandits who had surrendered and especially remembered that he had spared their lives. They all filed into the yamen to protect Long.

sentences.zh: 民婦就避兵，廊廡盈焉。

translations.literal: Townswomen came to seek refuge from the fighting, and the corridors were packed full.
translations.idiomatic: Local women crowded into the compound seeking shelter from the fighting; corridors and cloisters overflowed.

sentences.zh: 龍嚴戒奴婢毋號泣，鄉明，叛兵叩閤請謁，諸避兵者忷懼，請毋納。

translations.literal: Long strictly forbade the servants to wail. At dawn the next day, the rebels knocked at the gate requesting an audience. Those sheltering within panicked and begged her not to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Long sternly ordered the servants not to weep. At dawn, rebel leaders knocked at the gate to pay their respects. The frightened refugees pleaded that she refuse them entry.

sentences.zh: 龍曰：「愚哉！

translations.literal: Long said, "How foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "Fools!

sentences.zh: 彼輩且自入，孰能御之？

translations.literal: Those men will enter of themselves—who can stop them?
translations.idiomatic: They will force their way in—who can keep them out?

sentences.zh: 」乃啟門，納其渠數十人，咸泣謝，且請龍行。

translations.literal: " She then opened the gate and admitted several dozen of their ringleaders. All wept and apologized, and also begged Long to depart.
translations.idiomatic: She opened the gate and admitted several dozen rebel leaders. They wept and apologized, then begged her to leave with them.

sentences.zh: 龍謂之曰：「若曹雖叛戕官，其渠罪不逭，於多人何尤？

translations.literal: Long said to them, "Though you have rebelled and killed officials, the ringleaders cannot escape punishment—what blame lies on the many?
translations.idiomatic: She told them, "You rebelled and killed officials; the leaders cannot escape justice—what guilt do the rank and file bear?

sentences.zh: 主將旦夕歸，白若曹於朝，非盡殲也，可各罷歸伍。

translations.literal: The commander will return shortly. I shall report your case to the court—it need not mean total extermination. You may each disband and return to your units."
translations.idiomatic: Your commander will return soon. I will plead your case to the court; you need not be wiped out to a man. Each of you may stand down and return to your posts."

sentences.zh: 」叛兵不欲罷，堅請龍行，龍命以輿來，盡出諸避難者，而殿其後。

translations.literal: The rebels did not wish to disband and pressed her to go. Long ordered a palanquin brought, sent out all who had taken refuge, and brought up the rear herself.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers refused to disperse and insisted she accompany them. Long had a sedan chair brought, evacuated everyone who had sought shelter, and marched at the rear herself.

sentences.zh: 叛兵送至清澗，哭而返。

translations.literal: The rebels escorted her as far as Qingjian, weeping as they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels escorted her to Qingjian, weeping as they turned back.

sentences.zh: 龍兄為興安知府，乃之興安。

translations.literal: Long's elder brother was prefect of Xing'an, so she went to Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother served as prefect of Xing'an, and she went to join him there.

sentences.zh: 芳自固原至，撫叛兵，复定。

translations.literal: Fang came from Guyuan, pacified the rebels, and restored order.
translations.idiomatic: Fang returned from Guyuan, pacified the mutineers, and restored calm.

sentences.zh: 蒲大芳者，叛兵渠也，請於芳，迎龍歸。

translations.literal: Pu Dafang was the rebels' ringleader; he asked Fang to welcome Long back.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Dafang, leader of the mutiny, petitioned Fang to bring Long home.

sentences.zh: 芳遣大芳等二十輩以往，龍初舉子，即冒雪就道，道中大芳與其曹詬爭，舉刀傷其曹。

translations.literal: Fang sent Dafang and twenty others to escort her. Long had just given birth; still, she set out through the snow. On the road Dafang quarreled with his companions and raised a blade, wounding one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sent Dafang and twenty men to fetch her. Long had only just borne a son, yet she set out at once through the snow. On the road Dafang quarreled with his companions and struck one with his blade.

sentences.zh: 行至漢陰，龍使假刑具於有司，召大芳責曰：「汝叛，幸不死，更弄刀杖，又待叛耶？

translations.literal: When they reached Hanyin, Long had punitive gear borrowed from the authorities, summoned Dafang, and rebuked him: "You rebelled and by fortune were not put to death—yet you ply blades again. Do you mean to rebel once more?
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Hanyin, she borrowed punishment gear from the local office, summoned Dafang, and rebuked him: "You rebelled and were spared—now you brandish weapons again. Are you plotting another mutiny?

sentences.zh: 」杖之四十，械而行。

translations.literal: " She had him flogged forty strokes and sent him on in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: She had him beaten forty blows and marched him on in shackles.

sentences.zh: 三日，將至寧陝，其曹十九人者為之請，乃令脫械。

translations.literal: After three days, as they neared Ningshan, the other nineteen men pleaded for him, and she ordered the fetters removed.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, nearing Ningshan, the other nineteen men interceded for him, and she ordered the shackles struck off.

sentences.zh: 龍至，語芳曰：「事雖事，然君且有遠行。

translations.literal: When Long arrived she told Fang, "The affair is settled as an affair, yet you are soon to travel far."
translations.idiomatic: On her arrival she told Fang, "The crisis has passed, but you are bound for exile far away."

sentences.zh: 」芳曰：「何至是？

translations.literal: Fang said, "How could it come to that?
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "Surely it will not come to that—

sentences.zh: 」龍曰：「朝廷自有法度，兵叛事大，不容無任其咎者。

translations.literal: " Long said, "The court has its laws. A troop mutiny is a grave matter—it cannot go without someone bearing the blame."
translations.idiomatic: she replied. "The court has its laws. A mutiny of this scale cannot pass without someone held accountable."

sentences.zh: 」果有命戍伊犁。

translations.literal: An order indeed came assigning him to garrison duty in Yili.
translations.idiomatic: An order came indeed: he was banished to garrison duty in Yili.

sentences.zh: 龍歸侍姑，姑風緩不能言，惟龍達其意，左右在視。

translations.literal: Long returned to wait on her mother-in-law. The old woman was paralyzed and could not speak; only Long understood her wishes, while attendants stood by to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Long returned to nurse her mother-in-law, who was paralyzed and speechless. Only Long could read her wishes; attendants stood by at every hour.

sentences.zh: 居姑喪盡禮。

translations.literal: In mourning for her mother-in-law she observed every rite.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died, she observed the mourning rites to the letter.

sentences.zh: 芳復起，遷湖南提督，道光五年，龍卒。

translations.literal: Fang was restored to office and promoted to Hunan provincial commander. In the fifth year of Daoguang, Long died.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was reinstated and promoted to provincial military commander of Hunan. In Daoguang 5, Long died.

sentences.zh: 崔龍見妻錢，名孟鈿，字冠之，一字浣青。

translations.literal: Qian, wife of Cui Longjian—given name Mengtian, courtesy name Guanzhi, also styled Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, wife of Cui Longjian: her given name was Mengtian, her courtesy name Guanzhi, and she also used the style Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 龍見，永濟人；

translations.literal: Longjian was a native of Yongji;
translations.idiomatic: Longjian was from Yongji;

sentences.zh: 錢，武進人，侍郎維城女。

translations.literal: Qian was a native of Wujin, daughter of Vice Minister Qian Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was from Wujin, daughter of Vice Minister Qian Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 九歲刲臂療父疾。

translations.literal: At nine she sliced her arm to treat her father's illness.
translations.idiomatic: At nine she cut her own arm to heal her father's illness.

sentences.zh: 歸龍見，事姑謹，龍見以進士官州縣，為四川順慶知府。

translations.literal: Married to Longjian, she served her mother-in-law diligently. Longjian rose through the jinshi path to office in prefectures and counties and became prefect of Shunqing in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After marrying Longjian she served her mother-in-law with scrupulous care. Longjian advanced through the examination system to county and prefectural posts and became prefect of Shunqing in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 川東啯匪為亂，龍見師出禦，賊自間道來襲，吏民驚擾。

translations.literal: Gelaohui bandits rebelled in eastern Sichuan. Longjian led his troops out to resist; the bandits came by a bypath to attack, and officials and people were thrown into panic.
translations.idiomatic: Gelaohui rebels rose in eastern Sichuan. Longjian marched out against them, but the rebels struck by a hidden route and threw officials and townspeople into panic.

sentences.zh: 錢诇賊自府西至，遣人掣渡舟泊東岸。

translations.literal: Qian detected that the bandits were coming from west of the prefectural seat and sent men to pull the ferry boats to moor on the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: Qian learned the rebels were approaching from west of the city and sent men to haul the ferryboats to the east bank.

sentences.zh: 賊至，不得渡，遂引去。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived they could not cross and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels arrived, found the river uncrossable, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及為湖北荊宜施道，值白蓮教匪為亂，龍見出督餉，錢居危城中，烽火四偪，以龍見指發書，戒所屬州縣，令收附郭積聚，謹守備，毋與賊浪戰。

translations.literal: When he became Intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei, the White Lotus sect rebels rose in disorder. Longjian went out to oversee supplies; Qian remained in the endangered city with beacon fires pressing on every side. With Longjian's finger she dispatched letters, warning subordinate prefectures and counties to gather grain stored outside their walls, tighten defenses, and not join the bandits in reckless battle.
translations.idiomatic: As intendant of the Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei, he faced the White Lotus rebellion. Longjian went out to supervise grain transport while Qian remained in the besieged city, beacon fires closing in on every side. Writing in his hand, she issued orders to subordinate counties: concentrate stores from the suburbs, fortify defenses, and do not engage the rebels rashly.

sentences.zh: 賊偵有備，亦引去。

translations.literal: The bandits, finding preparations in place, also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the defenses ready, the rebels withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 龍見在官廉，錢每出餘財週戚黨。

translations.literal: Longjian was upright in office; Qian often took surplus funds to assist kin and allies.
translations.idiomatic: Longjian served with integrity; Qian often used their surplus income to aid relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 自四川還，泊燕子磯，見渡舟覆溺，出錢募救者，活十餘人，皆應試士也，羅拜岸上。

translations.literal: Returning from Sichuan they moored at Yanziji, saw a ferry capsize and drown its passengers, paid out money to recruit rescuers, and saved more than ten men—all examination candidates—who bowed in a ring on the bank.
translations.idiomatic: On their return from Sichuan they stopped at Yanziji and saw a ferry overturn. She paid to hire rescuers and saved more than ten candidates for the civil examinations, who lined the bank bowing in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 龍見卒，教諸子成立。

translations.literal: When Longjian died, she educated her sons until they were established.
translations.idiomatic: After Longjian's death she raised their sons to maturity and standing.

sentences.zh: 錢工詩詞，即以「浣青」名其集。

translations.literal: Qian was accomplished in poetry and lyric; she named her collected works "Huanqing."
translations.idiomatic: Qian was accomplished in poetry and named her collected works Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 沈葆楨妻林，名普晴，字敬紉，侯官人，雲貴總督則徐女也。

translations.literal: Lin, wife of Shen Baozhen—given name Puqing, courtesy name Jingren, a native of Houguan, daughter of Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Lin Zexu.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, wife of Shen Baozhen: her given name was Puqing, courtesy name Jingren. She was from Houguan and daughter of Governor-General Lin Zexu of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 則徐、葆楨皆有傳。

translations.literal: Both Zexu and Baozhen have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Both Lin Zexu and Shen Baozhen have biographies elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 葆楨故則徐甥，林六七歲時，嘗侍諸姑坐，臧否戚黨諸子弟。

translations.literal: Baozhen was formerly Zexu's nephew by marriage. When Lin was six or seven she would attend her aunts as they sat in judgment on the young men of their kin, praising and blaming.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was Zexu's nephew by marriage. When Lin was six or seven she would sit with her aunts as they appraised the young men of the clan.

sentences.zh: 戲以諮林，輒曰：「無逾沈氏兄賢。

translations.literal: In jest they would ask Lin, and she would always say, "None surpasses elder brother Shen in worth.
translations.idiomatic: Teasing, they asked her opinion, and she always said, "None surpasses Cousin Shen.

sentences.zh: 」及歸葆楨，葆楨貧，董中廚，斥奩具佐饈，能得姑歡。

translations.literal: " When she married Baozhen he was poor; she oversaw the central kitchen, selling bridal chest goods to supplement provisions, and won her mother-in-law's affection.
translations.idiomatic: When she married Baozhen he was still poor. She ran the household kitchen, sold items from her dowry chest to help with meals, and won her mother-in-law's favor.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，葆楨知廣信府，八月，出行縣，洪秀全將楊輔清自吉安潛師越山谷入。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, Baozhen was prefect of Guangxin. In the eighth month he went out to tour the counties; Hong Xiuquan's general Yang Fuqing secretly led troops over the mountain passes from Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 6, Baozhen served as prefect of Guangxin. In the eighth month he left on a county tour while Hong Xiuquan's general Yang Fuqing stole over the hills from Ji'an with hidden troops.

sentences.zh: 戊子，破貴溪，己丑，破弋陽。

translations.literal: On wuzi he took Guiqi; on jichou, Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the rebels seized Guiqi; on jichou, Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 吏具舟促林避寇，林勿行。

translations.literal: Officials prepared boats urging Lin to flee the bandits; Lin would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Officials arranged boats and urged Lin to flee the rebels; she refused.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，葆楨還，時遵義鎮總兵饒廷選駐軍玉山，乃為書乞援，而輔清兵益進，去廣信八十里。

translations.literal: On gengyin Baozhen returned. At the time Zunyi garrison commander Rao Tingxuan was encamped at Yushan; he wrote a letter begging aid, while Fuqing's troops pressed closer—eighty li from Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Baozhen returned. Rao Tingxuan, general of the Zunyi garrison, was stationed at Yushan; Baozhen wrote begging relief even as Fuqing's army advanced to within eighty li of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，廷選報書，言水涸，師不得下。

translations.literal: On xinmao Tingxuan replied that the rivers were dry and his troops could not descend.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Tingxuan replied that low water blocked his march.

sentences.zh: 僕役散走，林懷印倚井坐誓死。

translations.literal: Servants scattered and fled; Lin clasped the official seal, sat leaning against a well, and vowed to die.
translations.idiomatic: Servants fled in all directions. Lin clutched the official seal, seated herself by a well, and vowed to die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 乙夜，城南火，達曙，大雨火滅。

translations.literal: In the second watch fire broke out south of the city; by dawn a great rain extinguished it.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch fire blazed south of the walls; at dawn a downpour put the flames out.

sentences.zh: 林謂葆楨曰：「城中炊煙斷，火何由起？

translations.literal: Lin said to Baozhen, "Cooking smoke in the city has ceased—how could a fire arise?
translations.idiomatic: Lin said to Baozhen, "No cookfires smoke within the walls—how could a fire spring up?

sentences.zh: 此賊諜所為，以空城告也。

translations.literal: This is the work of rebel spies, reporting the city empty."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels' spies did this to signal that the city is abandoned."

sentences.zh: 今日賊當至，吾殉君固其所。

translations.literal: Today the bandits will come; to die with you is only fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels will come today; to die at your side is only right."

sentences.zh: 」解劍授葆楨曰：「雨甚，吾不可露坐，賊至，君以劍當之，使吾倉卒得入井也。

translations.literal: " She unbuckled her sword and handed it to Baozhen, saying, "The rain is heavy—I cannot sit exposed in the open. When the bandits come, hold them off with the sword so I may at once drop into the well."
translations.idiomatic: She drew her sword and gave it to him: "The rain is fierce; I cannot sit in the open. When they come, use this blade to hold them off so I can throw myself into the well in time."

sentences.zh: 」賊得諜，知城無人，易之，待霽乃發。

translations.literal: The bandits received the spy's report, knew the city was undefended, took the matter lightly, and waited for clear weather before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels learned from their spy that the city stood empty, grew careless, and waited for fair weather before moving.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，輔清兵復進四十里，而廷選師至，葆楨徒步迎以入。

translations.literal: On guisi Fuqing's troops advanced another forty li, but Tingxuan's army arrived; Baozhen went out on foot to welcome them in.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Fuqing's force pressed another forty li, then Tingxuan's troops arrived; Baozhen went out on foot to meet them and led them in.

sentences.zh: 甲午，輔清兵薄城，廷選軍出禦，其裨將畢定邦、賴高翔戰甚力，林煮粥啖士卒，士卒益奮。

translations.literal: On jiawu Fuqing's troops pressed the city. Tingxuan's army went out to resist; his lieutenants Bi Dingbang and Lai Gaoxiang fought with great vigor. Lin cooked porridge to feed the soldiers, and they fought all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the rebels closed on the walls. Tingxuan's men marched out; lieutenants Bi Dingbang and Lai Gaoxiang fought fiercely. Lin boiled porridge for the troops, and their spirit rose.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，賊大至，圍合，文吏竄伏，饋運犒勞，皆林會計而出納之。

translations.literal: On dingyou the bandits came in force and the encirclement closed. Clerks cowered in hiding; all provisioning, transport, and rewards passed through Lin's accounting and disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the rebels came in strength and the siege closed tight. Clerks hid in terror; Lin alone tallied and disbursed every ration, convoy, and reward.

sentences.zh: 乙亥望，大戰，解圍，輔清乃引去。

translations.literal: On the full moon of yihai a great battle was fought, the siege was lifted, and Fuqing then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai full moon a great battle broke the siege, and Fuqing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是葆楨治軍日有聲，擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: From then on Baozhen's conduct of military affairs daily won renown; he was promoted to Jiangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Baozhen's reputation as a commander grew daily, and he was promoted governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 治船政，林佐治官書，一一中條理。

translations.literal: When he managed the naval administration, Lin assisted with official documents—each one in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Directing naval affairs, he relied on Lin to handle official papers, every document in flawless order.

sentences.zh: 治家尤有節度，斷線殘紙，必儲以待用。

translations.literal: In household management she was especially disciplined: scraps of thread and torn paper were always stored away for future use.
translations.idiomatic: She ran the household with strict economy; every scrap of thread or torn paper was saved against need.

sentences.zh: 方葆楨試禮部，鬻金條脫治行，代以蜀藤，雖貴，弗易也。

translations.literal: When Baozhen went to take the metropolitan examination he sold gilt travel gear to pay his journey, replacing it with Sichuan rattan—though costly, he would not change it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen sat for the metropolitan examination he sold his gilt travel equipage to pay the journey and carried Sichuan rattan instead—pricey, yet he would not trade it for show.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Guangxu 3.

sentences.zh: 王某妻陳，皋蘭人。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of a certain Wang, was a native of Gaolan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of one Wang, was from Gaolan.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，河州回攻蘭州，師自平番來援，阻黃河不得渡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi, Hui from Hezhou attacked Lanzhou. Troops coming to relieve them from Pingfan were blocked at the Yellow River and could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 6, Hezhou Muslims besieged Lanzhou. Relief forces from Pingfan were stopped at the Yellow River and could not cross.

sentences.zh: 陳家河北，令其子化鳳集族黨，以舟濟師，蘭州以全。

translations.literal: Chen's family was north of the river; she ordered her son Huafeng to gather clan allies and ferry the army across by boat, and Lanzhou was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's family lived north of the river. She sent her son Huafeng to rally clansmen and ferry the army across by boat, saving Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 李某妻趙，營山人。

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of a certain Li, was a native of Yingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of one Li, was from Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 縣多虎，李子赴市，暮未還，李立村外待。

translations.literal: The county had many tigers. Their son Li went to market and had not returned by evening; Li stood outside the village waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers plagued the county. Their son went to market and failed to return by dusk; Li waited outside the village gate.

sentences.zh: 虎驟至，李驚呼，趙聞，持梃出，與虎鬥，虎弭尾去。

translations.literal: A tiger suddenly came; Li cried out in alarm. Zhao heard, took a staff, went out, fought the tiger, and the tiger lowered its tail and left.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger sprang upon him; Li shouted. Zhao seized a club, rushed out, fought the beast, and drove it off with tail lowered.

sentences.zh: 羅傑妻陳，安徽太平人。

translations.literal: Chen, wife of Luo Jie, was a native of Taiping in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, wife of Luo Jie, was from Taiping in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 傑與陳共入山採薪，虎攫傑，陳與爭，不得脫，急觸虎口，虎舍傑咥陳，陳死，傑得脫。

translations.literal: Jie and Chen went together into the hills to gather firewood. A tiger seized Jie; Chen struggled with it but could not free him. She thrust her hand into the tiger's mouth; the tiger released Jie and devoured Chen. Chen died; Jie escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Chen went into the hills for firewood. A tiger seized Jie; Chen grappled with the beast but could not free him. She thrust her hand into its jaws; the tiger dropped Jie and killed her instead. Jie escaped.

sentences.zh: 楊某妻唐，衡陽人。

translations.literal: Tang, wife of a certain Yang, was a native of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, wife of one Yang, was from Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 夫婦偕耘，虎攫其夫去，唐曳虎尾不捨，三踰嶺，傷左臂，卒負夫歸。

translations.literal: Husband and wife were plowing together when a tiger seized her husband and dragged him off. Tang clutched the tiger's tail and would not let go. Three times they crossed ridges; her left arm was wounded, but in the end she carried her husband home on her back.
translations.idiomatic: As they plowed together a tiger seized her husband. Tang seized its tail and would not release her grip though the beast dragged them over three ridges. Her left arm was torn, yet she carried her husband home alive.

sentences.zh: 數日夫死，以節終。

translations.literal: Several days later her husband died; she ended her life in chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband died a few days later; she remained a chaste widow to the end.

sentences.zh: 姚旺妻潘，旌德人。

translations.literal: Pan, wife of Yao Wang, was a native of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Pan, wife of Yao Wang, was from Jingde.

sentences.zh: 旺遇虎，潘奔救，同死。

translations.literal: Wang met a tiger; Pan ran to rescue him, and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang met a tiger; Pan ran to his aid, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 蓋氏，吉林涼水泉金廣年妻也。

translations.literal: The Gai clan woman was wife of Jin Guangnian of Liangshuiquan in Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Gai clan was wife to Jin Guangnian of Liangshuiquan in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 廣年貧，眇一目，有友與狎。

translations.literal: Guangnian was poor and blind in one eye; he had a friend on intimate terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnian was poor and blind in one eye and kept a close friend.

sentences.zh: 一日，戲語廣年：「汝何修得美婦？

translations.literal: One day the friend said in jest to Guangnian, "By what merit did you win such a beautiful wife?
translations.idiomatic: One day the friend teased him, "What virtue earned you such a beautiful wife?

sentences.zh: 」廣年心動，即曰：「若艷我婦，予我百金，以婦與若。

translations.literal: " Guangnian's heart stirred and he at once said, "If you desire my wife, give me a hundred taels of gold and I will give you my wife."
translations.idiomatic: Guangnian took it to heart and replied, "If you want my wife, give me a hundred taels of gold and she is yours."

sentences.zh: 」遂與友偕還語蓋，蓋曰：「貧死命也！

translations.literal: " He then went home with the friend and told Gai. Gai said, "To die poor is fate!
translations.idiomatic: He went home with his friend and told his wife. Gai said, "To die in poverty is our lot—

sentences.zh: 以貧而鬻其婦，生何心矣？

translations.literal: To sell one's wife because of poverty—what heart remains in living?
translations.idiomatic: but to sell your wife for poverty—what heart is left in living?

sentences.zh: 」噭然哭。

translations.literal: " She wailed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: She burst into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 廣年出以語友，聞哭止，入視，則自罄死矣。

translations.literal: Guangnian went out to tell his friend; when the crying stopped he went in to look and found that she had hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Guangnian went out to tell his friend. When the crying stopped he went in to look—and found she had hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 呼友共解之，友因摩其足，蓋蘇，以足抵友僕，走廚下，取刀自斫其足，立斷。

translations.literal: He called his friend to help cut her down; the friend rubbed her feet and she revived, kicked the friend's servant with her foot, ran to the kitchen, took a knife and chopped off her own foot—it severed at once.
translations.idiomatic: He called his friend to help cut her down. The friend rubbed her feet and she came to, kicked the friend's servant, ran to the kitchen, seized a knife, and chopped off her own foot—it came off at once.

sentences.zh: 昏臥血中，鄰里趨視，唾廣年。

translations.literal: She lay unconscious in the blood; neighbors rushed to see and spat on Guangnian.
translations.idiomatic: She lay unconscious in the blood. Neighbors rushed in and spat on Guangnian.

sentences.zh: 其友懼，請以百金療，廣年亦悔，力負販，育子姓甚繁。

translations.literal: His friend was afraid and offered a hundred in gold for her treatment; Guangnian also repented, labored as a porter and peddler, and raised a large family of sons and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: His friend was frightened and offered a hundred taels for her care. Guangnian repented as well, worked as a porter and peddler, and raised a large family of sons and daughters.
